chapters.title: Chapter 21 - 21: Donating to an Orphanage
chapters.content:
A crackling sphere of lightning struck the werewolf head-on, and in the next moment, the electricity leapt like wild serpents across the soaked ground.
The water Akira had released moments ago served as the perfect conductor, creating a brilliant flash of light and a symphony of screams.
"Gyaaaahhh!!"
The narrow alley echoed with pained howls as arcs of lightning coursed through the bodies of the four attackers.
The scent of burnt fabric and scorched hair filled the air, and the flickering blue of residual sparks danced over the wet cobblestones.
As the final surge of power dissipated, Akira strode over the unconscious forms, his boots splashing through shallow puddles.
He knelt beside the werewolf, whose twitching fingers still clutched at the ground.
The others were knocked out cold, but this one... this one was made of tougher stuff. Still conscious, even if barely.
Akira rifled through his belongings without hesitation.
"Fifty thousand Valis. Tsk. Not bad." He murmured, pocketing the purse.
"No wonder you've been robbing people."
Pasteur's face contorted with fear, forcing out trembling words, "P-please... spare us... sir..."
Akira froze. His golden eyes narrowed, his expression unreadable.
"Spare you?" He echoed softly, voice laced with a cold amusement.
He planned to just take their money and be done with it but when he heard them ask for mercy, his mood changed for the worse.
"Let me check something first."
His short hair gradually grew longer and his eyes turned bloodshot.
Without waiting, he reached out, and grabbed some of their blood to make a judgement.
"Tch... just as I thought. You all are inhumane"
"Your spirits are saturated with malice and the curses of those you've harmed. You've preyed on others so much that their hatred has stained your very soul."
He rose slowly, his gaze sweeping the bodies around him with growing disdain.
"Letting you go means someone else gets hurt later. That's not justice. That's negligence."
Akira's voice turned cold, devoid of sympathy.
"Choose. A long, painful death where you have time for repentance, or a clean, swift end into eternal silence."
"W-we're sorry! We'll never do it again!" one of the half-conscious men croaked weakly.
"It's not that you won't. It's that you can't." Akira raised his hand.
"I'm not a villain… but sometimes justice is cruel."
A spear of blood-red light materialized above him. It hovered, humming with energy, then shot down without hesitation.
Shunk!
The crimson spear pierced through their skulls one after another and the alley grew silent.
As their bodies twitched once, then went still, dark-blue flames—Ghost Flame—ignited above them. Their souls were cleansed, and their lingering curses burned away in the cold flames of judgement.
Blood flowed like a river across the stone, pooling beneath them. Akira's [Dark Eye] activated, absorbing the residual energy and strengthening his own body.
"You're insatiable, aren't you?" He muttered to the eye embedded in his hand.
"Always hungry for death and power."
The flames slowly faded. Akira stood there in the quiet aftermath, expression unreadable, then turned his gaze toward the end of the alley, where a quiet church stood silhouetted against the dusk.
Maria Orphanage
A peaceful haven tucked deep within the chaotic labyrinth of Daedalus Street.
Akira knocked gently at the heavy wooden doors. It was several minutes before the door creaked open, revealing a kind-faced black-haired nun.
She blinked in surprise at the boy standing at the doorstep.
"Yes? Can I help you?"
Akira gave her a soft smile and said, "I'm here to... make a donation."
The words were awkward, yet sincere. He handed her a small bag bulging with coins—today's spoils, earned through combat and survival.
"Oh!" She gasped.
"Please, come in!"
Rather than taking the money right away, the nun gently grasped his hands and led him inside the building.
Despite its age and disrepair, the orphanage had a warm atmosphere. Children ran around the hallways, laughing and playing simple games.
Akira and the nun sat down on an old, frayed sofa. Curious children peeked from behind furniture or clung protectively to her, wary of the unfamiliar guest. The nun calmed them with a gentle touch and a smile.
"I'm Maria Martel, the head caretaker here." She introduced warmly.
"And you are?"
"Akira." He replied.
Her eyes softened and she said, "Akira… why would a young adventurer like you donate such a generous amount? Valis isn't easy to earn, especially for those who risk their lives in the dungeon."
He scratched his cheek awkwardly and said, "It just felt right. My familia... they're good people. We do what we can."
A flicker of admiration passed through Maria's eyes. She finally accepted the pouch of money with both hands, as if it were a sacred offering.
"Some of our children went on to become adventurers too. They used to visit... bring back food, toys, books. But time passes, and eventually... they stop coming." Her voice trailed into silence, heavy with memory.
Then she straightened and smiled again. "Thank you, Akira. I can't offer anything in return but prayers."
She took his hands again. Her hands were rough from labor yet warm and full of gratitude.
"May the gods bless you, and may your path be safe."
The gesture triggered a bittersweet warmth in Akira's chest. The feeling reminded him of... home. Of something long lost.
He stood abruptly, cheeks faintly flushed. "I should go. My familia might be waiting for dinner."
Maria nodded with a smile and said, "Of course. I was going to invite you to eat here... but another time, perhaps?"Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
"Definitely."
Akira said with a grin, "I'll visit again when I can. See you, Maria-san."
She walked him to the door and waved. "Be careful out there, Akira."
— — —
Back at the Stardust Garden, the sun had dipped beyond the rooftops, casting a golden hue over the garden.
"Akira's still not back?" Maryuu looked toward the entrance with slight concern.
Lyra said with a smirk, "Shall we eat first and let him have cold leftovers as punishment?"
"Raise your hands if you agree!" Noin declared with a grin.
Three hands shot up immediately.
"Ha! Even Astraea-sama raised hers! That settles it!" Lyra laughed.
Astraea smiled softly, eyes closed. "It's only the three of you who find this amusing."
"Useless elf, go check the door!" Kaguya shouted playfully.
"Why don't you go yourself?" Ryuu replied, brow twitching.
But with a sigh, she stood and made her way to the entrance. Just as she approached, the door swung open.
"I'm back," Akira said, stepping inside—
Bonk!
"Guh—!"
Ryuu collapsed backward, having taken the full brunt of the opening door to the forehead.
"Ryuu?!" Akira panicked, crouching beside her.
He used a bit of ice elemental magic and gently pressed a cool hand to her temple.
"Sorry, sorry! Are you alright?!"
Ryuu's face turned red as she said, "I-I'm fine. But could you please... move your hand now?"
Alise burst out laughing and said, "Ryuu! Why does this always happen to you?!"
"Dinner's ready!" Maryuu called, setting dishes on the table.
"Wash up, everyone!"

chapters.title: Chapter 22 - 22: Blood Magic
chapters.content:
Yhe scalding water cascaded down, enveloping Akira in thick steam. He stood dazed beneath the shower, lost in thought.
Was it really just about killing them?
But what else could he have done? Even if they were arrested, they'd be out in no time. He had no proof they were murderers. And once free, they'd hurt more innocent people.
After a long moment, Akira stepped out and stripped off his soaked clothes. He tossed them into a bucket, then crouched beside it.
With a soft breath, he released a layer of frost that sealed over the surface, then gently blew into the bucket, mimicking the spin of a washing machine.
"There's no point thinking about this anymore. I should just report to Astraea-sama and get my status updated."
With that, he stood, feeling lighter, and made his way to her room. He knocked on the wooden door casually.
"Akira? Come in," came the warm voice from within.
Akira stepped inside, the soft light in the room washing over him. Inside were the four core members of the Alise group, each carrying different expressions—curiosity, concern, calm.
"We were waiting for you."
Alise said, "Time to check your stats. And while we're at it, we have some questions about what happened today."
"Understood."
Akira walked to Astraea's side and sat before her, quietly pulling down the back of his shirt.
Astraea pricked her fingertip, and divine blood shimmered as she traced sacred runes across his back.
The blood glowed, dancing with light. Moments later, invisible energy surged as his experience was transformed into raw strength.
Akira
LV 1
Strength: H171 → G274
Endurance: H156 → G256
Agility: G232 → F322
Dexterity: G201 → G295
Magic: F378 → D541
[Magic]
Elemental Control
– Can control all elements
– Increase the power of elements by consuming magic power.
– Ice Focus: Sacrifices other elements to exclusively enhance ice-based abilities
– Wind Focus: Sacrifices other elements to exclusively enhance wind-based abilities
Blood Magic
– Under a certain state, grants the power to manipulate and absorb blood to strengthen the body and control enemies
– Enables deep insight into a person's condition through their blood
.....
Astraea stared in awe, her fingers pausing for a second as she watched the magic entries change.
"The original magic has evolved—and there's a new one too. Akira, you really never stop surprising us."
She copied the divine text onto parchment. Akira picked it up and scanned the page, his eyes narrowing slightly.
Just as expected. The class advancement had triggered changes in his Elemental Control and now his Blood Mage traits had fully awakened.
The other girls leaned over to look.
"The stats are still increasing like crazy, but... not as explosively as last time." Alise muttered.
"Maybe Akira's growth is finally stabilizing." Lyra remarked, half-relieved.
"If he keeps growing like this, I'll have to hit the dungeon more seriously or I'll fall behind."
"Is something unusual about Akira's magic, Astraea-sama?" Ryuu asked, eyes fixed on the parchment.
A heavy silence followed.
Astraea glanced toward Akira and then the others. "You all know why we came here tonight, don't you?"
The four girls exchanged glances. Ryuu nodded and spoke first, "Akira… did you kill someone today?"
Akira blinked and said, "Ah. Four people tried to mug me. I defeated them, but—"
His voice grew quiet.
"I sensed something... terrible in their blood. Even if they were locked up, they'd be released soon. I couldn't risk them hurting anyone else."
"I see." Astraea reached out and gently stroked his head.
"What do you all think?"
"Haha! Serious topic, huh?" Alise chuckled, brushing her hair back.
"But honestly? I think Akira made the right call. When we go after an evil familia, we don't always have the luxury of showing mercy."
"Exactly." Lyra nodded.
"If it were me, I wouldn't have let them go either."
"Oh my, I'm with Akira on this too." Kaguya chimed in with a small smile. Her tone was light, but her past as a noble and assassin gave her words weight.
"But…" Ryuu hesitated, her voice tinged with worry.
"Even if it was justified, isn't it too soon for you to be exposed to this, Akira?"
Akira's lips twitched as he said, "You're only a year older than me, Ryuu. I know you're worried, but don't look down on me."
The others chuckled while Ryuu pouted in silent protest.
Astraea stepped in with a soft voice, "Everyone's just concerned, Akira. You've always seemed like such a sweet boy… seeing you covered in blood, it scared us."
She held his hand gently and said, "I'm not saying what you did was wrong. But listen, justice can vary from person to person. Just... don't lose yourself in killing. Don't let that become your purpose. Promise me."
Akira nodded solemnly and said, "I understand, Astraea-sama."
"Good." Astraea smiled.
"Now, let's move on. About your new magic... I'm guessing you already know the trigger conditions, right?"
As expected of a goddess—she had probably figured it out already.
Ryuu leaned forward and asked, "What does 'a certain state' mean? Is it like Alise's skill that activates in battle?"Google seaʀᴄh NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
"Want me to show you?" Akira grinned.
"Eh!? That easy?" Alise puffed her cheeks.
"That's so unfair! Mine only triggers mid-battle!"
"Wow… blood magic that gets stronger through absorption. No wonder Astraea-sama warned him about killing." Lyra said dramatically, though she looked more curious than afraid.
Kaguya tilted her head and asked, "What kind of blood strengthens it? Monsters? Humans? Even gods?"

chapters.title: Chapter 23 - 23: Akira, a Mascot
chapters.content:
Astraea raised a hand, gently stopping the two from approaching further. Her serene gaze shifted to Akira, eyes soft yet firm.
"You still have something else to show us, don't you?"
Akira gave a small nod, wordlessly shifting into his [Swift Master] state.
A soft breeze curled around him, dancing through the air like an invisible spirit. His hair faded back to its original hue, and his expression sharpened. Confidence radiated from his eyes, and a smug, playful smile tugged at the corners of his lips.
The transformation was astonishing—like watching a different person emerge from thin air.
"Hahaha, how about it? Handsome, right?" Akira said cheekily, striking the familiar narcissistic pose that Alise often made.
Lyra burst into laughter, nearly falling over. "Pfft—Alise, Akira in this form would totally vibe with you!"
The others chuckled as well. Alise could only shrug helplessly, palms up, caught between pride and exasperation.
Realizing how cringe his current state might be, Akira coughed awkwardly and promptly shifted again.
This time, long, flowing hair cascaded over his shoulders like a river. Proud scarlet eyes gleamed with cool authority, and his figure stood just a little taller than Alise's. Even in casual clothes, an air of elegance and unapproachable nobility clung to him like a second skin.
Akira sank lazily into a chair, arms draped across the armrests, and said with nonchalance, "This is the form required to activate [Blood Magic]—the one you were all so worried about."
"Relax. I haven't turned into a bloodthirsty monster. I don't crave blood or anything like that. It's just… my personality gets slightly altered. If I become stronger, that side effect should vanish."
"That's good to hear." Kaguya replied softly. "As long as you feel it's under control."
But Akira could sense their doubt. Even now, their eyes betrayed hesitation, their stiffened postures a silent admission of unease.
He sighed quietly. Without warning, Akira stood up and walked over to Alise.
"Eh? Akira, what's wrong?" Alise blinked in surprise, a hint of nervousness slipping into her voice.
Akira reached out and gave her a gentle hug. Then, without missing a beat, he did the same with Kaguya, Lyra, and Ryuu—one after another, brief but sincere.
Finally, he strolled over to where Astraea sat on the sofa, and, with a casual plop, laid down across her lap like a child seeking comfort.
"Don't worry. It won't end the way you're afraid of. This is my power. I can control it."
The four girls looked at each other, then to Astraea.
Astraea smiled, a look of warm contentment on her face.
"See? I told you I wasn't lying."
Only then did the lingering tension finally melt from their shoulders.
"Say, how long can you maintain these forms?" Kaguya asked curiously.
"I can stay in them indefinitely—until I feel like switching again." Akira replied with ease.
"Can we let the others know?"
"Of course."
Alise instantly lit up and pulled Akira to her. "Then let's show everyone! That way, they'll know what to expect if you suddenly transform again."
Lyra clapped her hands and said, "Since everyone's accepted Akira already, why not make it fun? Let's throw a pajama party in the lobby!"
"Brilliant!" Alise grinned.
"Ryuu, go round up the girls!"
"On it!" Ryuu nodded and dashed off toward the dormitory with surprising speed.
Kaguya turned to Astraea amd asked, "Astraea-sama, you'll come too, right?"
Astraea replied, "Of course. I wouldn't miss this wonderful moment with all of you."
— — —
The morning sun filtered gently through the curtains.
Akira lay sprawled across his bed, eyes half-lidded, staring blankly at the door. He had zero intention of venturing into the dungeon today.
No reason to rush, not after last night.
Regret settled heavily in his stomach like a stone.
Why… why did he agree to let the other members know about his transformations?
Last night, a group of normally quiet and reserved girls had gathered around him with frightening enthusiasm.
Touching. Stroking. Poking. Experimenting.
He thought he was a wolf among a horde of sheep. But it turns out he was the sheep that wandered into a den of wolves.
They had him acting out ridiculous scenarios in all his forms, pulling him into every sort of compromising situation their imaginations could conjure.
He'd switched back to his original form, thinking it would calm them down. But contrary to his expectations, it only made things worse.
What the hell was that madness?
They asked the Glacial Master, "Hey Akira, can I use you as my pillow when it's hot? You look chilly."
They looked at the Blood Mage, wide-eyed with glee, and added, "C'mon, Little Akira, give us a proud glare and say something tsundere! Try it!"
Even with the influence of his transformations, Akira's original personality was on the verge of breaking down. It felt like he had become everyone's toy—lower in status than even Ryuu.
Have I really become the mascot of the Familia?
Akira groaned into his pillow. "I was toyed with all night… I can already feel the trouble piling up."
Still, he consoled himself, 'At least I'm building good relationships… right?'
Dragging himself out of bed, Akira washed up and opened the door, heading toward the kitchen, hoping for a moment of normalcy—perhaps even something warm to eat.
As he entered, his eyes saw Astraea, Kaguya, and Maryuu. They were busy preparing breakfast, though Maryuu looked like she was on the verge of breaking something with every move.
"Morning." Akira said, trying to sound casual, pretending last night had never happened.
Kaguya, without turning around, snickered, "Oh? Isn't this our second mascot? You're up early. Going adventuring?"
Akira sighed, already feeling a headache, "Nope. I figured I've been too unlucky lately, so I'm taking a break. Instead of risking it in the dungeon, I'll patrol the city with everyone."
Kaguya glanced over and nodded. "That makes sense. With your current strength, you've got nothing to fear from average Level 3s. It's good for you to experience Orario outside the dungeon too."
Astraea, taking a dish from Kaguya, added, "Kaguya, take Akira to the clothing store later. He needs more casual wear. Also, help him pick out a custom outfit."
Akira stared blankly amd asked, "Eh? Astraea-sama, why is there a need for that? Can I… go alone?"
Astraea firmly said, "Denied."
"Nope." Kaguya echoed flatly.
Akira sighed, 'I really have become a dress-up doll now…'
"I wanna come too! I wanna shop with Akira!" Maryuu's eyes sparkled with envy.
"You just want to watch me suffer, don't you?'
Suddenly, two hands covered Akira's eyes from behind, and a mischievous voice rang out. "Guess who~?"
Akira didn't even flinch and said, "It's Alise, isn't it?"
"Ehhh?! How'd you guess it so fast?! I haven't even done this with you before!" Alise's shocked voice came from behind him.
"Only you would pull this stunt. You've got this passionate energy—it's obvious the moment you touch someone." Akira replied dryly.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.content:
"Wow, what does that energy even feel like? Why don't I know I have it?" Alise blinked, tilting her head in confusion.

"That's too much! I'm just warm! Look!" Alise puffed her cheeks in protest and placed her palm on the back of Akira's neck with a triumphant grin.

— — —

As they strolled through the bustling streets, Akira stopped in front of a small food stall, his eyes lighting up.

"We want two sauce and one red bean cream!" The girls said.

"Mmm! This one's really good too. I'm getting this flavor next time!"

In return, Alise beamed innocently, flashing a dazzling smile towards him.

Alise snickered and covered her mouth while Kaguya's eyes widened.

"It's obvious we all ordered the same thing."
"Aww, so cold."
After a short pause, Ryuu looked away, her ears tinged pink. "Don't bite too much. Just swap a little."

"A clothing store."
When the door swung open, rows of clothes in every style imaginable greeted them.
"Welcome, esteemed guests. Please browse at your leisure."

chapters.title: Chapter 25 - 25: Since When Was Evilus So Weak?
chapters.content:
"Akira, this is my good friend, Adi. You've met her before, remember? She's the one you ran into last time." Ryuu introduced with a gentle smile.
"And Adi, this is Akira, the newest member of our Familia."
This time, Akira took the initiative. He stepped forward and extended his hand politely.
He sincerely said, "Hello, Adi-san. I'm really sorry for the trouble I caused last time… and for running off without saying anything."
Adi reached out and shook his hand briefly, their palms just brushing before she pulled back. Her eyes swept over Akira, observing him with mild curiosity.Nᴇw ɴovel chaptᴇrs are published on ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
"You're still Level 1, right? But you've already awakened… magic or a skill, perhaps?"
"Eh? How did Adi know that Akira had magic or skills—ah!"
Ryuu suddenly realized her slip, belatedly covering her mouth as she turned to Akira with an apologetic look.
"Ryuu." Kaguya sighed helplessly.
"Adi is quite sharp. Judging from what happened that day, it was clearly the result of some powerful magic or skill. And… Akira and I looked so wrecked afterward that it was kind of obvious who was responsible."
"Hehe, you give me too much credit." Adi smiled playfully, clasping her hands together in a mock pleading gesture.
"So? Will you satisfy my curiosity? I promise I won't tell a soul."
Before Akira could answer, Alise chimed in, placing a hand on her hip. "It's magic."
"So it was magic!" Adi's eyes lit up with amazement.
"Wow… having such powerful magic at Level 1. I'm seriously jealous."
— — —
Adi didn't leave after having her curiosity satisfied. Instead, she stuck around, casually chatting with Ryuu about Familia matters while throwing an occasional question at Akira.
Suddenly, a commotion rose from the distance.
A Ganesha Familia soldier wearing a hieroglyphic mask came running toward them, panting heavily.
"Adi-sama! There are members of Evilus attacking civilians up ahead—we need your support!" He gasped, pointing toward the direction of the chaos.
"Looks like trouble found us." Alise muttered, her expression sharpening as she glanced at the others.
"Adi, let's move out."
"Right!" Adi answered without hesitation.
The group dashed toward the scene.
"Hahaha! You can't escape! Come to hell with me and pay for your sins!"
A dozen figures cloaked in tattered robes, clearly from Evilus, were rampaging through the streets. Their weapons swung wildly, cutting down anyone who couldn't fight back.
"Ahhh! Somebody help us! Please! Let me go!" Panicked screams echoed from all sides.
Without hesitation, the five charged into the fray. They scattered into different directions, drawing their weapons and diving into the rescue.
Alise spotted a cloaked criminal raising his blade against a terrified mother and child. Without hesitation, she invoked her magic.
"Arga, Arvana, Arvelia!"
Fire wrapped around her limbs like living snakes. With blazing speed, she shot forward, her rapier slashing the enemy's sword aside. She thrust the blade through the man's limbs, immobilizing him, then finished with a brutal kick to the stomach.
The criminal dropped to his knees, retching. Before he could recover, Alise stepped in again and stomped on his head with her heel, knocking him out cold.
"Yoshi! One down! Let's go, I'll get you out of here safely!"
She declared to the mother and daughter, then began leading them to safety. Any enemy in her path fell easily to her flaming sword.
Elsewhere, Akira's legs moved like a storm, kicking up a whirlwind as he clashed with two of Evilus' fighters.
He wielded a battered one-handed sword, aiming it squarely at an opponent's arm joint and smashing it cleanly. The man's weapon dropped.
In the same moment, Akira's magic surged, forming a cannon-like blast that hurled another man backward before he could even react.
The first attacker, despite losing his weapon, lunged forward with a barehanded punch.
Akira leaned back, dodging with minimal movement, then conjured a chunk of ice around his sword—morphing it into a gleaming hammer and smashed it into the man's face.
The second enemy charged with a roar, swinging a dagger at Akira's side.
"You dare get in our way?! You'll regret it in hell!"
Akira responded with a swift kick to his neck, then followed up by slamming the ice hammer into the man's skull. Both foes collapsed.
Without wasting a moment, Akira dragged them by the ankles, stacked them together, and froze their legs solid. Whether they got frostbite or not was none of his concern.
The battle raged on, but the tide quickly turned.
After the fighting died down, more than a dozen Ganesha Familia members arrived, taking control of the situation. The criminals were bound and loaded into carriages while the wounded were carried away for treatment.
Alise and the others regrouped.
With one hand on her waist and a half-serious smile on her face, Alise sighed.
"Phew. Another crisis handled. Some people were injured, but considering the situation, I'd say we got lucky."
Adi nodded. "Yeah. It could've been far worse. Still… I'm glad it wasn't."
Ryuu pulled down her mask, her face filled with solemn regret. "We didn't make it in time for everyone… some were still hurt."
"But."
She added softly, "It's a blessing that it wasn't worse."
Alise reached over and patted Ryuu on the back with a warm smile. "Don't beat yourself up, Ryuu. Not everything can be solved perfectly."
"She's right."
Adi added gently, "We're not gods. We can only do our best to protect those right in front of us. That's enough."
Akira walked up to Kaguya, who stood silently in thought. "What's wrong, Kaguya-nee? Something bothering you?"
Kaguya furrowed her brows and said, "Don't you think these people were… too weak? All of them were Level 1s. Not a single Level 2. What kind of fools launch an attack like this?"
Akira nodded, recalling how easily his spells dispatched them.
He said, "Could be brainwashing. They kept shouting about atonement. Or maybe… they were just disposable pawns."
He paused, his eyes narrowing. "Classic misdirection. Send out the cannon fodder to create chaos while something bigger happens elsewhere."
"That makes sense."
Kaguya murmured, "I'll report this to Astraea-sama when we return."
They waited a while longer, making sure no new incidents occurred, then resumed their patrol elsewhere.
Eventually, night began to fall. Their shift had ended, and the larger Ganesha Familia took over the watch. Adi prepared to take her leave.
"Well then, I'll say goodbye here. I'm heading off now—see you around!" With a wave, Adi turned and disappeared into the crowd.
"Bye-bye!" Ryuu waved politely.
"Alright! Let's head home too! Ooooh!" Alise stretched her arms high and struck a triumphant pose.
"Ahh, the diligent and dazzling me has once again solved a crisis with grace!"
Kaguya and Ryuu exchanged a look and sighed, clearly used to Alise's antics. They turned toward the Stardust Garden, silently continuing on.
Akira, meanwhile, grabbed Alise's hand and followed with a smile. "Yes, yes, our beautiful captain. Time to go back now."
On the way home, they stopped by the clothing store to pick up Akira's new outfits. Then, they returned together to their base—Stardust Garden.

chapters.title: Chapter 26 - 26: Light Banter
chapters.content:
At the entrance of the base, Alise and her group encountered Lyra and the others who had already returned earlier.
With an unmistakable smirk tugging at the corners of her lips, Lyra shot a teasing glance at the approaching group.
Her eyes zeroed in on Akira before she quipped playfully, "Oh my, are you guys done with your group date already? Akira, how does it feel to date three gorgeous women at the same time? Most guys would kill for that."
Akira responded without missing a beat. He gave her a bold thumbs-up, his mouth splitting into a wide, toothy grin as he laughed heartily.
"It was an absolutely riveting experience! And now, beautiful Lyra-san, you must accompany me on the next date. I insist. Hahaha!"
Lyra blinked. She hadn't expected that kind of shameless counterattack.
She stood frozen for a split second, then quickly said, "Wow, seriously? So having those three lovely ladies isn't enough, and now you're planning to drag me into your harem too? Wait a second—don't tell me... Akira, you're that kind of guy? A closet lolicon?!"Google seaʀᴄh NovᴇlFirenᴇt
"Ohhh, so that's what this is about." Akira said, feigning heartbreak as he dramatically wiped fake tears from his eyes.
"I thought tou were just jealous because you weren't invited. I was even planning to devote an entire day just to you! But I see now... you think so little of me. My heart is shattered!"
"Ahahaha! Okay, okay, I'm officially stunned and speechless." Lyra said, shaking her head with mock defeat.
"I give up. Where did this come from? Just a few days ago, you were like an innocent little kitten, and now suddenly you're this... this... shameless flirt. My poor brain can't keep up!"
"Maybe you should stop saying weird things then. He probably picked it up from you, you damn rascal." Kaguya reached out and bonked Lyra lightly on the head.
She then turned to the suddenly composed Akira and scolded, "And you! Stop saying weird things and making those exaggerated faces."
"Roger that." Akira raised his hand in mock salute, his face returning to its usual serious look.
With a cheeky smile, he shot a "yeah!" gesture at Lyra, clearly unrepentant.
Alise couldn't help but laugh, turning to Ryuu with bright eyes.
She happily said, "Looks like Akira has really accepted us. If it were before, he wouldn't have joked like that."
Ryuu smiled softly, nodding in agreement. "Yes, I'm glad. It feels like he's truly become part of our family."
After dinner, the Astraea Familia gathered in the main hall. The air was a bit heavier as they discussed the day's incident.
"Astraea-sama, regarding today's confrontation... this is what we encountered." Kaguya stepped forward, her voice steady as she summarized their battle and speculated about the Evilus attack.
The gentle but stern goddess listened intently, eyes narrowed in thought.
She said, "It's certainly plausible. Loki mentioned something similar—those secret factions have been moving in the shadows. We've been trying to track them down, but their actions are elusive."
"Everyone, please be cautious during the upcoming patrols. Remain vigilant and don't lower your guard." Astraea firmly said.
"Yes, Astraea-sama!" Everyone responded in unison, their tone resolute.
"Whoa, Alise, so you guys ran into those scumbags too?" Someone asked.
"Yeah." Alise replied, crossing her arms.
"It really seems like these small skirmishes are just distractions for something else."
"Tch, when will this nonsense end?" Lyra groaned, collapsing dramatically onto the sofa.
"I'm tired of patrolling every damn day. The secret faction can go rot."
Maryuu chuckled softly and comforted her, "Thanks for your hard work. But someone has to do it. If nobody steps up, Orario will just fall deeper into chaos."
"It's alright." Alise said with a firm smile.
"Today, no one died, and we dealt a blow to Evilus' forces. They're not invincible. As long as we spread the wings of justice, we will bring peace to Orario."
"I truly believe that if we keep walking forward with determination, our efforts will lay the foundation for defeating the Evilus completely!"
Then she raised her fist, her voice rising with fervor, "And after that, we're taking down the One-Eyed Black Dragon! Let's go, everyone! We've got this!"
The room fell into stunned silence.
Then Akira clapped enthusiastically and declared, "Captain is awesome! Captain is the best! Captain is the strongest!"
Everyone turned their heads to stare at Akira, stunned.
Meanwhile, Alise beamed at the praise, looking absolutely delighted.
Kaguya sighed, massaging her temples. "Captain, it's nice to dream about the future... but we should focus on the task at hand too."
"What are you saying, Kaguya?" Alise pouted.
"I am focusing! We're already fighting Evilus, aren't we? So taking down the One-Eyed Black Dragon is just the next step. Why not go big if we're going for it?"
Kaguya gave her a long, helpless smile and said, "I really can't win with you. Maybe it's your ridiculous optimism that makes people follow you."
"Seriously." Noin muttered, shooting Alise a tired look. "She always thinks things will work out somehow."
Maryuu giggled softly and said, "But that's why we all follow her, right? Because she is that kind of person."
Meanwhile, in the desolate ruins of Orario's 7th District, three shadows gathered in a crumbling base of Evilus.
Olivas Act slammed his fist on the old table, his face twisted in rage.
He shouted, "Who the hell leaked our location?! The base was almost exposed! Luckily, we threw out some pawns to bait those self-righteous fools."
"Who knows? It's not like we got caught." Valetta Grede snapped, flipping her pink hair in irritation.
"You made me come all the way here for this petty problem? You should've handled it yourself. Are you that useless?"
Vito let out a soft laugh, utterly unfazed. "Relax. We still have our core intact. The bait did its job. But... perhaps it's time to lie low. If they catch us again, we won't be so lucky."
"I have no interest in getting punished by Erebus." Valetta growled.
"He's still out searching for allies, and if we get discovered again, it's over."
Olivas clenched his fists under the table, his expression dark. 'If I had the strength, I'd kill the both of you right now.'
But all he could manage was a snarl. "Tch, don't act like you're any better. You've slaughtered your share of adventurers. Maybe you're the one who got us exposed."
Valetta pointed a sharp finger at him and snapped, "If I hadn't stepped in, this dump would've been gone already. I've got plans to execute, unlike you! Mess with me again, and I'll cut you up."
She stormed out, slamming the door behind her. "Disband!"
Vito shrugged and casually followed her out, leaving Olivas alone in the shadowed room, his fury barely contained.
"Enjoy your little victory, righteous scum. But soon... I'll crush your dreams."
— — —
"Rrraaargh!"
An orc roared, its massive frame charging forward like a raging boulder. Its meaty green arms swung like tree trunks, trying to crush everything in its path.
Akira's eyes narrowed. He bent his knees and ducked low, narrowly avoiding the sweeping strike.
With perfect timing, he sprang up and drove his one-handed sword into the orc's armpit.
Slash!
The sound of tearing flesh echoed as green blood sprayed from the deep wound. The severed arm flopped to the ground, and the orc howled in agony.
Without giving the beast a chance to recover, Akira leaped into the air, his body twisting mid-flight.
With a howl of wind, he brought down his sword in a fierce arc, cleaving straight through the orc's thick neck.
Thud!
The massive monster's head hit the ground first, and its body followed with a thunderous crash, kicking up clouds of dust.
Akira landed lightly, standing atop the fallen beast, his blade dripping with green blood.
Another enemy, another battle... and another victory.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 27 - 27: Stats or Technique?
chapters.content:
Akira had been grinding on the tenth floor of the Dungeon for quite a while now. In that time, he had grown confident enough to handle groups of up to four orcs with nothing but a one-handed sword.
As long as a massive wave of monsters didn't show up, he could now explore this floor with relative ease.
Having finally made up his mind to pursue the path of a magic swordsman, Akira requested both Kaguya and Ryuu to coach him in swordsmanship.
His mage identity remained his hidden ace—something he would unleash only when enemies lowered their guard, unaware of the storm he could bring.
His training plan was simple but disciplined: sharpen his swordsmanship during dungeon raids, then return to the surface to refine his magic in the evenings. With this dual-pronged approach, he was steadily evolving.
That evening, inside Astraea's room.
Akira
LV 1
Strength: G274 → E442
Endurance: G256 → E467
Dexterity: F322 → D502
Agility: G295 → E492
Magic: D541 → B721
He had now been training on the tenth floor for five days straight.
Yet, despite his continuous fighting, the pace at which his stats improved had significantly slowed down—except for Magic, which continued to soar upward at an impressive rate.
Apparently, the monsters on the tenth floor no longer provided him with meaningful growth. If he wanted to increase his growth rate, he would have to challenge the next floor.
Astraea studied his status sheet thoughtfully and said, "You've been pushing yourself lately, Akira. Is something driving you?"
"I just have this gut feeling." Akira replied, taking the parchment back with a steady gaze.
"Something big is coming. And when it does, I want to be strong enough to protect my goddess… and everyone in this family."
"Is that so?" Astraea smiled gently. "Then go on—train well with Kaguya."
"Thank you. I will!"
Out at the training grounds, wooden swords clashed.
Akira's blade met Kaguya's with a dull thud. As the force of the blow bounced their swords apart, Kaguya moved like a shadow, her blade striking toward him with sharp precision.
Akira instinctively stepped back, narrowly avoiding her swing, and retaliated with a swift downward slash.
Clack!
Kaguya parried with ease. Leaning in, she swung her sword in an arc, the blade slicing toward his neck like a flash of lightning.
"!"
Akira quickly reversed his grip and raised his sword vertically to block the incoming strike. The blades collided and he barely held on.
But just as he exhaled a breath of relief—
Smack!
A blow landed on his wrist.
Before he could recover, Kaguya's foot snuck in behind his heel, sweeping him off balance.
He stumbled, and the next instant, found himself flat on the ground, a wooden blade hovering in front of his chest.
"You're down." Kaguya declared, squatting beside him.
She ruffled his hair with a faint smile and said, "You lose."
Akira groaned in mock agony. "Ugh… Kaguya-nee, you're amazing."
"Flattery won't earn you mercy." She said bluntly.
"You asked us to teach you, didn't you? Then be ready to suffer. Got it?"
"Crystal clear." Akira nodded.
Kaguya proceeded to point out several flaws in his footwork and blade angles, demonstrating smoother techniques.
"You've heard this before, right?" She said, pausing.
"That combat skills don't matter in the Dungeon if your stats are high enough?"
She gave him a look and said, "Let me tell you now—only fools believe that."
She continued, "Yes, stats are crucial. But don't underestimate technique. Our enemies aren't just monsters. One day, you might face humans, werewolfs, beings far more cunning than Dungeon monsters. When that time comes, your skill might be the only thing standing between victory and death."
Raw strength could indeed overcome technique. Raise your stats, become faster and stronger. Then, one day, you might crush a monster that once made you flee.
But not every foe waits for you to level up. Some enemies will kill you before you get that chance.
That's when you'll realize—strength isn't everything. Skill gives you options. It's the difference between life and death when your power alone isn't enough.
"Take the dwarves." Kaguya said, standing tall.
"They've got an innate disadvantage in agility, but they train relentlessly. They learn every trick, every nuance, until their swordplay becomes perfect. That's how they survive."
She held out her hand and pulled Akira up from the ground.
"You're thinking about heading to the eleventh floor next, right?" She asked, narrowing her eyes.
"Are you sure you're ready for that kind of danger?"
"No problem at all!" Akira puffed out his chest with pride. "I'm a special mage, after all."
— — —

Age: 13
Level: 23
Status: Good
Class: Mage (Male)
Affiliation: Astraea Familia
Achievements: NoneFollow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt

Survive "Return of the Gods" and "Seven Days of Death" and fight Against: Evilus

Upon reaching Level 20, Akira's arsenal had expanded greatly. Included in the Level 20 gift box were 5 large HP potions and 5 large MP potions, all of which he promptly donated to the Astraea Familia for emergency use.
When he revealed these unusual potions, no one in the Familia questioned where they came from. Their silent trust made Akira feel warm inside.
Later, Akira sought out Celty, an elf with exceptional magical talent. He handed her a staff with a curious gleam in his eyes.
"Celty, can you try this staff? I want to see if it enhances your magic."
Celty took the staff, walked to the training field, and cast a fireball into the air.
Whoosh!
The spell flew faster and struck harder than usual, exploding with a loud boom that lit up the dusk sky.
"It works! The casting speed is faster, and the power's clearly increased." Celty exclaimed, eyes sparkling.
"Where did this staff come from, Akira?"
Akira shrugged with a grin. "It's from the system, so don't worry about that. Is it useful to you?"
"Very much so! But… this must be rare. If you give it to me, what will you use?" Celty asked, visibly concerned.
"It's fine." Akira assured her. "I already have a new staff lined up. Since this one suits you, I want you to have it."
Celty looked at him for a moment, then gripped the staff tightly.
She softly said, "Then I'll accept it. I promise to use it well. Thank you, Akira."

chapters.title: Chapter 28 - 28: What is the Limit?
chapters.content:
The eleventh floor of the dungeon bore a structure eerily reminiscent of the previous level.
It was shrouded in thick, heavy fog that dulled senses, stretching out into an endless expanse of overgrown grasslands riddled with traps, ancient mechanisms, and weapons scattered like the remnants of a forgotten battlefield.
Descending the stone staircase built precariously on the edge of a cliff, Akira finally stepped foot onto this floor.
As soon as he arrived here, he was immediately greeted by his first opponent.
A Hard Armored.
This beast was a terrifying fusion of brute endurance and deceptive vulnerability. Though its shell was hard as iron, its exposed underbelly was its fatal flaw.
Standing on two legs, it easily reached a height of over 1.5 meters—nearly matching Akira himself.
It was widely known as the upper floors' tankiest monster—one that most LV 1 adventurers wouldn't dare face head-on.
Before Akira could fully process its appearance, a new danger surged from the fog—imps. There were ozens of them, their eyes glinting red.
The Hard Armored curled into a ball and lunged forward with terrifying speed, aiming to crush him.
Seeing this, Akira's eyes narrowed. He quickly dodged to the side, fluidly changing his stance, and with a swift backhand slash, three imps fell in a single stroke.
At this moment, the Hard Armored came again.
Now!
His feet dug into the ground, his body shifted, and the sword in his hand thrust forward. His blade struck right into the exposed belly.
The monster screeched in pain.
Without missing a beat, Akira launched himself upward, flipping in midair just in time to dodge another wave of imp claws.
He landed with a light thud, then dashed into the pack of monsters fearlessly.
Steel flashed. Shadows danced. Screams echoed.
Within moments, more than a dozen imps had collapsed, their bodies dissolving into ash.
The fog pulsed again.
This time, five orcs emerged from the grasslands, each nearly three meters tall, their muscular bodies radiating primal rage. For a moment, even Akira felt a twinge of awe.
Then he leapt, landing cleanly atop one of the orc's heads. He plunged his sword downward, then leapt back before the others could react.
Before the remaining four could recover, Akira unleashed a spinning slash that swept through them, slicing their tendons and knees.
Then, he stepped back just as their massive bodies toppled down to the ground.
But there was no time to rest.
He crouched over the largest of the fallen orcs, dug out the largest visible magic stone, and shoved it into his [Backpack].
He didn't have the luxury of harvesting them all—there were too many enemies, and time was short.
That's when it came.ᴛhis ᴜpdated by ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
A deafening roar ripped through the fog.
"ROAR—!!"
From the shifting veil of mist emerged a towering beast—a Silverback.
Covered in thick white fur and plated with armor, its back shimmered with strands of dark silver hair. Its arms bulged with monstrous strength.
The ground trembled with each step it took as it ran on all fours, barreling toward him like a living avalanche.
Akira didn't run, instead charging forward.
The distance between them closed in an instant.
The silverback swung its massive fist towards Akira. In response, Akira ducked low, barely evading it. Then, he stepped forward into the Silverback's unguarded zone.
He slashed—clean, brutal, efficient—at the ape's elbow joint.
Splurt—!
Blood sprayed.
The silverback howled, shaking the very earth. In its madness, it ripped off its severed arm and hurled it at Akira, then lunged with the other.
Akira jumped, but the timing was off.
A huge fist collided with his raised blade.
BOOM!
The impact launched him sideways. He tumbled violently across the grass, coughing out breath after breath before finally regaining balance.
His sword was cracked.
Without hesitation, he flung it away and pulled another one from his [Backpack].
The silverback roared and came again. But Akira was ready.
He darted around it's side, striking its exposed arm with a feint, making it lose balance and topple. Then, he effortlessly landed on its back.
His expression turned cold, the blade gleaming with killing intent.
Shhkt—!
The sword pierced the Silverback's skull with surgical precision.
The ape let out a final spasm before collapsing, lifeless.
Akira landed beside it, panting softly, the blood-drenched blade still humming with energy.
"Now that was a thrill." He muttered with a grin.
His magic power, which had been roaring to life during the battle, slowly simmered down.
Had the fight gone on any longer, his instincts might have overwhelmed him—he would've unleashed devastating magic without meaning to.
He flipped the Silverback over, removed its armor, and carved out a magic stone the size of his palm.
A moment later, the body disintegrated into ash, returning to the dungeon's cycle of rebirth.
After a brief rest, Akira continued exploring—but this time, whenever he spotted other adventurer teams, he made a point to change direction, ensuring he was alone when hunting monsters.
On this floor, aside from the silverback and the occasional Infant dragons measuring three meters tall, there were no threats that could challenge him even when he just used his one-handed sword.
Seeing that there were only imps and orcs nearby, he sheathed his blade altogether, deciding to use his fists.
Maybe this way, his stats would receive a greater increase.
Dodging claw attacks from the imps, he honed his dexterity and agility. Wrestling with the bulky orcs, he tempered his strength.
By the time he sensed that the Astraea Familia's patrols would soon conclude, he made his way back to the surface.
Akira
LV 1
Strength: E442 → D563
Durability: E467 → D542
Dexterity: D502 → C642
Agility: E492 → C604
Magic: B721 → A887
Astraea carefully printed the updated stats onto a parchment and handed it to him. She couldn't hide her astonishment.
"Though it's slowed compared to your first days, your growth is still incredible. Your magic is already close to S. Maybe... you can even surpass the limit." Her voice carried a tinge of reverent awe.
Akira blinked and asked, "The limit?"
Astraea lifted her snowy-white arm and gracefully drew two glowing letters in the air.
S S
"We all know the basic rule—stats cap at S999. Take Ottar, for example."
The name carried weight.
Ottar—the king, the undisputed number one in all of Orario.
But he wasn't renowned for overwhelming his enemies. His legend came from something far more grueling—his defeats.
Defeat, followed by relentless challenge. Again and again.
That was Ottar's path.
He would not level up unless every stat hit S999.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 29 - 29: Magic Stat SS, A Jack Bird
chapters.content:
"But S999 isn't truly the limit." Astraea said softly, her eyes calm yet profound.
"That number… it only seems like a limit because most people can't even dream of reaching S in the first place."
The closer one's stats approach the so-called threshold, the harder it becomes to break through.
Every increase takes double—no, perhaps triple the effort. It's like trying to climb a mountain that gets steeper with every step.
And the cruelest part?ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
Even if you pour in endless sweat, even if you risk your life day and night, you still might not make the slightest progress.
"That's the reason the gods never made SS the official highest rank."
Astraea continued, "But Akira, there are indeed some who've surpassed the barrier of S999. They've broken through to SS. So I believe you can too. No—I know you can."
She spoke with a finality that resonated in Akira's heart.
Indeed, seven years from now, a boy—Bell Cranel—would prove the same truth.
His story shouted at Akira across time. As long as your potential hasn't run dry, as long as you face mighty foes again and again, you will rise.
The status board was never a ceiling—it was a sky. Beyond 'S', there is 'SS'. Beyond 'SS', there's 'SSS'. And even that isn't the end.
SSS1300+… SSS1400+… SSS1500+...
So where exactly is the limit?
Akira raised his chin, his eyes blazing with determination as he looked into Astraea's gaze.
"I understand now, Astraea-sama. I'll surpass my limits and show you!"
Astraea felt her heart ripple as she looked at the child before her. She smiled warmly and wrapped him in a hug full of justice and love.
"You definitely will." She whispered close to his ear. "My brave hero."
— — —
[Personal Information]
Name: Akira
Age: 13
Level: 25
A resolve began to bloom in Akira's chest, fierce and unwavering. He would protect the Astraea Familia from the looming storm ahead.
Wielding a one-handed sword in his right hand and an elegant spear in the left, Akira surged forward.
The winds howled around him, wrapping his body like a tempest. He didn't even spare the imps a glance as he sprinted directly toward the orcs and silverbacks that awaited.
A clash of steel and flesh rang out as Akira's blade met the orc's armored fist.
The deadlock lasted just a moment. Then, Akira leaped back, narrowly evading a retaliatory blow.
Then, with lightning reflexes, he thrust the spear into the orc's nape, using it's skull as a platform to pivot mid-air. With a clean arc, his sword flashed and the orc's head fell clean off.
Then just a moment later, the silverback swung its giant fists. Just before impact, Akira moved.
He stepped onto the fist crashing toward the earth, ran up its arm, and with a single, fluid movement, decapitated the towering beast.
Once their strongest had fallen, the remaining orcs and imps were nothing. One by one, they were cut down—until silence reclaimed the dungeon floor.
By the third day of his exploration on the eleventh floor, Akira had grown powerful enough to defeat a silverback, even while fending off multiple threats.
Akira
LV 1
Strength: D563 → C689
Durability: D542 → C686
Dexterity: C642 → B787
Agility: C604 → B767
Magic: A892 → SS1008
Astraea's eyes sparkled as she looked at the updated parchment. She gently touched the glowing numbers, as if reaffirming they were real.
"Akira, you did it. You've crossed a threshold others can barely even glimpse."
She leaned forward, smiling meaningfully. "If others found out about this, you'd be the talk of Orario. I wouldn't be surprised if even Loki or Freya herself tried to poach you."
Akira didn't flinch. He simply looked at his goddess with unwavering loyalty.
He firmly said, "Astraea-sama… I'll never leave your side. And this—this isn't my peak. The real show's only just beginning."
— — —
Thick mist blanketed the eleventh floor of the dungeon, making visibility tricky but not impossible.
"Oi, is that guy even human? No way a Level 1 can move like that…"
"He's from the Astraea Familia, right? I saw him with Scarlet Harnel a few days back. Weren't they famous for turning people away? Are they recruiting again?"
"Wait, didn't I see that kid on the tenth floor earlier? What the hell's he doing, already fighting on the eleventh?"
Akira's name spread like ripples in water, carried by the awe-struck voices of adventurers.
What was he doing while all this buzz swirled around?
Facing a silverback ape.
The beast's iron fist thundered toward him, blowing wind through Akira's hair as magic surged through his veins.
Power exploded in his limbs, and he met the blow head-on—fist against fist. The impact blew the fog away, revealing the battlefield in startling clarity.
Akira was thrown back several meters, blood trailing from his hand. But despie that, he had a grin stretched across his face. He had moved the silverback back.
He stepped forward again.
"Ora ora ora ora!!"
His fists flew faster, wrapped in howling wind. As the silverback's punch neared, Akira's fists struck faster than the eye could follow, battering every inch of the beast's exposed skin.
With a final, thunderous blow, the silverback's arm erupted in blood—bone shattered, muscle torn.
The once fearsome beast backed away in terror. It let out a hollow roar and turned tail, trying to escape.
But Akira didn't let it do that. He soared into the air, his right leg wrapped in howling wind, forming a whirlwind of pressure around him.
His body became a missile, and his foot—the hammer of judgment.
With a single, explosive kick, he pierced through the silverback's back.
But he didn't stop there. He extracted its magic stone, and stepped firmly on the ground and slid over, the wind on his body, cracking the ground beneath him.
His hands were swollen, his arms sore. But his spirit blazed ever hotter.
"That's enough for today." He muttered.
He retrieved a potion to heal his battered limbs before turning toward the exit.
Three days. That's how long he'd spent boxing with silverbacks.
And now? He could win with his fists alone.
A lone adventurer watching from afar mumbled in disbelief, "Is he... really just LV 1?"
Back on the first floor, Akira spotted a peculiar rooster with bright yellow-green feathers. His body reacted before his mind caught up.
He switched his class to Swift Master, vanished, and reappeared in a blur—his blade executing a flawless slash.
The creature collapsed.
Jack Bird. A rare monster, not dangerous, but fast—absurdly fast. If it noticed an enemy, it would escape immediately.
But not today.
Akira picked up the golden egg it dropped—worth at least a million valis—and tucked it safely into his [Backpack].
He couldn't wait to return home and show it off to his Familia.

chapters.title: Chapter 30 - 30: Golden Egg, SSS
chapters.content:
Evening.
The kitchen of Astraea Familia.
Laughter and chatter echoed around the dinner table as the members gathered, enjoying the warm, home-cooked meal prepared by their goddess.
As always, the conversation drifted toward daily life, and tonight, it was cheerful—no ambushes, no Evilus sightings.
Indeed, not a single report had come in about those vile factions causing trouble.
Ordinary citizens now dared to stroll the streets, and merchants resumed their businesses with hope. Even petty crimes seemed to be fading. Orario, for once, thrived in peace.
Amidst this rare serenity, Akira stood up from his seat with a mysterious smirk.
He threw both arms in the air and proclaimed dramatically, "Good evening, my lovely sisters!"
Everyone froze, turning to look at him in bewilderment.
What was he up to now?
After spending so much time with him, they'd all come to know his quirks quite well.
When they first met him, he'd been a shy and bashful boy. But over time, it had become clear—he was a curious blend of Alise's recklessness and Ryuu's aloofness. Half fool, half goof.
"Today is a day worth celebrating! No tragedy, no disasters—only pure, unadulterated good news!"
Akira closed his eyes, arms raised, wearing an expression of deep satisfaction and exaggerated elegance.
Laughter broke out around the table at his theatrical display.
"Look at what you've done, Alise." Someone teased, pointing at her.
"You've totally corrupted him. He's a miniature version of you now."
Rather than being offended, Alise looked absolutely thrilled, puffing up her chest proudly. "Naturally."
"Alright, Akira, stop being so dramatic. If you've got something good to share, spill it already."
With exaggerated slowness, Akira reached behind his back as if unveiling a grand treasure. Everyone leaned in, their curiosity bubbling.
With a smug grin, he suddenly pulled out a glittering golden egg and held it high over his head. The dazzling light caught everyone's attention.
"What is that? It's sparkling so brightly!" Someone exclaimed, shielding their eyes.
Truthfully, the "sparkle" was just a trick—Akira had secretly used a light enchantment to enhance the effect.
Alise was the first to pounce. She snatched the egg and inspected it with gleaming eyes.
"Whoa! It's a golden egg!" Her excitement quickly faded.
"Eh? What's it for though?"
Lyra sighed at Alise's confusion and stepped in with her usual calm.
She said, "If Akira's this excited to show it off, it must be a rare dungeon drop. Considering he's been underground all day, it likely came from some unusual monster."
Neze leaned forward impatiently and said, "Don't stop halfway—just tell us already!"
Flustered, Akira snatched the egg back, raising it high.
He said, "I-I got it myself! Shouldn't I be the one to say it?"
"Fine." Lyra smirked. "Then say it together."
"In fact."
Akira and Lyra chorused, "This is a drop from the elusive Jack Bird, a rare monster found only on the dungeon's first floor!"
Akira turned to glare at Lyra, who was sticking out her tongue mockingly. He sighed with exaggerated despair.
'Finally got payback for teasing me last time.' Lyra thought smugly.
Gasps rang out.
"The golden egg worth a million Valis?!"
Asta reached out to touch the golden surface and said, "I heard that thing's only appeared once in years… and Akira actually ran into it. What incredible luck!"
Ryuu gently tugged on Akira's sleeve, smiling. She asked, "So? What will you do with this treasure? Are you planning to sell it?"
Hearing Ryuu's inquiry, Akira blinked. He hadn't even considered that. He'd just wanted to show it off. But now that Ryuu mentioned it…
After a moment, he beamed and said, "No! Let's not sell it. I think… we should keep it as a keepsake! Something for our familia to treasure. It's rare because it's precious, after all."
He turned to Astraea, his eyes gleaming with pride.
He said, "Astraea-sama, don't you think this would be perfect for you to show off to the other gods?"
At the head of the table, Astraea had been quietly watching with a serene smile. When Akira looked at her with such innocent pride, her heart melted.
She walked over and gently tapped the golden egg with her finger, smiling warmly.
She said, "I will absolutely show this off to the other gods. I'll tell them it was a gift from my precious child—a symbol of luck and pride."
"Well done, Akira." Neze said as she ruffled his hair affectionately.
— — —Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
Later, in Astraea's room, she was updating Akira's Falna. Alise and the others had gathered too, and Astraea shared the momentous news.
Akira had broken through the limit.
Ryuu, who once aimed to reach S999 herself, recalled how she had fallen short of that impossible line. Upon hearing Akira had gone beyond, she couldn't hide her joy.
"Congratulations, Akira." She said with a gentle smile.
Looking at the happy faces surrounding him, Akira suddenly understood something—it wasn't just about breaking limits. It was about why he did it. He'd done it for this. For them.
"We've only just begun." He said confidently.
"You'll see even more surprises from me soon!"
Akira
LV 1
Strength: C689 → S912
Durability: C686 → S908
Agile: B787 → S986
Agility: B767 → S978
Magic: SS1008 → SSS1220
"I didn't even know SSS was a thing, Akira, you're full of surprises."
Hearing SSS, Lyra leaned toward the parchment and stood on tiptoe to peek. "What's this? A brand-new tier!?"
Astraea chuckled and handed the parchment to her. Lyra's eyes lit up as the others crowded around to see.
When they saw the soaring magic stat, Alise burst out laughing and said, "Hahaha! With Akira and me at the helm, the Astraea Familia will defeat Evilus and slay the One-Eyed black dragon!"
Kaguya, watching their antics, exploded. "You two idiots!!"
She punched them both on the head.
"Ow!" ×2
"Quiet down, morons!"
Ryuu quickly pulled Kaguya into a hug and said, "They're just excited, that's all. No need to get violent."
Watching them bicker and banter as usual, Lyra's concerns eased. Akira hadn't changed at all despite his skyrocketing stats. He was still the same boy who got flustered easily and acted goofy around family.
Astraea watched them with gentle eyes.
Akira… While your breakthrough is incredible, what truly makes me proud is your humility. Fame, power—you don't chase those things. You value your familia.
She stepped forward, pulling them all into a warm hug. "Having all of you as my children… It's the greatest blessing I've received since descending to this world."
"And we're lucky to have you too, Astraea-sama!" Alise grinned radiantly.

chapters.title: Chapter 31 - 31: Akira VS Infant Dragon
chapters.content:
[Personal Information]
Name: Akira
Age: 13
Level: 26
Twilight Manor
"Captain, is it true that a Level 1 adventurer can fight a silverback barehanded?" Raul, a new recruit, asked his captain with curiosity.
Although Finn initially found the question strange, he still replied thoughtfully, "A Level 1 adventurer capable of reaching the eleventh floor should have fairly high stats. But even so, very few can take on a silverback unarmed. Why do you ask, Raul?"
Scratching his cheek with an awkward smile, Raul replied, "I heard a rumor from the guild when I came back. They said someone on the eleventh floor fought a silverback with their bare hands."
Finn narrowed his eyes slightly and asked, "Did they mention which familia that person belongs to?"
Raul thought for a moment and answered, "Oh, right! Yes, Captain. I think I heard them say it was a new recruit from the Astraea Familia."
"Astraea Familia?" Finn murmured, a faint smile forming on his lips.
"Looks like the righteous familia just added a remarkable new member to their already impressive lineup."
Recalling the powerful group of eleven girls and a certain troublesome one among them, he couldn't help but chuckle bitterly.
Finn said, "You've done well, Raul. You can leave the documents here and return to your duties."
Raul replied, "Understood! I'll head back now."
— — —
Silver Mansion
After gently knocking, Ottar stepped into a room as he handed over a document to Freya.
Freya casually flipped through the pages, her gray eyes filled with lazy disinterest.
Tossing the papers aside, she said languidly, "I've seen this one before. His soul has a decent shine—but only decent. Don't waste time watching him too closely."
"Yes, Freya-sama. Understood." Ottar replied dutifully.
— — —
Today, Akira set his sights on the twelfth floor.
Though the monsters on the twelfth floor were mostly the same as the eleventh floor, their frequency and danger had notably increased.The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
Silverbacks, for instance, now appeared in clusters—four or five at a time rather than just one or two.
There was even the looming possibility of encountering an Infant dragon, one of the upper-floor bosses known for its fearsome might.
Thanks to a recent status update, Akira could now handle these dangers with remarkable ease.
Using a one-handed sword he had purchased for 150,000 Valis, he intercepted a charging Hard Armored's wheel-like body. Then, he shifted his footing, and drove the blade into its core, exposing its insides.
Blood coated his sword as the beast collapsed.
With swift reflexes, Akira dodged a barrage of spinning beasts, then intercepted a silverback's massive punch.
Without wasting a single moment, he sliced through the limb, surged forward, and met the creature's scarlet eyes with his own black ones.
In the blink of an eye, his sword flashed and the ape's head soared.
He stomped on the falling corpse to gain height, flipped midair, and launched another slash at a second Silverback rushing in. Blood exploded as he landed smoothly in front of its crumpled body.
"Too easy. Looks like silverbacks don't even qualify as warm-up anymore." Akira muttered, visibly pleased with his performance.
At this moment, a sudden noise entered his ears.
Boom! Boom! Boom—
The ground trembled far more violently than it had before.
Through the dense fog, a shadow began to take shape. Four to five meters tall, its massive figure loomed ever closer.
"Is that… an Infant dragon?"
Akira's eyes sparkled as he watched the monster approach, its long neck and tail swinging ominously through the mist.
"ROAR! ROAR! ROAR—!"
The ground-shaking howls echoed through the floor, causing nearby adventurers to pause and instinctively prepare to retreat.
As the mist cleared, its form became unmistakable—amber scales, razor-sharp claws, a maw full of deadly fangs, a muscular tail, and a horned, majestic head that radiated terrifying power.
Akira's lips curled into a grin.
As part of the legendary dragon race—considered the strongest among monsters—this young dragon, despite its undeveloped wings and inability to fly, exuded overwhelming might. Its hardened scales alone hinted at monstrous strength far exceeding that of any orc.
This was a monster that could easily wipe out a low-level party. Many adventurers had lost their lives just trying to escape it.
But Akira didn't flinch.
He stepped forward and then bolted straight towards it.
'There's no turning back now. Let's see just how much nourishment you can offer me!'
The Infant dragon spotted him and bent its limbs, making the earth quake as it braced for combat. Then it spun around and swung its tail with immense force.
Akira ducked low, narrowly evading the sweeping strike. Rising, he dashed forward and carved into the dragon's hind leg with his sword.
The dragon bellowed in pain, its long neck twisting around. It's blood-red eyes locked onto Akira and it raised its front claws, poised to crush him.
'Just one strike from that, and my head will pop like a melon.'
He rolled forward, just escaping the blow, and retaliated by slashing deep into the dragon's exposed belly.
Then, evading its claws again, he leapt, gripping one of the raised scales with his left hand, and vaulted onto its back.
As the dragon tried to shake him off, Akira stepped firmly, drove his fingers into one of its eyes, then kicked its writhing head and launched himself into the air.
He landed on the grass with practiced ease.
The dragon writhed in agony, its rage intensifying. It lunged at Akira, jaws wide and drooling, its breath hot and reeking of blood.
Akira danced through its strikes, carving shallow wounds along its head. The more injuries he inflicted, the slower and heavier its movements became. Now, even its breathing was loud and ragged.
Seeing the monster panting and stumbling, Akira knew it was over.
"Time to finish this."
Power surged around his sword as he gathered wind into the blade. With a sharp cry, he swung down fiercely. A bright green arc slashed cleanly across the dragon's body.
The Infant dragon gave one final roar and then split in two and crumbled to the ground.
In the center of its remains lay a fist-sized magic stone, a dragon horn, and several gleaming dragon scales.

chapters.title: Chapter 32 - 32: Ais: He is a Good Person
chapters.content:
Akira calmly collected the Infant dragon's magic stone along with the horn and several shimmering amber scales, storing them neatly into his backpack.
The adventurers nearby, who had been watching from a distance with eyes full of expectation or perhaps greed, began to quietly disperse.
They had initially assumed the solo adventurer couldn't possibly handle an Infant dragon alone.
In fact, several of them had already begun subtly repositioning themselves, waiting for the right moment to swoop in and "rescue" him—then conveniently claim the kill.
But who would have thought… one person would take it down on their own?
Apparently, after his latest status update, not even an Infant dragon could pose much of a threat to Akira.
Akira glanced around the area where the Infant dragon's rampage had left its mark. It's lingering pressure still clung to the air, causing lesser monsters to stay away for the time being.
Taking advantage of the momentary peace, Akira leaned against a thick tree trunk and pulled out the boxed lunch carefully prepared by his goddess.
A pleasant aroma drifted in the dungeon air as he bit into it, savoring both the taste and the brief calm.
After wandering the twelfth floor for quite some time, he found no sign of another Infant dragon. Instead, the dungeon decided to spice things up by spawning five silverbacks around him at the same time. That almost cost him his life.
Five silverbacks in unison were no joke—they charged at him from two different angles, fists pounding like thunder, and then lunged in from above in a coordinated assault.
Akira barely avoided getting crushed. If not for his resilience and reflexes, he might have been forced to reveal more than just swordsmanship.
And things only got worse. Because he took too long to deal with them, their roars attracted even more monsters—imps, orcs, and Hard Armoreds all came rushing in like an avalanche.
By the time Akira finished dispatching them, his arms were sore, and his sword had already started showing cracks.
Then it happened.
As he brought his blade down to slash at a rolling Hard Armored, the one-handed sword he'd purchased for a whopping 150,000 Valis finally gave up.
Bang!
The blade snapped in half with a metallic cry of protest.
Akira stood in silence for a moment, staring at the broken remains of his beloved weapon.
He bent down, calmly collected the fragments, and tucked them away in his bag with a sigh.
He would have them reforged at one of the Hephaestus familia's shop later.
"…Damn it, this is absurd! I don't want to play anymore!!" He shouted, half in frustration, half in mock despair.
Donning his hood to obscure his identity, Akira made sure not to reveal that he was a magic user. Drawing his staff would be too risky. For now, he'd fight with raw magic power alone.
The magic power in his body surged, converting into frost energy. Dozens of massive, cone-shaped icicles formed above him, suspended like divine spears.
Akira pointed forward.
"Go!"
The lances screamed downward, skewering the charging orcs with deadly precision.
Raising his hands skyward, he willed flame into existence. Three rows of fiery columns erupted from the earth like volcanic geysers.
Imps and freshly spawned silverbacks wailed in agony, consumed in searing light, reduced to charred ash.
Then, pressing his palms together, a magic circle spun into existence above him.
Dozens of spectral Ice Swords manifested mid-air, glimmering with blue light.
A whirlwind formed at his feet, lifting his body into the air. Then, with a sweeping motion, Akira directed the Ice Swords toward his enemies.
The blades surged forward, piercing skulls, torsos, or limbs.
Changing into Swift Master, Akira darted through the battlefield with blinding speed, slicing through the horde while simultaneously gathering materials and magic stones.
"I'll head to the thirteenth floor and see what kind of beasts are waiting there."
From the thirteenth floor onward, the terrain shifted dramatically.
The ceiling rose even higher, and passages twisted through the stone like veins in a living organism.
Unlike the simple layout of the upper floors, these caves led not only to different rooms but sometimes straight down to lower floors through vertical holes. The place was a true maze, both horizontally and vertically.
Akira didn't plan to go too deep for now. But as he entered a wide cave, dozens of glowing crimson eyes glared back at him.
Almiraj.
Rabbit-like monsters with snowy white fur, nearly human-sized.
They looked cute but don't be fooled. They were battle maniacs.
Individually, they weren't dangerous. A Level 1 adventurer could take one down alone. But in groups, they were recognized as Level 2.
Worse, they carried tiny hand axes, useful for both melee and throwing.
But their most iconic trait?
A relentless will to fight to the bitter end.
"Squeak... Squeak..." ×N
Akira pulled out a spare one-handed sword from his [Backpack], infused it with magic power, and charged into the mass of hopping maniacs.
A minute later, he was crouching, digging out magic stones from the limp, fur-covered corpses.
Despite being chopped in half, several Almiraj had still attempted to hurl their axes at him mid-death. It was... impressive in a way.
At this moment, he suddenly heard cracking sounds from the cave walls.
Several pitch-black hounds leapt out of the darkness, snarling.
Hellhounds.
The first two charged in with bared fangs, jaws wide, while the rest opened their mouths—fire beginning to flicker inside.
Hellhounds were on the weaker end of the middle-floor monsters, but their fire breath had claimed the lives of many overconfident adventurers.
That's why most carried a Salamander Wool protection when exploring these levels.
Akira, without such luxury, met the bites with his blade and released another round of Ice Swords with his free hand, slashing open the hounds' throats.
Then—
FWOOSH!
Twin flames burst toward him.
Akira instinctively summoned a towering ice wall, blocking the inferno just in time.
Then he charged forward, flipped mid-air, and with a flash of sword light, decapitated both flaming beasts in one elegant motion.
"…Alise's clothes…!"ᴛhis ᴜpdated by
Akira looked down, horrified. Several blackened holes marred the outfit Alise had lovingly bought for him.
His skin was unharmed, protected by his magic, but the damage to the clothes was irreparable.
"Those flames! They got my clothes!" He wailed internally.
Among all the monsters on the thirteenth floor, only the hellhound's flame had proven troublesome to him. So, he decided it was best to retreat and prepare before pushing deeper.
Just as he ascended the stairway from the thirteenth to the twelfth floor, his gaze caught sight of a familiar green figure ahead.
She had sensed him, too. The figure turned—golden eyes locking with his.
Loki Familia.
Ais Wallenstein stood quietly, her expression unreadable.
Riveria, noticing Ais had stopped walking, raised an eyebrow. She followed Ais's gaze and spotted a young half-elf adventurer.
"Do you know him?" Riveria asked, crouching slightly.
Ais tilted her head, nodded, and then shook it.
"He gave me two red bean cream-flavored potato balls. He's a good person." She said softly.
Riveria sighed deeply and said, "Don't just take food from strangers… and don't judge someone's character based on snacks, either."
Akira, intent on simply slipping past as an anonymous passerby, had already turned to leave—when Ais suddenly grabbed his sleeve, forcing him to halt.
He turned around slowly, a helpless smile tugging at his lips.
"Aren't these Sword Princess and Nine Hell? What business might you two have with a lowly adventurer like me?" He asked, raising a brow.
Ais met his gaze, frowning slightly.
She asked, "Good evening. Why are you avoiding me? What's your name?"
(End of Chapter)
