chapters.title: Chapter 33 - 33: Akira: What an Old Lady
chapters.content:
With a sigh, Akira finally replied, "My name is Akira, and I'm a member of the Astraea Familia."
Both Ais and Riveria were well-known figures and would eventually find out about him anyway.
Especially with his level-up looming—it wasn't worth hiding anymore.
"Astraea Familia? I didn't hear about any new members joining…"
Riveria's brows furrowed slightly, her tone laced with curiosity and doubt.
"Ais Wallenstein, member of the Loki Familia." Ais mimicked Akira's tone and gave her own simple introduction with a composed expression.
After their brief introductions, both sets of eyes landed on Riveria, silently urging her to speak next.
Caught in their gazes, Riveria let out a breath and complied. "Riveria Ljos Alf. Deputy Captain of the Loki Familia. My full name is rather long, so just call me Riveria."
"Understood, Riveria-san." Akira nodded calmly, his demeanor neither arrogant nor too reserved.
Riveria raised an eyebrow, clearly pleased by the respectful yet unfawning response. Despite her origins from the royal elven line, Akira didn't show the kind of reverence that usually irritated her when coming from her own people.
As the silence lingered awkwardly, Riveria took the initiative and asked, "When did you join the familia? Are you adapting well to Orario? Anything I can help you with?"
Her barrage of questions rolled out rapidly, as if she'd stored them all for this one moment. She reminded Akira of a nagging elder, which made him twitch internally.
Ais gently tugged Riveria's sleeve and spoke up softly, "Riveria, that's too many questions. Akira can't answer them all at once."
Akira muttered under his breath with a helpless face, "What an old lady…"
Bonk!
A staff landed squarely on his head. Akira clutched the sore spot, blinking at Riveria with innocent eyes.
"I thought I heard something disrespectful just now." Riveria's gaze sharpened.
"Akira, don't go teasing people lightly. It doesn't suit you."
Akira exaggerated a deep bow, playing along. "Forgive me, Riveria-sama."
Bonk—again!
This time, Riveria calmly withdrew her staff, as though it were routine. Having handled all sorts of personalities in her familia, she could already tell Akira was going to be a handful.
She said, "You deserved that. You're just as troublesome as Ais."
"I'm not a troublesome child!" Ais puffed up her cheeks and shot Riveria a pouty glare, like a sulking kitten.
Riveria ignored her protest entirely and turned her attention back to Akira. "The Astraea Familia's base is near ours. Come back with us."
Then, after a moment's pause, she narrowed her eyes. "Also, you didn't answer my question."
Akira let out a weary sigh, as though dealing with Riveria required more stamina than a dungeon dive.
He said, "I arrived in Orario half a month ago. The people in Astraea Familia are kind and welcoming. I've enjoyed my stay."
Riveria didn't pry further, even though she'd clearly noticed that a newcomer reaching the thirteenth floor in just two weeks was far from ordinary. Everyone had their secrets.
Instead, she simply smiled and said, "That's good to hear."
The three of them began walking side by side, chatting as the night breeze drifted around them.
— — —
Back on the surface, along the quieter northern end of the city streets…
"Guess I'll head off here. See you next time, Ais, Riveria-sama." At a fork in the road, Akira waved and bid his farewell.
"Goodbye, Akira." Ais waved softly in return, her small hand brushing the edge of her waist as she murmured a gentle parting.
Riveria nodded slightly, her expression unusually warm. "Take care. And if you have the chance, I think you and Ais should go on an adventure together. You two seem like a good match."
"I'll remember that. I'll visit the Loki Familia next time and invite Ais personally. How about it, Ais?" Akira turned to the golden-haired girl with a teasing glint in his eyes.
Though she normally wore a blank expression, Ais's eyes sparkled slightly at this moment.
She nodded firmly and said, "I want to go on an adventure with Akira."
She sounded like a child who'd been promised a rare treat. Clearly, she hadn't had enough fun adventuring under Riveria's supervision.
Riveria tapped her on the head lightly and reminded, "You can adventure together, but don't drag him too deep. Understood?"
"...Yes."
Ais pouted and nodded reluctantly, glancing at Akira once more before saying goodbye again.
As the two turned to leave, Akira headed off toward a quiet corner of the city—Stardust Garden.
As soon as he stepped through the doorway, Akira spotted Ryuu standing there absent-mindedly, almost like a statue guarding the entrance.
He asked, "Lion? What are you doing just standing there?"
Startled, Ryuu twitched slightly at the sound of his voice.
She said, "Akira… I was just… waiting for you."
Akira tilted his head and asked, "Waiting for me? Why?"
Blushing faintly, Ryuu crossed her arms and explained, "It was Kaguya. She said, 'You're in the way standing there. Go wait for Akira at the door unless you want to get hit by it again like last time.'"
Akira laughed and said, "Haha, Kaguya-nee always loves giving you a hard time, huh? But don't worry—next time she tries that, I'll be on your side."
Ryuu's lips curled into a faint smile. Her heart fluttered as she looked at him.
She said, "Akira… can you… just call me Ryuu?"
"What was that?" Akira leaned in, pretending not to hear.
Flustered, Ryuu waved her hands and stammered, "N-Nothing! I was just talking to myself!"
But Akira wasn't letting her off that easily. He moved in even closer, nose nearly touching hers. "Really? Lion, are you hiding something from me?"
Ryuu was about to collapse from the sheer tension of the moment, her pale cheeks burning like embers.
Just as she looked ready to faint, Akira straightened up with a mischievous grin, turned sideways, and extended his hand.
"Come on, Ryuu! If we're late, someone's going to eat all the food!" He gently grabbed her hand and led her inside.
After dinner, Akira showered and headed to Astraea's room for his status update.Follow current novᴇls on ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
Akira
Level: 1
Strength: S912 → SS1102
Endurance: S908 → SS1103
Dexterity: S986 → SS1156
Agility: S978 → SS1146
Magic: SSS1220 → SSS1384
Astraea silently stared at the numbers on the parchment, her brows twitching slightly. Akira's stats were climbing at a pace that defied common sense.
"Just how far are you planning to raise your stats before leveling up?" She asked, gently brushing aside the strands of hair falling into her eyes.
Akira's gaze fell to the parchment. He thought for a moment before replying, "I think I'll level up once all my stats hit 'SSS'. Right now, the floors I'm on feel a little too easy. I want to go deeper before I break through."
Astraea smiled gently, wrapping her fingers around his hand—the one now interlocked with hers.
"As your goddess, I'll respect whatever path you choose. But as your familia, I hope you won't be reckless. Don't let your ambition drive you into danger too soon."
With a quiet hum, Akira leaned back into her arms, resting his head comfortably in her lap. His hand, entwined with hers, rose to his face. He pulled it over his eyes like a veil, blocking out the flickering candlelight.
"I understand."
As your familia… I want you to come back safely. Always.

chapters.title: Chapter 34 - 34: Seventeenth Floor
chapters.content:
On the way to the fifteenth floor, Akira donned a cloak made of salamander wool to prevent his clothes from being scorched by the Hellhounds' flames, as had happened before.
With the wind wrapping around his body, he slashed through the group of Needle Rabbits at blinding speed.
He cleaved a charging Hellhound in half, then kicked another just as it began to gather flames in its mouth. Its jaw snapped shut, causing the fireball to detonate prematurely.
In the same motion, Akira spun and sliced cleanly through its neck.
His goal today was to fight the Minotaurs and Ligers that roamed the fifteenth floor.
Although some monsters occasionally wandered up to the fourteenth floor, it was far more efficient to confront them at their source than to search endlessly through the sprawling maze.
After much effort, Akira finally arrived on the fifteenth floor.
He stepped down the stairs into a vast cavern. The ceiling loomed nearly twenty meters above the ground, surrounded by towering stacks of stone and treacherous pits scattered across the terrain.
These vertical shafts connected directly to the floors below—dangerous chasms that could drop an uncareful adventurer straight from the thirteenth to the seventeenth floor in an instant.
"ROAR—"
As Akira moved deeper into the cave, several large cracks split open in the cavern walls. Thick, gray-brown hands emerged, pressing against the stone.
Five Minotaurs, each towering over two meters tall, stepped forward.
These monsters, with bull heads and humanoid bodies, were slow and simple-minded—but they were one of the deadliest monsters of the middle floors. Their roars alone could strike fear into the hearts of most Level 1 adventurers.
The ground trembled as they charged, their massive arms extended to grab and crush him.
Akira ducked low, avoiding the first Minotaur's grasp, and slashed its thigh with his green-glowing sword. With fluid motion, he surged forward to face the others.
A flash of his blade severed an oncoming fist. Kicking off the wall, he flipped midair, evading a second Minotaur's punch.
With a spinning motion, Akira's blade sliced through the necks of three approaching Minotaurs like a hot knife through butter.
The remaining two, wounded and frightened, tried to flee. But Akira silently chased them down, dispatching them in quick, merciless cuts.
Just as he finished extracting the Minotaurs' magic stones and horns, the ground trembled. From beneath, eyeless worms with gnashing teeth burst out of the earth.
Before Akira could react, a loud cracking sound came from above. Four Ligers leapt from the ceiling to ambush him.
"Seriously? Am I being targeted by the dungeon? Why are there so many monsters all of a sudden?!" Akira growled.
He leapt backward to avoid the worms' bite, then twirled his blade and severed their writhing forms.
At that moment, a Liger lunged. Akira raised his left hand—an ice shield materialized just in time to block the beast's claws. Then with his right hand, he slashed.
Blood sprayed from the Liger's mutilated face, bone exposed as half its head peeled away.
Akira raised his shield to intercept more attacks. His sword began glowing red, flames spiraling around the blade. The searing heat forced the other Ligers to hesitate.
Akira hurled the shield aside and stomped hard, the ground cracking under the force.
In a burst of wind, he teleported into the middle of the triangle formation, his flaming sword cleaving through the rightmost Liger.
Then, his blade reversed and cleaved the central beast from groin to skull before pivoting again.
The inferno around his blade expanded into a massive, flaming greatsword. With one final swing, he brought it crashing down on the last Liger.
The firestorm faded.
Only scorched corpses remained, and a deep, black four-meter gash marked the earth.
He cooled his blade with a stream of water, then drew a knife and extracted the monsters' magic stones and fangs. Then he carefully placed them into a cloth bag and tucked into [Backpack].
Just as Akira moved to rest on a rock, the ground began to quake once more. The walls around him seemed to shift and retreat.
He tensed, a trace of panic creeping in. With a thought, he switched to his Swift Master, invoking powerful wind currents to flee.
Cracks spiderwebbed across the ground. A deafening boom echoed as the terrain within ten meters collapsed, transforming into a vertical pit.
During the fall, Akira prepared to summon a cushion of wind to escape—only for his vision to go dark.
A massive conical boulder plummeted directly toward the pit.
"What the hell! Are you kidding me?!" Akira swore.
He twisted mid-air, wind blasting beneath him. The currents slowed the boulder and flung him away.
"What the HELL!!!"
He hit the bottom hard and scrambled toward a nearby cave.
"BOOM—"
The boulder crashed down at the entrance, sealing it shut with rubble and dust.
Breathless, Akira collapsed on the ground. He wasn't dead, but he certainly felt like it.
After several minutes of lying there, he rose and began walking deeper into the cavern.
Winding through the tunnels, he eventually emerged into a massive chamber.
Shimmering rock lined the walls, stacked in perfect symmetry like crystal bricks.
The structure, known as the Wall of Sighs, formed the arena-like expanse of this colossal cavern.
Akira realized where he had landed, the Seventeenth Floor.
No random monsters were born here—only one, the infamous Floor Boss: Goliath.
The setup resembled a coliseum. One entrance, one exit—no ambiguity.
Fight or die.ᴛʜɪs ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀ ɪs ᴜᴘᴅᴀᴛᴇ ʙʏ NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
Beyond the arena, the hole in the wall led to the Eighteenth Floor—a safe zone rumored to be breathtakingly beautiful.
An underground paradise of nature and crystal, nearly the size of Orario itself. At night, its ceiling turned into a radiant starry sky.
The entire forest shimmered with ethereal crystals, irregularly shaped but dazzling in their glow. Their reflections painted the woodland in a soft, glowing blue.

chapters.title: Chapter 35 - 35: Killing the Goliath
chapters.content:
I have to go and check it out!
Akira made up his mind. Since the Goliath seemed to have been defeated, there was no harm in taking a look.
Thinking this, Akira casually walked toward the entrance up ahead.
Just as he stepped into the center of the massive cavern, preparing to proceed further—
Bang!
The wall, glittering like crystal, let out a sudden crackling explosion.
Jagged fissures webbed across its surface with a sharp bang, as if something monstrous was about to burst out from within.
With a deafening crash, a black hole erupted in the wall. From it, a massive head emerged.
"ROARRRR—!"
A ferocious roar assaulted Akira's ears, the sheer sound forcefully vibrating his chest.
The creature's massive hands slammed against the wall. With terrifying power, it pried the wall open wider, causing the crystalline structure to collapse entirely—revealing the beast within.
Amid the shattering debris, a towering giant over ten meters tall stood revealed before him.
"You've gotta be kidding me... it really just shows up like that?!"
Akira stared at the monster in disbelief, his mood quickly souring.
"This damn dungeon is just...!"Follow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
The Goliath's gray-brown skin bulged with terrifying muscles.
Oily black hair, slick like grease, hung to its neck, and a pair of burning scarlet eyes locked directly onto Akira.
With each slow, thundering step, the massive Goliath approached.
"This thing... isn't something I can deal with using just a one-handed sword."
Although this wasn't the enhanced black variant, it was still a bona fide Level 4 monster—complete with a ridiculously massive HP bar. A frontal confrontation wouldn't end well.
Akira's instincts kicked in. In a flash, he leapt left—just in time.
The monster's fist smashed into the ground he'd been standing on, reducing it to shattered rubble and blasting chunks of rock outward.
Dozens of spear-like ice crystals shot into existence, spinning through the air and crashing into the Goliath's face.
The giant staggered backward, dazed. Not missing a beat, Akira raised his hand and summoned a massive fireball.
BOOM!
Flames exploded across the Goliath's head. The stench of scorched hair filled the cavern. Black burns marred its face, with drops of blood trickling down grotesquely.
With a snarl, the Goliath retaliated, swinging a monstrous punch that gouged a trench into the nearby Wall of Sighs.
Akira activated his teleportation, vanishing into the air and reappearing above, transformed into his Swift Master form.
Fierce gusts howled around him, swirling into a coalescing tornado.
The Goliath below sensed the shift and its crimson gaze darted up. With a roar, it heaved a massive chunk of stone at Akira midair.
Unfazed, Akira focused on strengthening the storm. The winds intensified, whirling faster and faster. The boulder disintegrated at the edge of the vortex, shredded into fragments by the sheer force.
He pushed both hands forward, channeling the cyclone. A glowing magic circle ignited beneath his feet, and then—
Whoooosh!
A massive ten-meter-wide tornado surged downward.
The Goliath crossed its arms instinctively to shield its head. The storm ripped into its flesh like thousands of blades. The cavern floor itself was soaked red.
Ordinary Goliaths lacked the regenerative abilities or magic resistance of enhanced species. All they had was brute strength and a roar meant to terrify weak adventurers.
Now, before Akira's storm and tactics, it was nothing but prey.
Akira's shoulder-length hair slowly drifted with the wind. A faint coppery scent of blood clung to his body. His crimson eyes narrowed as he watched the dying Goliath twitching on the floor.
When the Goliath's dimming eyes met his own, the beast suddenly gasped and swung one final palm strike at Akira.
"Oh?"
Akira smirked and lightly raised his hand, as if to greet the monster.
CRACK—!
With a burst of blood magic, the blood pooled around the Goliath's body was instantly weaponized.
Blood-red spears impaled its body from every direction. One particularly large stake pierced it straight through the chest.
The massive hand that had been reaching toward him froze in mid-air.
Moments later, the Goliath's magic stone fell to the ground with a dull clink. Its massive body broke into ash, dissolving into the air.
All remaining blood energy in the area surged into Akira's Dark Eyes, strengthening it.
[Personal Information]
Name: Akira
Age: 13
Level: 30
Now that his level had reached thirty, his strength had taken another massive leap.
For the first time, Akira seriously considered advancing to a new class—Dimension Walker.
As the thought surfaced, his appearance changed yet again. At the same time, the Dark Eyes underwent another transformation.
A flood of new knowledge rushed into his brain—techniques for wielding dimensional energy, theories of space manipulation, and even the operation of a strange tool known as a Dimensional Distortion Device.
The moment he transformed into a Dimension Walker, his perception of the world shifted dramatically.
He could sense unseen movements, formless flows, creeping presences—and even eyes watching him from beyond.
As his gaze swept across the Wall of Sighs, he spotted several bizarre creatures slinking about. When they noticed Akira observing them, they shrieked eerily and vanished.
Akira exhaled and switched back to Elemental Blaster, still slightly dizzy. Though he'd taken no damage in the battle, the inherent power of the new class had nearly overwhelmed him.
He was just about to collect the fallen magic stone and head for the eighteenth floor when a glowing screen suddenly appeared in front of him.
[You have activated the power of all male mage sub-classes and met all the system's criteria. System update in progress. Estimated time: 3 days.]
"...The system can update?" Akira muttered, eyes blinking as the screen faded.
Well, nothing he could do now but wait and see what the update brought.
He bent down and picked up the massive one-meter-tall magic stone, carefully placing it into his [Backpack]. With nothing more to do here, he headed toward the entrance of the safe floor.
What awaited him was a place of mystery and breathtaking beauty—the 18th floor.
Majestic wetlands to the north, enchanted forests stretching to the south and east, sparkling lakes and scattered islands to the west, and in the east of one island stood the small adventurer town, Rivira.
Prices there were outright extortionate, yet the constant stream of goods proved just how essential it was to keep supply chains flowing even inside the dungeon.
Though Rivira had been destroyed and rebuilt over three hundred times, it always stood again. Its self-appointed administrator was a man named Bors Elder.
Akira, finally able to breathe, sat by a stream, cleaning his gear and clothes. After crawling around a collapsing cave and battling monsters, he was absolutely covered in dirt and dust.
He dunked his head directly into the flowing river, letting the cold water wash the grime from his hair. Afterward, he channeled wind fused with fire to create warm air, drying his hair with comfort.
Sometimes, Akira couldn't help but marvel at just how useful elemental magic really was.

chapters.title: Chapter 36 - 36: Thanatos, God of Death
chapters.content:
After lingering on the safe floor for a while, taking in the breathtaking scenery that one would never expect to find deep within the dungeon's depths, Akira finally began his journey back to the surface.
As he passed by the infamous Wall of Sighs, he noticed that the damaged floor had already begun to slowly restore itself to its original, pristine state.
Unable to suppress his irritation, he kicked the wall a few times, hurled a few curses at the dungeon itself, then swiftly turned and darted toward the upper floors.
Upon reaching the twelfth floor, Akira was suddenly met with an unexpected sight.
Emerging from the thick white fog was a figure clad in black robes. From beneath the figure's lowered hood, thick purple hair—so long it could be mistaken for a woman's—cascaded down like a waterfall.
His slender physique and symmetrical, refined features exuded a certain decadent charm, one that was unsettling rather than appealing.
The man's expression lit up with eerie joy the moment his eyes fell upon Akira.
He hadn't anticipated that aside from Ais, there would be another existence with such a dense, oppressive aura of death—and one that surpassed hers several times over.
Though Akira himself had not revealed anything outwardly, the man, a god attuned to death, had perceived it instantly.
"Ah… so it was you." He murmured softly,
"The one I sensed back on Daedalus Street. That stifling aura of death… it could only have belonged to you."
A twisted gleam entered his eyes.
"If it's you… surely, you could kill even more. Yes… so much more." Thanatos mused, locking eyes with the boy before him.
"Child, you must be so very lonely. No one understands you. No one can relate to your yearning for death. You've been suffering in silence all this time, haven't you?"
His voice dripped with enchantment, seductive and sinister, as if attempting to ensnare Akira's very soul.
"I can offer you a sanctuary, a place where no one will shackle you. Where you can indulge yourself—destroy, slaughter, unleash whatever darkness festers within you. I will never reject you."
"I shall shoulder your sins. You need only kill to your heart's content. All I ask… is that you join my Familia."
With a gentle smile, the god of death extended his hand in a gesture of invitation—one he had made to many before, yet always with the same expectation.
Akira's gaze sharpened. He silently narrowed his eyes at the bizarre deity spewing madness, his presence in the dungeon raising even more questions.
Something about this god reeked of wrongness.
Could it be… the very evil god that Astraea had once warned him about?
Akira slowly unsheathed his one-handed sword, his stance shifting subtly. His eyes didn't just lock on the god—he glanced behind him as well, alert for hidden threats.
Thanatos sighed, as though disappointed by a child who had failed to meet his expectations.
"Oh dear… it seems I've failed again. What a shame. That girl rejected me, and now you—so thoroughly soaked in blood—also turn me away."
"But then again." He said with a bitter chuckle.
"It's only natural. If you were someone who could be swayed by words, you wouldn't have fallen under that goddess of justice's wing. What a waste… I had such high hopes of discovering another avatar of death."
Though Thanatos could clearly sense the presence of the goddess of justice on Akira—the same one who had thwarted Evilus again and again—he still made one final, desperate attempt to seduce her champion.
Akira tightened his grip on the sword and carefully asked, "Are you… a god of Evilus?"
As if on cue, the fog stirred.
Two adventurers, previously hidden within the mist, stepped forward to stand in front of Thanatos, weapons drawn.
Thanatos waved dismissively and said with mock embarrassment, "I'm terribly sorry. I truly wanted to introduce myself properly, but Evilus always insists on such secrecy. Didn't I say before that I shouldn't reveal my name to mortals? Ah… such a nuisance."
It was clear that he was associated with Thanatos.
Akira's gaze returned to him. If he could defeat this so-called god of death here and now, perhaps it would weaken Evilus' grip on the world, even if just a little.
"Haha… that expression… that gleam in your eyes as you look upon me, filled with such intense killing intent…" Thanatos grinned, his amusement only growing.
"You truly are worthy of that justice goddess's favor. Bold. So bold… And yet, you do know, don't you? That killing a god is taboo."
"But I do adore your courage."
His words rolled off his tongue like sweet poison.
"I have no intention of killing gods." Akira replied coldly. "I simply want to send them back where they belong."
And with that, he raised his sword and slashed at the two adventurers who stood in his way.
The clash of blades rang out as the two forces collided. Akira found himself pushed back by the sheer force of the defenders.
From the weight of their strikes and their steady coordination, Akira could tell—they were probably Level 2 adventurers. And they might possess specialized magic and unique skills as well.
His sword blazed with crimson flame. Akira moved to finish the skirmish swiftly and focus on Thanatos but just then, one enemy vanished in a flash while the other hurled a handful of flaming projectiles.
Explosions rocked the space.
Smoke enveloped everything, mixing with the thick white fog, reducing visibility even further.
From the depths of the smoke, a sudden glint of steel appeared and a sword whistled toward his neck.
In a split-second reaction, Akira raised his blade to intercept it. He pivoted sharply, his foot slamming into the ground as he twisted his body and delivered a fierce kick—sending the attacker hurtling backwards.
Without pause, he unleashed a devastating arc of blazing slash.
The scorching flame roared forward, intent on cleaving through the enemy—
Only to dissipate entirely.
A wave of ominous energy surged through the area—dark purple, suffocating in intensity, and undeniably divine.
The flame vanished like a candle snuffed by water.
Thanatos had broken the ultimate rule.
Divinity had been released in the dungeon.
"Oops." Thanatos chuckled with mock concern.
"My bad. I couldn't help myself. What a pain." His carefree tone was utterly out of place given the disaster he had just triggered.
The dungeon responded almost immediately.
The entire twelfth floor began to tremble. A deep, guttural groan echoed from the walls, followed by a rumbling roar—like a beast stirred from ancient slumber.
The ground shook violently.
Akira's eyes scanned the area. Through the fog, he could make out three distinct cave entrances.
Then came the sound—like an avalanche crashing down from every direction.
The exits were collapsing!?
At that moment, the ceiling above them cracked. Debris rained from above as something massive hurtled down with tremendous force—straight for Thanatos.
"Eh? So fast this time? Even the reaction zone has narrowed?" Thanatos muttered with a sigh.
Hovering above him was a pitch-black wyvern-like creature, its wings like jagged blades and radiating intense murderous intent.Follow current novels on Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
"They're not playing around this time. Looks like they want me dead before I can even blink."
All across Orario, the gods felt it—another surge of divinity released from within the dungeon.
And this time, it was from the upper floors—close to the surface.
The reaction was instantaneous.
"Who the hell's using Divinity again!?"
"Which damned idiot is causing trouble now!? Can't they give it a rest for once!?"

chapters.title: Chapter 37 - 37: Facing the Black Wyvern
chapters.content:
Loki Familia – Twilight Manor
"Loki, what's the matter?"
Finn turned toward Loki, who had suddenly paused in the middle of lounging, her expression uncharacteristically serious.
"Finn… someone just released divinity inside the Dungeon. Judging by the tremors, he's probably on the twelfth floor—same as when Ais encountered that situation before."
After years of working side by side, Finn immediately understood the unspoken urgency in Loki's words.
Without hesitation, he issued commands and gathered a select group of elite members to descend into the Dungeon, their goal clear.
Deal with the threat and subdue the chaos caused by the unnatural eruption of divine power.
— — —
Astraea Familia – Stardust Garden
In the tranquil hall, Astraea opened her eyes. Her calm but firm voice echoed throughout the chamber, instantly silencing the conversations of her followers.
"Alise. A god has released their divinity on the twelfth floor. Akira is likely still inside—possibly caught in the aftermath. I need the four of you to descend immediately."
She gestured to her most dependable warriors and said, "The others will continue patrolling Orario to ensure there are no further surprise attacks from Evilus. I trust you understand the weight of this."
"Yes, Astraea-sama!"
Alise, Kaguya, Ryuu and Lyra replied in unison, their voices ringing with determination and discipline.
— — —
Amidst the chaos, Akira made a decision. Given the current situation, there was no point in hesitation.
He needed to eliminate Thanatos first—then he could handle the mutated dragon-like beast.
However, Thanatos—always an astute observer—seemed to read his mind. A sly smile spread across his face.
"Are you sure you want to waste your precious time with me, boy?" He asked with mocking amusement.
"You should know better than anyone—those other adventurers don't have your strength. One misstep and they'll be slaughtered by that thing."
As if to further taunt him, Thanatos pulled out a shimmering silver-white orb, likely a magic tool, and turned to walk deeper into the caverns.
Two silent followers flanked him—well-trained and familiar with Thanatos' methods.
"Come, oh heroes of justice." Thanatos said with an exaggerated bow, his voice oozing with sarcastic grandeur.
Akira clicked his tongue in annoyance. In the next moment, he changed to Swift Master. A sharp wind blade streaked through the air, slashing toward the retreating god as Akira rocketed after the wyvern with deadly intent.
Thanatos flinched as the blade grazed his arm, drawing blood. Watching Akira's figure fade into the distance, he cradled his wounded arm and let out a faint sigh.
"What a petty child…"
"RROOOOOAAAARRR!!!"
A deafening, bestial roar reverberated across the twelfth floor like a massive gong.
The few adventurers still huddled near the entrance instinctively cowered at the monstrous presence that approached.
A creature emerged from the mist—a draconic behemoth nearly six meters long.
Its pale red skin was barely visible beneath hardened dark scales that shimmered with an unnatural luster. Its sheer aura exuded a sense of overwhelming oppression.
A mutated enhanced species. One that had clearly been corrupted by divine influence.
It hovered in mid-air, its eyes glowing blood-red as they scanned the area, locking onto traces of residual divine power. Its mouth opened wide, revealing rows of jagged teeth, and within, a fiery core began to glow.
It was preparing to launch a devastating fireball toward the location where Thanatos had just been.
But in that instant, a spinning tornado slammed into its skull from above.
Akira, who had teleported to the ceiling to conceal his presence, had launched the attack before the Black wyvern even noticed.
The tornado violently knocked the beast to the ground, creating a massive crater as it crashed.
As the Black Wyvern thrashed and attempted to rise, two slicing wind blades cleaved its back, eliciting pained screeches from its twisted throat.
Snarling in fury, the Black Wyvern anchored itself to the ground with it's clawed feet, then unleashed a torrent of searing flame from its gaping maw.
Akira hovered in mid-air, his entire form wrapped in howling wind. Drawing deeply upon his magical reserves, he summoned wind magic into his palms—refined, compressed, and explosive.
The winds erupted forward, a surging storm that met the Black Wyvern's inferno head-on.ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
For a moment, it was a struggle of pure elemental force—fire against storm.
The Black Wyvern's neck bulged, straining to unleash its entire fiery arsenal. But Akira's magic was relentless.
Little by little, the roaring storm pushed back the flames. The Black Wyvern's expression contorted in desperation as its fire faltered, and finally—was smothered.
The wind storm swept through the monster's body. Its scales were peeled away by the magic's fury, exposing its wounded, blood-red hide beneath. Half its face was destroyed, revealing the bone and flesh inside. Its wings hung limp, shredded and broken.
In one final motion, Akira darted forward and drove a storm-infused punch into its chest. The concentrated gale penetrated deep, tearing open its torso and revealing the shimmering magic stone inside.
Simultaneously, Akira's palms absorbed the remnants of its blood—an effect he did not yet fully understand.
He exhaled heavily, taking a moment to rest.
"I should be able to finish that thing in a few minutes." He muttered to himself.
"No one should have seen me…"
Stuffing the magic stone into his [Backpack], he turned toward the exit with quiet haste.
And in his heart, he made a solemn vow. "Tomorrow… I'm staying at the base the whole day. Nobody's stopping me."
With a thunderous boom, the exit to the upper floors burst open. Akira, now wearing his hood, blended into the crowd of adventurers preparing to leave.
But he hadn't escaped unnoticed.
Standing at the forefront were Alise and her team—joined by members of the Loki Familia. They were already busy calming frightened adventurers.
Spotting him, Alise's eyes lit up, and she waved enthusiastically. Akira, ever silent, quietly moved to stand beside Ryuu.
Finn, standing before a group of survivors, addressed them with calm authority, "So all of you saw an adventurer, his body engulfed in wind, defeat the monster. Is there anything else you can tell me?"
"I'm sorry, Captain Finn… they were fighting far away, and the white fog made it impossible to see clearly." One adventurer replied apologetically.
Finn gave a brief nod and said, "Understood. Please return to the surface. You've done well."
Returning to his companions, Finn let out a sigh and shrugged.
"Well… looks like someone beat us to it. And here I was hoping to deal with it swiftly. I even brought Riveria and Gareth along. Guess we were just extras this time."
Riveria narrowed her eyes, scanning the battlefield with her staff in hand.
She said, "It's good there were no casualties. Did we find out anything else?"
"Only that a wind-shrouded figure did all the work." Finn said.
The trio turned their gaze toward Ais—who had slowly drifted toward Akira, a dreamy expression on her face.
Riveria sighed, pinching the bridge of her nose.
She said, "It's not Ais. She was with me all day. Probably just someone who uses similar magic."
Soon after, Alise approached with her team and greeted Finn, "Finn, is everything under control?"
Finn nodded and glanced at the young half-elf boy standing beside Ryuu.
"This is the new recruit of the Astraea Familia, right? Reached the twelfth floor already… impressive."
He had already spotted Akira earlier and, recalling Raul's previous reports, made the connection.
Akira stepped forward and extended a hand. "Hello, Captain Finn. I've heard a lot about you. I'm Akira."
"Finn Deimne." Finn said, shaking his hand firmly.
"Goddess Astraea hasn't taken in new blood for a long time. Earning her trust means you've got a strong sense of justice."
Akira smiled modestly and said, "I'm very thankful she accepted me."
"Alright, that's enough introductions." Riveria interrupted, waving her staff.
"This is still the Dungeon. Not the place for a meet-and-greet."
Kaguya and Gareth nodded in agreement.
Alise, energetic as ever, thrust her hand into the air. "Don't worry! As a girl of justice, I'll protect you as long as you want to chat!"
"Huh? What are you even saying?" Riveria glared at her.
"Ahaha, sorry, Riveria!" Alise laughed sheepishly, not even bothering to hide her cheerfulness.
Kaguya smacked her on the head, while Lyra slapped her butt.
"Apologies. Our captain gets a little too enthusiastic sometimes." Lyra said.
"We'll keep her in line."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 38 - 38: Level Up
chapters.content:
Akira, accompanied by his companions, walked alongside Ais and her comrades as they returned together to the base, their steps light yet steady.
"So Akira already made it to the middle floors on his own? That's truly impressive." Finn remarked, genuinely taken aback after learning Akira had come up from the deeper floors.
"Yeah, no kidding. At his age, I was still bumming around in the upper floors." Gareth let out a hearty laugh, stroking his beard.
At that moment, Alise wrapped her arms tightly around Akira from behind, rubbing her cheek against his and beaming with pride.New ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄhapters are published on novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
She happily said, "Hehe~ Akira's a prodigy I picked up in Orario! Under this captain's rigorous training, he's going to become our familia's ultimate trump card!"
As if carried away by her own enthusiasm, she began spinning in circles with Akira still in her arms, laughing brightly like a child showing off her prize.
When she finally came to a halt, dizzy but delighted, Akira calmly placed his hands on either side of Alise's flushed face and leaned in, the tips of their noses nearly touching.
He said, "Captain… could you please put me down?"
His gaze was steady, his breath brushing her cheek.
Alise froze, her eyes wide, then she quickly yelped, "S-Sorry, ahahaha!"
Then, she scurried forward to walk ahead of the group, her red ears poking out from beneath her hair.
Seeing this, Akira's lips curled into a quiet smile.
While Finn and the others remained focused on the journey, Kaguya and Lyra glanced at each other knowingly, having noticed Alise's unusual behavior.
Meanwhile, only Ryuu remained steadfast, silently inspecting Akira's body for any hidden injuries.
"Good grief! Hugging each other in public like that… have you no shame, you airheaded captain!?" Kaguya dramatically embraced Alise from behind, making sure everyone could hear.
Then, she whispered slyly into her ear, "You actually blushed."
Lyra joined in with a playful grin, nudging Alise in the ribs with her elbow. "Wow~ Usually you've got the skin of a rhino, but one look from Akira and you're pink as a peach. What gives?"
Alise faltered for a second, fidgeting with the hem of her clothes before finally mumbling, "W-Well… his face was so close… We almost kissed…"
As the girls in front whispered in flustered tones, the conversation in the rear shifted toward graver matters.
"Akira." Finn called out directly, his tone laced with curiosity.
"The divine-powered monster… you were the one who defeated it, weren't you?"
"Mm, yeah." Akira replied casually, his eyes still resting on the flustered trio ahead. "I did."
Finn blinked at his directnessand asked, "Then… did you meet a god in a black robe with purple hair? Did he say anything?"
Akira nodded and said, "He talked a lot of crap. But his goal was clear—he wanted me to join his familia. Said I had the potential to be a valuable piece in their twisted little game."
"So it's just like with Ais..." Riveria murmured, recalling the eerily similar encounter from before.
"But why?" Finn muttered, thoughtful.
"Why did he release his power now? Last time he did, the industrial district was hit at the same time…"
At those words, something clicked in Akira's mind.
He raised his hand and replied matter-of-factly, "Ah, that might be my fault. I was planning to weaken Evilus and maybe… send that god back to heaven permanently."
The entire group came to a dead stop. Even Alise and the girls up front stopped whispering and turned back to stare at Akira in disbelief.
Seeing everyone's expression, Akira simply shrugged and let out a breath. "Unfortunately, I failed."
Finn stared at him, his expression somewhere between admiration and bewilderment.
He said, "It's already astonishing that you even had that idea, let alone acted on it."
Before Akira could respond, Kaguya and Ryuu grabbed him by the head simultaneously, each examining him like inspecting a rare specimen.
"My head's fine, you know…" Akira sighed, utterly resigned.
Riveria stepped forward, arms crossed, her brows furrowed.
She asked, "Are you really one of us? I knew the people from my homeland were obsessed with learning, but even they wouldn't go this far."
Lyu stepped forward anxiously, her voice laced with concern. "Akira, that kind of ambition is dangerous."
Only two voices sounded out with unfiltered admiration.
"Akira, you're incredible." Ais said earnestly.
"Haha! If you're aiming that high, kid, you might just surpass us all someday!" Gareth added with a bellow of laughter.
Thwack!
Riveria smacked Ais on the head with a swift hand chop and said, "You are absolutely forbidden from adopting that kind of thinking! I can tolerate your disregard for Loki, but show some respect for the gods. That includes you too, Akira."
Finn finally stepped in to ease the tension. "Alright, alright. The important thing is that no one got hurt. Akira only acted with the intention of protecting peace."
"Hahaha, that's my member alright! You even dared to judge a god!" Alise announced proudly, puffing her chest out.
Lyra groaned. "Don't make this worse than it already is..."
— — —
Inside Astraea's private quarters, word had already spread among the familia that Akira had slain a divine-powered enhanced species. Everyone was eager to see how much his stats had improved.
As they gathered around, Astraea pricked her finger, allowing a single drop of divine blood to fall onto Akira's back. Sacred text glimmered into view.

Astraea gazed at his back in silence, thoughts swirling in her mind.
She asked, "Akira, before slaying that black wyvern… did you by chance descend to the 17th floor to challenge Goliath?"
That question made Akira freeze. He blinked, wide-eyed.
"Wait—how did you know?! I haven't even told anyone yet!"
Sighing, Akira scratched his head and said, "Well… yeah. I fell to the 17th floor during a collapse. I thought about heading to the 18th floor for a breather, but well—Goliath happened to respawn right then."
He puffed out his cheeks, aggrieved. "So I had to take care of it first..."
Alise and the others watching him speak couldn't help but wince in sympathy. Even Astraea sighed, exasperated.
With your speed, escaping Goliath should've been easy...
Still, after she finished transcribing the stats onto a parchment, the parchment was passed around silently.
One by one, shocked expressions overtook the faces of the familia members, followed by loud exclamations from the hallway. The sheer jump in stats was enough to shake the foundation of their understanding.
Astraea then spoke again, her expression bright, "Akira, your feats today were great. Your abilities have evolved, your achievements legendary. So, tell me—are you ready to rank up?"
Akira's eyes gleamed. "Yes. I am."
[T/N: Why didn't he go to SSS 1999 OR 2999 OR EX 9999 or whatever? The same reason Bell didn't.]
Astraea smiled gently and said, "Then let's begin."
As Akira lied down, Astraea's hand moved gracefully, divine blood tracing the falna with glowing radiance. The touch tickled slightly, but he welcomed the sensation.
''From today onward, I am a Level 2 adventurer. In the battles to come… my power to protect others will grow stronger than ever.'
"Akira." Astraea whispered, her voice bringing him back to the moment.
"The level up is complete. You can now choose a development ability. Choose wisely."

chapters.title: Chapter 39 - 39: Development Ability
chapters.content:
In addition to basic stats, magic, and skills, a unique set of options known as development abilities may manifest upon leveling up—keyword being may.
These development abilities are not fixed like the 5 stats, but instead change depending on an adventurer's actions and performance. They are additional, acquired abilities gained through practical experience and relentless effort.
For example, adventurers who slay a great number of monsters in a short period might be granted [Hunter], while those who frequently heal and support allies may get [Healer].
In a way, development abilities serve as a reflection of the adventurer's path—a unique signature of their journey and growth.
Although development abilities don't offer the immediate, overwhelming power of magic or skills, many of them are nothing short of extraordinary.
Some adventurers, those with exceptional aptitude and who consistently walk the edge of life and death, may even unlock rare and unique abilities far beyond the norm.
Standing beside Akira, Astraea began listing the possible development abilities, naming them one by one as if she were reading a sacred scripture—or announcing a banquet of blessings.
"Let's see… First, there's [Hunter]—"
[Hunter] is granted only when one slays a vast number of monsters within a short timeframe. It can only be acquired upon reaching LV 2 and enhances combat effectiveness against monsters.
"Then there's [Mage]—"
This development ability generates a magic circle beneath the adventurer, significantly enhancing their magic's potency, expanding the range of effect, and increasing mind efficiency. It even boosts their magic stat as if they had ascended another level.
"[Abnormal Resistance]—"
As the name implies, it theoretically grants resistance to status effects like poison, charm, and dizziness. In early stages, it can be obtained by frequently being exposed to the venom of purple moths.
Of course, it's not as good as it sounds. In truth, this often only succeeds to resist poison and fails against other abnormal conditions.
"And then, the rarest among them… [Mystery]!"
[Mystery]—a development ability so rare and valuable that its appearance is recorded only in fragments of public knowledge.
It grants the ability to create miracles and craft powerful magic items.
One of its applications is the creation of the legendary Status Thief, brewed using a god's blood. With it, one can view someone's status. Only those possessing [Mystery] can craft such an item.
Furthermore, [Mystery] can amplify the effects of other development abilities or synchronize them in unique ways.
For instance, both [Mystery] and [Mage] are prerequisites for creating Grimoires used to awaken magic.
Even within all of Orario, the number of adventurers who possess [Mystery] can be counted on one hand.
Suddenly, Astraea tilted her head and raised an eyebrow. "Wait, what is this one… [Integration]?"
Her voice was tinged with curiosity. "This… this isn't in any of the lower world's records. Akira, what do you think it means?"
Akira pondered for a moment, then said thoughtfully, "Judging from the name… perhaps it refers to the unification of all forces?"
He paused, then added, "It might mean that in that special state—my Element Blaster form—I could use all powers in harmony, even magic."
Astraea nodded in agreement and said, "Yes… that does seem to be the essence of it. I can sense that much."
It was undoubtedly a powerful and fitting ability for Akira. But Astraea was not one of those controlling gods who forced her will upon her children. She would never treat her children like mere tools.
Instead, she offered the choice freely, "Then, Akira, it seems you'll have to decide between [Mystery] and [Integration]. No matter what, I'll support you."
Without hesitation, Akira replied firmly, "Astraea-sama, I choose [Mystery]."
It was the most practical ability for him—one that would enable him to craft items, artifacts, and protective equipment for Alise and the others, to safeguard them in times of peril.
He would use the knowledge and power he had gained as a Dimension Walker to forge tools of protection.
As for [Integration], it wasn't necessary—at least, not yet. There would come a time when he would gain the ability to command all sub-classes and wield them in unison. He had that feeling. For now, this power was more than enough.
Astraea, seeing the clarity in his eyes, said no more. She simply smiled and began completing the final step of the rank up.
"Very well. I understand."
"It's done."
A warm glow suffused Akira's body. Power rose from within him.
