chapters.title: Chapter 57 - 57: Akira VS Green Dragon
chapters.content:
Now, Ais was no longer the silent "Puppet Princess" who only cared about hunting monsters.
A subtle change had taken place. She had begun to show glimpses of her more youthful, innocent side.
More importantly, after spending so much time with Akira, it seemed that his carefree, unrestrained personality had begun to rub off on her.
The days they spent together were no longer just intense training sessions or battles—they were slowly becoming filled with small, unexpected moments of joy.
Ais puffed out her cheeks slightly and shot Akira a discontented look. "Akira is just like Riveria. Always nagging. It's annoying."
Akira reached out and gently poked her soft cheek, teasing, "Oh? Has Ais finally grown tired of adventuring with me? What a tragedy."
Understanding his teasing tone, Ais responded in kind. She reached out, caught Akira's fingers with her own, and gave him a mock frown.
"Yes, Akira is still too weak. I think it's time I abandon you... and go adventure with Gareth instead."
With that, she swung their clasped hands back and forth playfully, her eyes scanning the dim expanse of the 24th floor, searching for signs of powerful monsters. Her Desperate gleamed faintly in the dungeon's unnatural light.
"Huff—"
A sudden, heavy breath of air interrupted the moment.
Akira swiftly pulled Ais beneath a thick-rooted tree, crouching low with alert eyes.
Peeking out carefully, he spotted a massive green dragon not far away. It had leathery wings, a sharp horn protruding from its head, and a body roughly the size of the Infant dragon they'd once faced on the 18th floor.
"That must be it... the green dragon, the apex predator of the 24th floor." Akira muttered under his breath.
"And if I'm not wrong, it's also the guardian of the treasure tree that holds rare materials."
He quickly relayed this information to Ais, matching the creature's features with everything he'd read in the Guild's monster records.
Holding her Desperate, Ais narrowed her eyes and asked in a low voice, "Are you going to fight it? If so, Akira, finish it quickly."
Over the past few days, he had watched Ais fight countless monsters with overwhelming ease.
This green dragon might be formidable, but with Ais's abilities and especially her innate skill that increased damage against dragon-type monsters, she would likely make quick work of it.
However, Akira had a different thought. He unsheathed his one-handed sword and glanced at Ais.
He said, "Let me handle this one. May I?"
Ais gave a quiet nod, obedient and trusting. "If things get dangerous, I'll help you right away."
"Then just watch for a bit. I'll be back before you know it."
Smiling, Akira gently patted her head before stepping out from under the tree's cover.
"RRAAAOOOHHH—!!"
The green dragon immediately sensed the intruder. With a thunderous roar, it flapped its disproportionately small but surprisingly powerful wings, lifting its massive body into the air with ease.
Despite its size, the green dragon was swift and deadly. With potential nearing that of a Level 4 adventurer, its thick scales, razor fangs, and aerial mobility made it a nightmare for most. It wasn't something a mid-tier adventurer could handle lightly.
The beast dove at him, its maw wide open, filled with fangs that looked ready to crush steel. But Akira twisted his body and dodged nimbly, avoiding the attack by a hair's breadth.
He swung his sword upward in retaliation—but the dragon wasn't slow.
It flapped its wings sharply, avoiding the blow with shocking agility, and countered by sweeping its colossal tail in a wide arc toward Akira.
Akira's eyes glinted. Using the thick bark of a nearby tree, he vaulted upward, twisting in the air to avoid the tail. Landing deftly on a high branch, he regained his balance in an instant.
Boom!
The tail slammed into the ground where he'd stood moments ago, reducing several trees to splinters.
Seeing its attack fail, the green dragon snarled and twisted mid-air, preparing for another charge.
But Akira was ready. He crouched, bent the branch beneath his feet, and used its tension to launch himself forward like an arrow released from a bow.
Bang!
While in flight, he slashed at the monster's wing, precisely targeting a weak point in the membrane. The edge of his blade tore through it.
"RAAAAAHH!!"
The green dragon let out a bloodcurdling cry as it lost balance, its wings faltering. It spiraled and crashed to the ground.
But even when injured, this monster wasn't easy prey. With a swift roll, it landed on all fours and snarled with fury, eyes glowing with killing intent.
Akira landed a few meters away, wasting no time. He darted forward, weaving through gnarled roots and shattered trunks, evading the snapping jaws and claws of the monsters.
Then—
His sword flashed.
He slashed across the green dragon's face, and the blade slipped between its thick scales, drawing blood.
In one fluid motion, he vaulted upward, drove his sword into its hide to steady himself, and sprinted across it's back like a gymnast.
As the green dragon twisted to throw him off, Akira leapt again. The white gleam of his blade became a streak as he aimed straight for its head.
Shlunk!
With precision, he drove the blade into the side of the green dragon's skull, twisted, and—
Crack!
It's neck jerked violently. With a final thrash, the head detached, its body collapsing as it gave a final gurgling roar.
Thud!
The green dragon's severed head hit the ground.
Panting slightly, Akira stood atop the corpse. It was over.Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
Without pause, he dug out the monster's magic stone, broke off the horn, and harvested several pristine scales.
Seeing the fight conclude, Ais stepped out from behind the tree and walked over to Akira's side, her expression calm but her eyes shining with pride.
"I recall there's usually a treasure tree growing near green dragons." Akira remarked as he looked around.
"Do you see anything?"
Ais didn't answer immediately. Instead, she walked over to a seemingly ordinary tree, observed it closely, muttered a brief chant, then leapt gracefully onto its branches.
Akira followed her gaze upward and saw it.
Clustered high above, nestled between thick foliage, were glimmering fruits that looked like they were carved from red and blue sapphires. Sparkling in the dim light, they looked like treasures from a fairy tale.
Akira scratched his head and laughed. "Honestly, I thought they'd be hidden in tree hollows like in those old RPGs. I didn't expect it to be this... literal."
As Ais sliced off the branches holding the gem-like fruits, Akira couldn't help but marvel at her ease.
"You're amazing, Ais. Did you use a special method to find it?" He asked as he took one of the shimmering fruits from her hand.
Ais pointed at the trunk of the tree, her expression tinged with subtle pride.
She said, "This tree doesn't have any claw marks. Also, it gives off a distinct scent."
Akira looked at her fondly and said, "Is that so? As expected of a Level 3 adventurer—your experience really shows."

chapters.title: Chapter 58 - 58: Changes in Ais and Akira's Status
chapters.content:
Upon arriving at the guild hall, Akira casually slung his backpack off his shoulder and walked toward the reception counter.
Without hesitation, he retrieved the collected magic stones and monster materials. Then, he carefully distributed them according to his and Ais's efforts and handed them to the guild staff for conversion into Valis.
After a quick calculation, the staff returned the exchange with two neatly packed bags of Valis.
Akira glanced at the heavier pouch and, without needing to think twice, handed it over to Ais.
"You should take the larger share." He said with a faint smile.
"You did more of the work today. I was mostly letting you practice and watching your back."
Ais blinked, her expression calm but eyes flickering with a hint of warmth. She didn't refuse, simply accepted the bag with a slight nod, as was her way.
Before they parted ways, Akira made a small detour to a familiar stall nestled in the busy plaza—one known for its fried potato balls.
He ordered the red bean cream flavor, Ais's favorite without question. Watching her quietly nibble on them with a rare hint of joy in her expression was more than enough reward.
When they reached the gates of the Loki Familia's estate, Akira waved goodbye, watching as Ais turned and disappeared behind the gates. Only after she was gone did he begin his quiet walk home.
Meanwhile, Ais returned to her quarters and began the post-adventure routine. She removed her armor and Desperate, placing them carefully on the rack. Without delay, she walked to the girls' shower room, her steps silent and unhurried.
The sound of water and steam filled the chamber. Ais washed away the dust and blood of the Dungeon. Her golden hair, now loose, clung to her back and shoulders like threads of sunlight.
Just as she was about to wrap herself in a towel and step out, something unexpected happened.
A splash.
Then—wham!
A figure burst out of the tub like a sea monster ambushing prey and latched onto Ais.
"Let me see if Ais-tan has grown! Come on, let me touch you!"
Loki's perverted, sparkly-eyed face lunged forward like a lecherous ghost from the mist, her fingers wriggling ominously.
Ais, completely unfazed, leaned slightly to the side, dodging Loki's grab with practiced ease.
"…Loki."
She said flatly, her tone carrying the weight of pure disapproval as she evaded another attempt with minimal effort.
"Ufufu~! I just love this cold attitude!" Loki squealed, undeterred as always.
Dressing quickly, Ais ignored her antics and voiced her intent, "Loki, I want to update my status."
Loki's eyes sparkled like twin stars. "Oh ho~? Alright, come with me, my adorable ice princess!"
…
Inside Loki's private room, Ais sat quietly with her back exposed, her smooth skin illuminated by the warm lamplight.
Loki pricked her finger, letting a drop of divine blood fall onto Ais's back. The divine Falna began to shimmer.
As numbers and runes danced before Loki's eyes, she hummed at first, noting the steady growth in stats.
But then—she froze.
"…Oh?"
Her expression twisted into one of stunned surprise.
"What do we have here? A brand-new skill?"
Hearing those words, Ais's calm facade cracked slightly. She turned quickly, excitement flashing in her usually serene golden eyes.
"What kind of skill? Tell me, Loki!"
With an exaggerated chuckle, Loki held up the parchment and said, "It's your lucky day. Here, take a look yourself."
Ais's fingers trembled ever so slightly as she accepted the sheet. Her gaze darted to the familiar but always hopeful section.
Ais Wallenstein
LV 3
[Magic]
Ariel
[Skills]
Avenger
Wind Master
-Enhances wind magic while enhanced by Ariel. Increases range, control, and damage amplification.
Her heart swelled with joy. Finally, after two years of stagnation—when only her stats had grown—there was real progress.
A new skill. A tangible sign that she was still evolving. That her limits hadn't been reached.
The thought of Akira surfaced in her mind.
She clenched the parchment and whispered to herself, "This is because of him… because of training and learning alongside him."
"I need to tell Riveria!" She said, rising to her feet with determination.
Loki chuckled and gestured. "She's in the office right now, probably sipping tea with Finn and Gareth. Let's go."
…Tʜe sourcᴇ of thɪs content ɪs Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
When Ais shared the news in the office, the three high-ranking members of Loki Familia offered their congratulations without hesitation.
Riveria smiled, a rare softness in her eyes. "It seems your efforts in practicing magic with Akira have borne fruit. You should thank him properly, Ais."
Loki, never one to stay quiet, waved a hand. "Nonsense! This is all because our little Ais is just naturally amazing. What does that brat have to do with it?"
"He's helped a lot." Ais muttered, puffing her cheeks slightly.
"And I'm not stupid, Loki."
"Eeeh~? I never said you were!"
Loki threw up her hands in mock surrender, laughing as Gareth and Finn exchanged amused glances.
…
Elsewhere, inside the quiet halls of the Astraea Familia manor, Akira stood still as the divine presence behind him came to a halt.
"What's wrong, Astraea-sama?" He asked, blinking in confusion.
Astraea narrowed her star-like eyes and held up the newly updated parchment. "Akira… your status changed again."
Akira raised a brow. "Another change?"
She handed the sheet to him.
Akira
LV 2
Strength: I0 → F312
Durability: I0 → F305
Dexterity: I0 → F334
Agility: I0 → F324
Magic: I0 → D509
Development Ability: Mystery I
[Magic]
Element Control
Blood Magic
Dimensional Erosion
- A type of dimensional magic. Under certain conditions, magic power can be transformed into dimensional power to unleash specialized effects.
"It's probably recorded because of the power you used when activating your Dimension Walker abilities." Astraea murmured.
She circled Akira, tapping her chin. "This magic is dangerous, no doubt. But also... fascinating. Is this the secret behind how you create magical artifacts?"
Akira scratched his head and said, "More or less. Without this, I wouldn't have gotten far in enchanting."
Astraea's eyes twinkled mischievously and she said, "So… it says 'under certain conditions.' Meaning you have a transformation, don't you? A new form."
She leaned in closer, voice soft and coaxing, "Come on~ Let me see it. Just once."
Akira flinched and said, "You're not going to laugh, are you?"
Astraea crossed her hands dramatically and said, "Astraea, the purest of deities, swears upon the stars!"
"…Alright, fine."
The moment he allowed the transformation to begin, his body began to subtly shift.
Though still youthful, Akira's appearance now held an ethereal neutrality. His features refined into something androgynous, delicate, like an elven noble—eerily reminiscent of Celty.
Dark circles appeared beneath his eyes, unearned yet persistent, giving him a tired and almost melancholy aura.
But what disturbed him most was the sensation… that ever-familiar feeling of being watched—a gaze brimming with hostility, jealousy, and something else he couldn't place.
It was like being accused of a crime he didn't commit—like a man caught cheating.
He knew that the gaze belonged to that guy but what he couldn't understand was why he was being targeted.

chapters.title: Chapter 59 - 59: Akira's Alias, Harem Prince?
chapters.content:
"Haha, so this is your new look? You look really cute, but those dark circles under your eyes are far too heavy."
Astraea chuckled softly, her delicate fingers brushing gently against the tired skin beneath Akira's eyes. Her laughter was light, but the concern in her voice was genuine.
Akira let out a sigh, his expression a mix of resignation and annoyance.
He said, "Yeah… that's why I don't like using this form. It really does look like I've been pulling all-nighters every day. Even worse, it's not just about looks."
"The longer I stay in this state, the more I start to feel like my sanity is… slipping. Sometimes, I can even hear strange whispers—like voices murmuring just beyond comprehension."
With a faint shimmer of magic power, his form reverted back into his standard Elemental Blaster appearance.
The unnatural aura and dark circles vanished, and once again, he looked like the usual bright, determined boy everyone knew. The strange, oppressive line of sight that always seemed to follow him when he was in that form was gone.
Astraea tilted her head and smiled. "Oh right, that reminds me. Akira, are you planning to give yourself an alias soon?"
Akira blinked in confusion and asked, "Alias?"
Astraea leaned in, her smile turning sly. She said, "Denatus is coming up. It's not just about politics, you know. Everyone loves showing off their 'children.' And your achievements will definitely draw attention. If you don't choose an alias for yourself, my fellow gods will happily make one up for you. And trust me… you won't like it."Google seaʀᴄh N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
Akira froze. His mouth twitched, and his gaze shifted to the side. "…Do I have to pick an alias?"
He scratched his head helplessly, muttering, "If I had to come up with something, it'd just be lame names like 'Elementalist,' 'Blood Mage,' or 'Swift Master.'"
His shoulders slumped as he said, "All just literal descriptions from my magic list. I'm terrible at naming things…"
Astraea stifled a giggle behind her hand and said, "I figured as much. It sounds like you just pulled them directly from your status sheet."
"Exactly!" Akira gave her a defeated look.
"So please, Astraea-sama, I'm counting on you to help me out here. Even if it's something like 'Sword of Justice,' 'Right Hand of Justice,' or even 'Rookie of Justice,' I'll accept it. Anything's better than… that."
He suddenly turned pale as he continued, "Just please—don't let them call me something ridiculous like 'Justice Freak,' 'Harem Prince,' or 'Clown of Orario'…"
With a warm smile, Astraea reached out and ruffled Akira's hair, then raised a fist solemnly with her other hand.
She said, "Don't worry. As your goddess, I swear I'll fight tooth and nail to make sure you get a decent, dignified alias."
Akira groaned dramatically, "I'm begging you, Astraea-sama! I want something cool, like the ones Alise and the others have!"
His exaggerated plea drew a soft laugh from Astraea, who couldn't help but find his sincerity adorable.
Later that night, back in his room, Akira opened the [Personal Information] tab and reviewed his current growth.
[Personal Information]
Name: Akira
Age: 13
Level: 32
"…Still just two levels gained over several days." Akira muttered as he stared.
"The higher I go, the more experience it takes… and the monsters aren't making it easy either."
His eyes shifted to the corner of his room, where a pile of broken one-handed swords was stacked. The sight made him wince.
"I really need to get a better weapon. One that won't break after just a few battles…"
He lay on his bed and covered his eyes with an arm, his mind drifting between thoughts of crafting, dungeon runs, and alias selection. Before long, sleep took him.
— — —
The Next Morning.
When Akira arrived at the gate of the Loki Familia's estate, the guard informed him that Ais had already been dragged off by Loki for something urgent. Apparently, Riveria had sent word in advance to let Akira know.
"Looks like I'm soloing the dungeon today," Akira muttered, glancing up at the Tower of Babel that loomed in the distance.
"Well, that's fine. I've got a lot to catch up on…"
But before diving into the depths of the dungeon, there was something he had to take care of.
— — —
Orario's second district—the Industrial Zone—was alive with noise and movement.
The clatter of machinery, the hiss of steam, and the rhythmic thudding of hammers formed a chaotic symphony.
Laborers in simple work garb, both human and demi-human, bustled through the streets, moving heavy materials and managing construction projects.
Everywhere he looked, buildings rose skyward, mechanical limbs turned gears, and the air itself smelled of molten metal and coal dust.
This zone wasn't known for comfort or elegance. It was where progress was forged—literally and metaphorically. And today, Akira was here for a purpose.
"Daedalus Street… if I remember right, there should be a Hephaestus workshop near here." He murmured.
Turning a corner, Akira found what he was looking for.
In front of him stood a workshop that, while built in the same blocky industrial style as its neighbors, bore a distinctive symbol above its door—the blazing hammer insignia of Hephaestus Familia.
"This must be the place."
With a sack of high-grade monster materials slung over his shoulder, Akira stepped inside.
The scent of burning coal hit him immediately, and the sound of metal striking metal echoed from deep within. A rhythm of labor, loud and constant.
The workshop was dimly lit, with only thin rays of sunlight filtering through the soot-streaked windows. The magic stone lamps hadn't been activated, but the roaring forge in the back filled the room with flickering light and heat.
He walked toward the sound of hammering—and there, standing at the anvil, was a striking figure.
A tall, tanned woman stood before the forge. Her long black hair was tied up in a practical bun. She wore a red hakama that fell just above her ankles and a tightly wrapped white cloth around her upper body.
Sweat glistened on her skin, but she didn't pause in her work for even a second.
A black eyepatch covered one of her eyes, giving her a rough, intimidating look—but there was an undeniable strength and beauty to her presence.
Every swing of her hammer radiated skill and experience. With each strike, sparks flew and a soft glow pulsed from the red-hot metal she was shaping.
[Blacksmith], a rare development ability.
Through sheer effort and technique, she imbued the metal with a spiritual energy that elevated its quality—almost akin to the divine grace of a Falna.
With a final clang, she brought the hammer down hard. The red block glowed, then slowly dimmed as the energy settled into it.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 60 - 60: Customized Equipment
chapters.content:
"What are you here for?"
The rhythmic clanging of hammer against steel halted.
The tall, toned woman—rumored to be a half-dwarf from the Far East—turned slowly.
Her sharp, chiseled features and bronze-toned skin glistened with sweat. Her single visible eye, unhidden beneath a black eyepatch, scrutinized Akira curiously.
Despite her well-known status as a blacksmith, this woman was far more than a forge-dweller.
Tsubaki Collbrande, the famed blacksmith of the Hephaestus Familia, was also a Level 5 adventurer—someone who personally tested her weapons in the depths of the dungeon before deeming them worthy.
A powerhouse with calloused hands and unmatched strength, whispered to be the most powerful blacksmith in all of Orario.
"Excuse me."
Akira stepped forward respectfully, dropping a bulging sack of monster materials onto a nearby bench with a dull thud.
"Can I customize weapons here?"
The sack split slightly as it landed, revealing a massive green dragon horn, the size of a full-grown man's torso, along with scales, claws, and other valuable materials.
Tsubaki raised an eyebrow and said, "Hoh? Custom weapons, huh? You don't look familiar. Are you a new recruit? A low-level adventurer?"
Her gaze lingered on the dragon horn, more intrigued by the haul than the person at first glance.
Akira scratched his cheek and replied earnestly, "No, I've already leveled up to Level 2. I'm Akira, from the Astraea Familia."
For a moment, Tsubaki was silent. Then her expression lit up as she slapped her chest.
She said, "Why didn't you say so earlier?! I'll take the commission!"
With a booming laugh, she added, "I'm Tsubaki Collbrande, head blacksmith of the Hephaestus Familia and its captain. Just call me Tsubaki."
She paused, then squinted. "Wait a sec... Is there someone named Akira in Astraea's Familia? I thought they were mostly female..."
As if realizing her mistake, she added, "Sorry, I don't keep up with the latest gossip. I usually stay in my forge, working on equipments so I don't know what goes on in the outside world."
The cloth wrapped on her upper body clung to her skin due to sweat, making her cleavage prominent.
In theory, she should've been seductive but her laid-back, almost unkempt personality strangely neutralized the allure. If anything, she gave off more of a boisterous Amazonian vibe than that of a sensual half-dwarf.
Tsubaki picked up the broken one-handed sword Akira had brought along. Her practiced eyes scanned it from hilt to tip.
"Crude. Just a fine sword, but poorly maintained." She said bluntly.
"The edge is chipped, the tip's flattened, and these tiny fractures—magic damage. You've been using this thing carelessly."
As a skilled blacksmith that's been in the business for years, Tsubaki could easily tell from these clues that the adventurer in front of her had a general fighting habit and was the type who didn't care about the damage to their weapon when fighting.
Akira gave a dry chuckle, rubbing the back of his neck.
She added with a grin, "Forget it, it's your luck that you ran into me today. So, what kind of weapon and armor are you thinking?"
He glanced away awkwardly as her laugh jiggled... well, everything.
That casual laugh, combined with the way sweat trickled down her throat, gave her a wild, primal sort of charm. Her powerful physique rivaled even the goddesses in allure.
"A one-handed sword would be best. Durable. As for armor, something light—scaled vambraces should work." Akira responded, keeping his eyes level.
Tsubaki nodded, kneeling to inspect the materials.
"Hmm... this horn... green dragon, huh? Not bad at all. Did you take it down yourself?"
"Yes." Akira replied, lifting the damaged sword in confirmation.
"Solid work."
Tsubaki rose to her feet and strode into the back room, muttering, "Pity I'm running low on high-grade steel again... Guess we'll need that super-hard stuff."
The steel mined from the deeper dungeon layers was known to surpass other materials in purity and resilience. Depending on the floor, its grade could vary drastically.
"What kind of steel do you need? If it's urgent, I can head back down and get it." Akira offered.
Tsubaki waved him off casually. "What kind of smith makes the customer do the legwork? Relax. I'm Level 5, remember?"
In the next moment, she transformed from craftsman to warrior, strapping a freshly forged katana to her waist. No armor. Just her red hakama pants, a sleeveless top that exposed her navel, and a fearless grin.
"I'm heading to the dungeon myself."
Since the owner of the workshop was planning to go to the dungeon, Akira certainly would not stay here.
Akira, curious, followed her out of the workshop. Together, they walked toward the Tower of Babel—her strides confident and unhurried, even without armor.Follow current novᴇls on NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
Midway through the walk, Tsubaki tilted her head and said, "You ever think of buying a magic sword? I've got some prototypes I just finished. If you buy one now, I'll knock off some of the forging price later."
Akira shook his head and said, "Thanks, but I already know some magic. Using a magic sword would be kind of redundant for me."
"By the way, how much does a magic sword cost?"
"Oh? Still curious, huh?" She grinned and held up three fingers.
"Three million a pair. That's cheap, you know."
Akira chuckled awkwardly and said, "Hahaha... right. Super cheap."
Tsubaki blinked and said, "You didn't ask about my forging fee either."
Akira froze and asked, "Oh—how much?"
She leaned in close with a mischievous grin. "Around ten million."
Akira blinked, then exhaled in relief. "That's... actually fine."
Tsubaki looked momentarily disappointed by his lack of reaction. "Tch, not the shocked face I was expecting."
Still, she slung her arm over his shoulder with a hearty laugh and said, "That includes the steel, so it's a great deal. If you're good with that, I'll get started."
"Thank you, Tsubaki-san." Akira replied, smiling warmly.
"I'll be counting on you."
Her loud laughter echoed down the busy street, blending with the clang of distant hammers and the steady pulse of Orario's industrial heartbeat.

chapters.title: Chapter 61 - 61: Hobgoblins and Moss Huge
chapters.content:
"Then we'll say goodbye here. You can come to me for weapons in a few days." Tsubaki waved to Akira and turned to walk into the dungeon entrance.
24th floor, large tree maze.
A group of goblin monsters that look similar to those on the upper floors, but are obviously its superior species, Hobgoblins, reaching two meters in height, spawned.
"Roar!"
Pairs of eyes flashed with strange red light in the thick fog, and low growls came from their mouths.
All the monsters attacked Akira fiercely without any coordination. Their only bloody purpose was to tear apart all the outsiders in front of them.
In this crowded space, their mighty bodies could not show their full strength, but facing such a large number of monsters, an ordinary team of adventurers might still lose their composure.
Akira exhaled, but did not draw the one-handed sword at his waist. Instead, a huge amount of magic power rose from his body.
If someone was here, they would see that the air around Akira was faintly shaking, and if they got close to him, they might have difficulty breathing.
Akira raised his right hand, and a faint light condensed in his palm. Then a shrill scream sounded, similar to the sound of thousand birds chirping at the same time.
Akira controlled the lightning in his hand, holding it like a whip. Then, he swung his arm violently and threw the lightning chains towards the group of monsters.
Swoosh!
The lightning chains cut through the air, making a sharp whistling sound, and chased after the monsters with astonishing speed and power.
In an instant, lightning mercilessly pierced through the bodies of the Hobgoblins one after another.Follow current novels on No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
Sometimes, the lightning even turned around as if they were equipped with trackers, stringing the Hobgoblins on the lightning chain like skewers of meat.
The air was filled with the smell of something burning and blood flowed out like a fountain, but was instantly evaporated by the high-temperature of the lightning.
Smoke floated out from the holes on the monster's body, creating a horrifying phenomenon.
A Hobgoblin who was trying to escape was instantly caught up and pierced by the lightning chain. With a look of obvious fear on it's terrifying face, it fell stiffly to the ground.
In a flash, Akira eliminated the group of Hobgoblins with just one move.
Akira clapped his hands and said happily, "That was easy. I should go to the next floor."
Akira, who had already gone deep into the large tree maze, scanned the front and fixed his eyes on the only tree hole in front of him. The empty tree hole seemed to be covered with transparent crystal and was particularly eye-catching.
But it was not like the angular crystal seen on the eighteenth floor, but was flat and smooth like condensed ice.
He could feel the moist air coming from the front, which was completely different from the gloomy atmosphere in the large tree maze. If he listened carefully, he could even catch the subtle sound of water.
The cave in front of him led to the stairs below, which was the path to the lower floor.
As the information provided by the Guild stated, once you leave the scope of the large tree maze, you will step into a world full of water.
When Akira was about to grab the vine and climb up to the cave entrance, he heard a rustling sound in the woods next to him. He looked towards the place where the sound came from.
Instantly, a huge fist covered with moss tore through the air and quickly smashed towards Akira.
Akira had no time to dodge so he could only raise his hands in front of him.
He was knocked away by the huge force from his hands, and crashed into several trees, breaking them. He rolled on the ground for several meters and stopped under a huge tree.
"Ahem, why do I always encounter some special monsters? This dungeon must have a grudge against me."
Akira propped himself up with his bare arms and looked at the large monster over 2 meters tall rushing towards him.
A Moss Huge, having a body made of moss, with pieces of upright moss as sharp as dragon scales, and roots extending all the way to the fingertips of its hands and feet.
"Ohh..."
The Moss Huge made a shockingly dull roar that made Akira want to plug his ears.
It then raised its two rough hands, clasped them together, and slammed them down towards Akira.
In an instant, a loud "bang" sounded and a large amount of dust was raised where Akira was.
Fragments of rock splashed on the ground, and a deep pit covered with cracks appeared under the monster's fist.
When the moss Huge realized that it had not killed Akira, it turned it's body alertly and looked around, it's arms shaking slightly to ensure that it could act quickly.
Just as the monster's red and cloudy eyes were shifting its gaze, Akira suddenly appeared in front of it and violently smashed its disgusting face with his flaming fist.
"This punch is a return gift for the previous punch!"
The Moss Huge took a few steps back and fell backwards, its face obviously burnt. Green liquid flew out, and the vines on its legs dug into the ground to help it stabilize its body.
The Moss Huge's twisted face roared at Akira, disgusting saliva spurted out, and then its strong arms stretched out to the side.
It's huge body made an annoying beeping sound, and then several small bumps suddenly appeared on the surface of it's body.
It's arms, shoulders, neck, legs, it's whole body was covered in small bumps. It was as if it was ready to launch something at any time.
But Akira would not let it succeed so easily. He raised his hand and released a Flame shield.
Unlike before when he could only make a flame shield the size of an average person's height, now as long as Akira uses up all his magic power, the Flame shield can cover the entire Moss Huge.
At the same time.
"Boom boom boom—"
Sharp projectiles—Dozens of seeds fired from all over the Moss Huge's body. The countless seed bullets were not fired in a straight line but from all directions.
But unfortunately for the Moss Huge, it's attack didn't work. The whirling Flame shield blocked the seed pellets.
Then the whirling Flame shield suddenly expanded and exploded, shrouding the Moss Huge in smoke.

chapters.title: Chapter 62 - 62: 25th Floor, Water City
chapters.content:
Akira used an ice shield to block the seed bullets that bounced back from the ground, and then used Ghost Flame on the smoke-filled area. Fierce flames erupted like a volcanic eruption.
"…Wuwu——Ooooohhh!!"
A tragic cry sounded, and the body of the moss Huge finally appeared in view.
The charred moss on its body fell down with a clatter, and the outer layer of armor-like roots was almost gone. The eyes that had been flashing red just now were now dim.
"It can even recover its body. It's really a tenacious monster."
Akira condensed a huge fireball in his right hand and was surprised to see new moss growing on the place where the monster had shed its moss.
"It's waiting for my magic. What is it waiting for? Waiting to die?" Akira thought as he looked at the motionless moss Huge.
Feeling that death was near, the vines on the moss Huge's legs pierced through the ground and quickly wrapped around Akira's feet.
At the same time, it tore the vines apart and turned to run away.
"If only I can...if only I can reach that place!" The Moss Huge thought, running and stretching out it's hand towards the forest.
The expanding fireball instantly compressed into a thin sheet, and then began to spin at an astonishing speed.
The high-speed rotating fire disc drew streams of air.
With a crisp "crack" sound, the running moss Huge was caught up by the fire disc and it's body was cut in half.
Akira aimed at the target and clenched his palm. The fire disc containing the violent fire element quickly expanded and exploded.
"Boom boom—"
The place where the Moss Huge was turned into a charred pit. The body of the moss Huge turned into ashes, and even the magic stone shattered. Nothing was left.
"It seems to be an enhanced species that can devour magic stones. Ordinary Moss Huges are not that strong."
Akira had encountered Moss Huges several times after staying with Ais on the 24th floor for a few days, but none of them were so durable.
Akira found no trace of the monster in the pit. After using magic to check, he confirmed that the monster was really dead. Hethen planned to turn around and go to the next floor.
If the monster was still alive and had escaped into the forest, Akira would have to give up his plan to venture to the next floor and continue to hunt it down.
After all, leaving this enhanced species would not be a good thing for others.
— — —
"Wow."
A crystal cave appeared in Akira's view. A gentle slope pointed downward, extending into unknown depths.
The cool breeze blowing in from the depths of the cave gently ruffled the tips of his hair. This is a fresh air current that he had never experienced in the "Large Tree Maze".
It leads people without any explanation, heralding that the next chapter of adventure is about to begin.
Akira snapped his fingers, and a ball of fire appeared out of thin air and floated in front of him.
What caught his eyes was a smooth cave with a floor, walls and ceiling that looked like an ice cave.
Going down to the depths of the cave, the sound of water flowing appeared in his ears, and he could gradually see the end of the slope.

After that, the two walked out of the no-man's land. Astraea led Akira along the complicated road, going up, down, left, and right for several times before reaching their destination.
A quiet church located deep in the maze of streets - Maria's Orphanage.
Astraea walked forward slowly, stretched out her hand and knocked on the door. With the sound of footsteps, the door quietly opened a crack.
Ten children carefully poked their heads out. When they saw that it was the goddess who often came to take care of everyone, a bright smile appeared on their faces, and they quickly opened the door, revealing the figures of other children, who were holding "weapons" in their hands.
All the children were very happy when they saw Astraea. They gathered around her and greeted her.
Two older children came to Akira and wanted to take the bag, but Akira only gave them the bag with toys and took the heavier books himself.
When Akira first came here that day, he didn't realize that this was an orphanage, but now he sees... there are indeed many children.
In Orario where many adventurers gather, many children are born among the countless adventurers coming and going.
However, not all of these children are the fruit of love. Some may have been abandoned simply because of their parents' momentary passion. Others may have become orphans because their adventurer larents died young in the Dungeon.
Children who are not cared for by their families or abandoned by their biological parents often end up in Daedalus Street, which is known as the slum.
Akira and Astraea entered the church hall surrounded by the children. Last time, he only thought about donating Valis and did not observe the church carefully.
The interior of the church was deeper than its exterior. In the spacious hall, several doors led to different rooms.
Although the walls and pillars were covered with traces of time, the graffiti and daily necessities left over from long-term use added a touch of life to this place.
For the children growing up here, although the environment was a bit tough, it was enough to meet their needs.
Astralia smiled and gently asked the children, "Is Maria not at home? If anyone knows where she went, I will give him a small reward."
"Me, me"
"Goddess, choose me."
"It's my turn now, goddess."
The younger children raised their hands and cheered.
Astraea picked out a little girl who was trying to tiptoe and said with a smile, "Then let's go with this cute child."
"Maria mom went out to buy ingredients." The little girl answered excitedly.
Astraea picked out a cute doll from the toy bag and handed it to her. "Is that so? Then, this cute child is handed over to you. Please cherish it."
"I understand!" A clear voice came from the girl's mouth.
Before Maria arrived, Astraea and Akira could only do their respective duties. Astraea was responsible for distributing the toys she had brought and telling them stories.
Akira could only sigh helplessly and play games with these active children, searching his mind for those simple and interesting games.
Akira first brought some children to an open space and drew 9 numbered squares on the ground, deciding to play "hopscotch".
Then he explained the rules of the game to them and demonstrated how to play it.
There was also a stone catching game introduced to those children who did not like sports. Akira went outside, picked out a few stones of suitable sizes, and taught them how to play.
"Hahaha, you didn't hit the grid, you lose, it's my turn now."
"Damn it! I won't lose next time."
After hearing the excited voices of the children, Akira finally breathed a sigh of relief.
Although these children were all well-behaved, sensible and lovable, it was indeed not an easy task to deal with them. He didn't know how Maria handled them.
"It seems that the games proposed by Akira are very much to their liking. Even the children who were originally concentrating on listening to my story ran over to play." Astraea said with a smile as she sat next to Akira.
"Isn't this the nature of children? Playing is often much more interesting than sitting there quietly reading a book." Akira said slowly, a trace of nostalgia appearing on his face.
"Besides, it's fine if it's just for fun. Unlike when I was a kid, I was so reckless."
Astraea, who was standing by, looked at Akira with interest, and gently took his hand.
She smiled and softly said, "So, as your goddess, may I have the honor of listening to those interesting stories from your childhood?"
There was nothing that could not be said. As Akira described the situation vividly, Astraea sometimes opened her eyes wide in surprise, and sometimes chuckled. Akira was also infected by her smile and his face was also filled with a smile.
The whole scene was filled with laughter and joy, as if time had stopped at this moment.

chapters.title: Chapter 68 - 68: Swordsman VS Dragon
chapters.content:
After a while of waiting, Maria slowly appeared.
When she pushed open the door of the church carrying several children and a basket full of food, Astraea, who often came here to take care of the orphanage, and Akira, who had recently become famous, appeared in front of her.
Maria said, "Ah, Astraea-sama, you are here. Sorry for the trouble."
Astreaa said, "No, it makes me happy to see the children growing up healthily."
Maria then looked at Akira and said, "And isn't this Akira? It's been a long time since we last met. I'm so glad you're safe and sound. I've been hearing your name a lot in Orario recently."
Maria walked forward with the ingredients and greeted the two of them enthusiastically.
At this time, Akira took the heavy food they brought and said apologetically, "I'm sorry, Maria-san, it took me so long to come and say hello to you."
"No, no, I'm very happy that you came again. After all, you are an adventurer, so it's normal to be busy." Maria smiled and waved her hand.
Akira followed Maria to the kitchen, while Astraea stayed behind to look after the younger children.
Along the way, Maria was extremely talkative. She always had a smile on her face and kept asking Akira about his well-being.
After a while, she asked with concern, "Akira, how have you been recently? Did you encounter any danger or difficulties during your adventure?"
After a while, she reminded with concern, "Remember to eat well on time, don't treat your body badly!"
As expected of the mother of all the children in the orphanage, her caring ability is high level!
After putting down the ingredients, Maria said, "Akira, please wait outside. Since Astraea-sama has taken so much care of us, let us entertain you and Astraea-sama this time."
"I understand. I'll go out first then." Akira nodded obediently.
When Akira returned to the hall, he saw that Astraea had joined the game of hopscotch. In order to prevent her long skirt from dragging on the ground and tripping herself, she lifted the hem of her skirt lightly and shrugged it. The action was both elegant and dignified.
Every time she jumped lightly, her beautiful body that carried a heavy heart of justice would tremble, attracting him, and every time it was a feast for Akira's eyes.
After Astraea deliberately lost to those lovely children, she slowly stood up, and adjusted her skirt gracefully. Then she sat down steadily beside Akira with a smile on her face.
She turned her head slightly, stared at Akira with her beautiful eyes, and said softly, "It seems that Maria plans to entertain us."
Akira replied, "Well, after all, she is very grateful to you for coming to take care of the orphanage frequently. Otherwise, with the level of chaos on Daedalus Street, I don't think it would be possible for the children here to be safe and sound."
Akira today is no longer the ignorant man he was when he first arrived in Orario.
Through the information obtained from various channels and the detailed descriptions given to him by Kaguya and the others, he gradually realized that Daedalus Street was a mixed crowd of all kinds of people.
Not only do all kinds of people gather here, but even Evilus frequently appears here.
In addition, the terrain here is as complex as a maze, and it has been unsupervised for a long time, so it naturally became an ideal hiding place and base for many dark forces.
Therefore, it is not an easy thing for these innocent children to survive in such a harsh environment.
As if seeing through Akira's thoughts, Astraea took the initiative to reach out her hand and interlocked her fingers with his.
She gently said, "Don't worry, one day this place will be prosperous again, and by then, even child will be able to play here freely."
Akira joked, "Is this Astraea-sama's wish? If everyone knew about this, they would work together to make this wish come true, no matter how difficult it is."
Astraea stretched out her other hand, as if to hit him, but in the end she just gently stroked the top of his head.
"Doesn't that make it a responsibility I impose on you? I'm not such a goddess."
After saying that, Astraea withdrew her hand and leaned slightly against Akira, her tone somewhat relaxed and playful.
After all, even the goddess of justice will be more or less partial to her own children.
Akira didn't say anything else, but just smiled and shared this warm moment with Astraea.
After a while of waiting, it seemed that the lunch was ready.
A cute little girl ran over excitedly and announced loudly, "Everyone, Maria mom said that lunch is ready. She told me to call everyone to come over to eat."
Then, she came to Akira and Astraea. She stretched out her tender little hand, hoping to hold their hands and go to the kitchen together.
However, when she noticed their tightly clasped hands, a puzzled expression appeared on her face.
Akira and Astraea let go of each other's hand, gently reached out to the little girl in front of them, and held her hands at the same time.
Seeing the bright smile on the little girl's face, Akira and Astraea exchanged a knowing smile.
After lunch, the children could only sit in their chairs, bored and drowsy. It seemed that they had played too many games in the morning.
The children who went out to help had not seen the new game, nor had the experience, so they could only look at Akira and Astraea with pitiful eyes.
Akira and Astraea realized that it was almost time to leave. However, in order to leave good memories for these lovely children, Akira decided to give a wonderful magic show as a farewell gift.
Akira clapped his hands and said excitedly, "Does anyone want to see a magic show? If so, raise your hands."
The originally silent atmosphere immediately ignited and the children's spirits were lifted.
The church became extremely lively as countless little hands raised high. Several pairs of bright eyes sparkled with curiosity and excitement.
The whole room seemed to be infected by this innocent joy.
Akira walked to the empty space in front of the church and raised his hands. Magic power was boiling in his body.
Fortunately, Akira was far enough away from the children, otherwise they might be frightened by the oppressive feeling of magic.Thɪs updatᴇd by Novᴇ(l)Fɪre .ɴᴇt
Two 2-meter-tall ice blocks appeared in front of Akira. Although ice was the forte of Glacial master, not Elemental Blaster, its strength was enough for Akira to fool the children.
With a "crack", the two ice cubes shattered.
"Wow!!" The children exclaimed.
A cute ice dragon and a ice man holding a sword appeared in front of the children.
They didn't know that the two ice dolls in front of them were wrapped and controlled by Akira's magic power. The ice dolls began to move.

chapters.title: Chapter 69 - 69: A Date With Astraea
chapters.content:
Although they were made of ice, Akira made the inside of their limbs movable.
The dragon opened its mouth and sprayed a mist at the swordsman. The man squatted slightly, then jumped into the air under Akira's control to avoid the mist.
At the same time, Astraea narrated the battle to add some fun to the performance.
After flipping and turning a few times in the air, the Man stabbed the Dragon with a sword but it blocked it with its arm.
With a "ding" sound, the sword bounced off and fell to the side.
Then, the dragon bit the man's shoulder. To make it more realistic, Akira let the ice on his shoulder melt and water flow out.
"Oh no, it looks like the swordsman won't be able to defeat the monster. Everyone should cheer for him." Astraea said with a smile, pretending to be surprised.
"Come on!!!"×N
As if he really heard the children's cheers, the swordsman stood up and gave them a thumbs up.
Then he raised his hand and aimed at the falling ice sword. With a "swoosh", the sword flew into his hand.
Then, a faint blue light bloomed from his body, and his ordinary body instantly became covered with an armor and a cloak.
The transformation made many children exclaim.
The sword in the man's hand was surrounded by a gust of wind, and he slashed at the dragon's body, cutting it in half.
Then, amid the cheers of the children, he raised the sword in his hand, which slowly turned into ice crystals and disappeared.
Seeing this, Maria began to lead the children to applaud.
Before leaving with Astraea, Akira wanted to do one more thing.
"Maria-san, could you please come over here for a moment?" Akira waved to Maria and led her to a more secluded corner.
Maria asked with a friendly smile, "What's wrong, Akira? Is there anything you need my help with?"
Akira took out a bag of Valis from his backpack and handed it to Maria, whispering, "This is the Valis I want to donate this time, please accept it."
Although Akira was able to provide more funding, he was worried that too generous a gift would bring unnecessary trouble to the orphanage, so he deliberately kept the amount to 500,000 Valis.
When Maria took the bag, which was obviously heavier than the last time, she immediately realized that it contained a considerable fortune.
"I know you will definitely not agree with my refusal. But I want to ask why you want to help us." Maria said silently.
Hearing this, Akira said happily, "Just like Maria-san, I just do what I can. At least I am able to do something good, which makes me feel genuinely happy."
After hearing Akira's reason, Maria stood on her tiptoe and patted his head as if he were her own child.
"Thank you, Akira."
'Just this thank you is enough.' Akira thought.
When it was Astraea and Maria's turn to chat before leaving, Akira quietly stepped outside the church.
Without drawing attention, he set up several protective magic circles at the gate and surrounding areas—silent barriers meant to guard the children while he was away.
The time to depart soon arrived. Everyone in the orphanage gathered by the entrance, waving with bright smiles and teary eyes as they saw the two off.
"Brother Akira, you better come back and play with us again!" A little girl shouted, clinging tightly to her ragged but well-loved doll.
"Stay safe out there, Brother Akira!" A boy called, his voice filled with genuine worry and admiration.
Akira turned as he walked backward, waving at them with all the energy he could muster.
"No problem! I promise!"
Though they had only spent half a day together, Akira had managed to win over the hearts of the children completely.
Watching their reactions, Astraea couldn't help but notice—Akira had a natural ability to bond with children. That warmth of his… it made him instantly likable.
They walked away from the dilapidated Daedalus Street, passing through a dim alley. As they stepped out of the shadows, the narrow path opened up, and a bright expanse of blue sky filled their view.
From the ruins of the slums to the vibrancy of East Street, the shift in scenery was almost disorienting.
The air buzzed with energy—voices chatting, merchants shouting, and the sound of laughter mingling in a lively chorus. A sharp contrast to the heavy silence of where they had just been.
Walking side by side with Akira, Astraea stood out. Her serene beauty, paired with her divine presence, drew countless stares from pedestrians—some filled with admiration, others with awe.
She reached over and gently took his arm, her lips curved in a soft smile as she asked, "So, Akira, what do you plan to do next?"
"Then… will Astraea-sama go on a date with me?" Akira replied with a grin.
Standing at nearly the same height as Astraea, he only needed to tilt his head slightly to meet her gaze—eyes as clear and gentle as still water, framed by softly lifted lashes.
And then there were her lips—delicate, slightly parted—and just beneath that, if one's eyes dared to wander lower, the gentle slope of her chest that her garb didn't bother hiding much.
"A date? If other gods see us acting so intimately, they'll gossip non-stop." Astraea muttered.
Her cheeks puffed ever so slightly as she poked his arm with her smooth, fair finger.
"Didn't you say you hated being the center of attention?"
Akira gently patted her hand and sighed. "If you hadn't insisted on not letting me act like a transferred member, I wouldn't have become so conspicuous. At this point, I might as well lean into it."Follow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
"Besides, gods being affectionate with their children isn't that rare. I don't get why it bothers you."
Astraea added with a smirk and an air of teasing nonchalance, "Hmph. Even among gods, few act as close to their children as we do. Except for the weird ones… and you know who I mean."
"Let's not drift into those kinds of conversations, Astraea-sama," Akira said quickly, pointing at a charming little café just ahead.
His eyes lit up like a child spotting a rare treasure. "Let's go try that place! I haven't had coffee in this world yet."
Before she could protest, Akira slipped his arm free and took her hand, pulling her gently toward the café like an eager boy dragging his date to a favorite spot.
Feeling his fingers wrap around hers, Astraea gave an exaggerated sigh, but there was no hiding the soft smile that spread on her lips.
"Alright, alright. There's no need to rush—I'm not going to vanish. Take it slow."
But despite her words, her grip on his hand only tightened. The warmth that radiated from Akira's palm brought a flutter to her chest. It was a warmth that made her heart feel light.
"Akira." She called gently.
Hearing his name, Akira slowed his pace and turned to her, puzzled. "Hmm? What is it, Astraea-sama?"
Astraea took a few steps closer, her eyes filled with an emotion difficult to define—something deep, tender.
She leaned in, her lips brushing the edge of his ear as she whispered softly, "On this date… you don't need to call me with an honorific. Just call me by name."
At that moment, their connection subtly shifted. This was no longer the casual outing of a god and her child.
No—this was unmistakably a lover's stroll beneath a sunlit sky, hearts drawn close by something far deeper.

chapters.title: Chapter 70 - 70: Black Eyed Susans
chapters.content:
Akira looked at the slightly bashful Astraea with surprise flickering in his eyes. The corners of his lips curled upward without thinking, and he softly replied, "I know… Astraea."
The café wasn't far—just a short walk away. In only a few minutes, the two arrived at their destination, a quaint little café that clearly stood apart from the surrounding buildings.
There were no flashy signs or grand entrances, but delicate art pieces were hung tastefully near the door.
Light filtered in through the glass panels, casting a gentle glow over the small wooden round door entwined with creeping vines.
Greenery and hand-drawn posters adorned the entrance, creating an ambiance that felt both natural and serene.
Inside, the interior opened into a flexible and thoughtfully designed space. There were cozy open seating areas and tucked-away private corners, separated not by walls, but by half-height partitions and lush potted plants. It gave the feeling of intimacy without isolation.
The blend of warm off-white tones with dark brown wooden textures made the atmosphere feel calm and inviting. It was a bar-style café, run with quiet efficiency and charm.
After indulging in rich coffee and delectable desserts, the two slowly departed, smiling as the owner bid them a heartfelt farewell.
"I didn't expect coffee and sweets to be so unique here. It really opened my eyes. I'll try making it for you next time."
Astraea said softly, savoring not only the taste but the rare recipe the café manager had so casually shared with her.
Of course, recipes were the lifeblood of any eatery. Yet the manager had offered it to her without hesitation.
Perhaps it wasn't merely her divine identity that invited trust—Akira believed it was her gentle, open-hearted aura that made people want to draw near.
After a short rest on a roadside bench, the two began strolling again, hand in hand. They wandered leisurely through the street, stopping often to watch the impromptu performances of local entertainers.
With each stand they passed, Akira bought a different snack to try, almost as if he were on a quest to taste everything the city had to offer.
Astraea would sneak a bite the moment he wasn't looking, only to flash him a mischievous smile and say, "This one's delicious too, Akira."
Looking at the half-eaten snack in his hand, Akira chuckled and took a bite from the same spot. "Hehe, you're right… it is delicious, Astraea."
"It seems my boyfriend's a bit of a pervert." Astraea teased, feigning outrage.
She clasped her hands and gave him a light knock on the head, as if reprimanding a naughty child.Thɪs ɴo(v)elFɪre.ɴet
As they walked, the sky shifted into a warm orange hue, dusk gradually painting the city in shades of gold.
From the direction of the clock tower, the sound of chimes rang out, a gentle reminder that their date was nearing its end.
The gentle breeze danced across Astraea's face, swinging her long brown hair.
She turned toward Akira and opened her soft red lips. "It seems our first date is drawing to a close. But as a first date… this time we shared together has brought me so much happiness and contentment."
She looked at him with eyes that sparkled like starlight—filled with affection, quiet joy, and something deeper that she didn't try to hide. A faint, gentle smile played on her lips, touching Akira's heart like a melody only he could hear.
Akira met her gaze and returned her smile with radiant warmth. "Astraea… I'm so glad you like it. I'll remember this date for the rest of my life."
Then, as if remembering something important, he suddenly turned away and said, "Wait just a moment—I'll be right back."
He hurried toward a flower shop he often passed by during his return from adventuring.
Stepping inside, he scanned the displays until his eyes landed on a particular blossom. Small golden petals surrounding a raised, purple-brown core. The sight sparked something in his chest.
He didn't know why, but he had a gut feeling that these flowers suited Astraea perfectly.
"Boss, could you wrap a few of these for me?" Akira asked, pointing to the flowers.
The shopkeeper glanced toward the figure waiting outside. Though he couldn't make out her full appearance, her elegant presence was impossible to overlook.
With a knowing smile, he asked, "Is it for your goddess? Just a few will do?"
Akira nodded. Flowers with such prominent petals didn't need to be excessive. A few were more than enough.
With practiced hands, the florist trimmed the lower leaves to keep them from draining water from the blooms. He carefully pierced the stems to maximize absorption, then wrapped the bouquet with care and handed it over to Akira.
With the bouquet in hand, Akira stepped out of the shop and returned to Astraea, offering the flowers to her with both hands.
"Astraea … please accept these flowers. I don't know exactly what kind they are, but I just have a feeling—they're perfect for you."
Astraea accepted them gently, holding them with both hands. She leaned in and inhaled the subtle scent—a mix of jasmine and rose, delicate and warm.
Then, still holding the bouquet in her right hand, she linked her left arm with his.
The two began walking toward the Stardust Garden, their steps in perfect sync.
"Akira… you really don't know what kind of flower this is?" She asked, curiosity tinged with amusement.
Akira scratched his cheek and thought aloud. "It looks a little like a sunflower… but not quite."
Astraea giggled softly and explained, "These are called black-eyed susans. The name might sound a bit strange, but they carry a beautiful meaning in flower language. Would you like to hear it?"
Akira groaned and shook his arm, feigning frustration. "Astraea, stop being so mysterious. Just tell me already."
Astraea giggled and replied in a soft, teasing voice, "Guess what it is. If you get it right, I'll give you a reward."
Akira rubbed his chin, thinking seriously. He knew flower meanings often revolved around love, so he ventured, "Is it related to love?"
"Correct. That's one of them. Can you guess another?" She asked, her expression hopeful as she watched him.
He pondered for a long time, but nothing came to mind. Eventually, he could only shake his head.
Astraea gently guided his arm to point at herself and asked, "When you see me, what comes to mind?"
It was like a jolt of electricity went through his brain. His eyes widened slightly as the answer clicked into place.
"…Justice… Astraea-sama?"
At that moment, Astraea's face bloomed with joy. Her expression was brighter than spring blossoms, her smile so radiant it made time seem to pause.
"Exactly! You got it! Akira really is sharp." She said happily.
Akira chuckled, though he felt her hints had been pretty blatant.
"Hehe… it's just that my love for you is strong. When we're on the same wavelength, nothing can stop us."
Astraea reached out and gently tapped his forehead with her finger—her skin smooth and fair like polished jade.
"You're such a sweet talker."
She then added, "The flower's meaning is generally understood as fairness and justice, believing in one's own love, and a love that's truly unique."
Akira didn't reply with words. Instead, he simply held her hand a little tighter, as if trying to pour all his emotions into that single gesture.
Feeling the warmth transmitted through their entwined fingers, Astraea turned her head to look at him.
In the quiet of her heart, she murmured, 'The meaning of this flower must be the perfect embodiment of our love. You chose them without knowing, Akira… That's why I believe—our meeting must have been fate.'
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 71 - 71: A Gift From Astraea
chapters.content:
Because the Astraea Familia's base was located near a bustling, noisy vegetable market, Astraea could easily purchase all the ingredients needed for tonight's dinner from nearby stalls.
Of course, Akira was the one who paid. Just one look at Astraea's elegant divine robes made it clear she couldn't exactly carry a coin pouch.
And as a proud member of the Astraea familia, how could he possibly let his goddess foot the bill?
When Akira took the heavy bag of groceries from her hands, he turned without hesitation into a narrow alleyway. Moments later, he emerged empty-handed, his expression calm and composed.
Storing everything in [Backpack] makes it easier to keep holding her hand, after all.
Just as Akira was enjoying the moment of walking hand in hand with Astraea, she spoke softly beside him, "Didn't I promise you a reward if you guessed the flower's meaning correctly? Come with me."
She led him to the clothing store where they had shopped before—more precisely, to the inconspicuous watch shop nestled beside it.
"Welcome." The store manager greeted them with a warm smile.
He was a middle-aged man with a gentle expression and wore a single-sided monocle, adding to his vintage charm.
Akira stepped inside, his gaze drifting curiously across the walls. The shop seemed like a shrine to time—ancient wooden wall clocks, gleaming metal table clocks, and artistically shaped timepieces filled the room, each one ticking with its own rhythm.
In a glass display case in front of the manager were an assortment of delicate pocket watches. Some were embedded with dazzling gemstones, others engraved with intricate patterns, and still others clearly made of rare and valuable materials.
Akira glanced at Astraea with understanding. So this is the reward she mentioned.
Astraea approached the counter and said in a whisper, "Manager, is the special pocket watch I commissioned last time ready?"
The manager nodded. "Yes, Astraea-sama. I will bring it out now."
As the man disappeared into the back room, Akira leaned down slightly to observe the pocket watches up close, then whispered, "So... you're giving me a pocket watch."
Astraea tilted her head amd asked, "What's wrong? You don't like pocket watches?"
Akira smiled gently and said, "I like anything Astraea gives me. I'll treasure it."
Soon the manager returned and set a pocket watch carefully on the counter.
Its surface was a warm rose-gold hue, like the soft blush of a blooming flower. The outer cover was carved with the emblem of the Astraea Familia—delicate, divine, and unmistakable.
When opened, the inside revealed the same insignia in fine detail, inlaid around the edge.
Most striking of all were the hands of the watch. They shimmered faintly in the fading sunlight, casting a soft blue glow that resembled twinkling stars in the night sky.
"This is the custom piece you ordered, Astraea-sama." The manager said.
"I hope it's to your satisfaction."
Astraea turned to Akira and gently handed him the watch.
Her eyes gleamed with affection as she asked, "What do you think? Do you like it?"
Akira took it with both hands, a bright smile lighting up his face.
He happily said, "It's perfect. I think any man would fall in love with such a beautiful watch. Thank you, Astraea."
Unable to contain his gratitude, he stepped forward and embraced her lightly, returning the warmth she had shown him.
After returning to the base, Akira helped Astraea wash and prep the ingredients as usual, chopping them into neat pieces. Once that was done, the two sat together in the hall, waiting for the others to return home.
Every night was the same—they waited until the rest of the familia came back before officially starting dinner. After all, it was hard for Astraea to cook for everyone by herself, and their group included some rather ravenous eaters.
"Astraea-sama! We're back!"
Even before the door opened, Alise's vibrant voice echoed through the entrance.
Footsteps approached quickly, and Alise burst through the door of the hall, rushing straight toward them and throwing herself down across their laps.
"Ugh! I'm so tired. Everything today was such a hassle!" She groaned, resting her head dramatically.
Akira chuckled and gently tapped her thigh as if massaging it and asked, "Weren't you patrolling Orario today? What kind of trouble did you run into?"
"We're preparing for a dungeon expedition." Kaguya's voice cut in as she entered the hall. She looked particularly exhausted.
"If we don't take more commissions and make more Valis, we won't even be able to maintain our equipment."
"That's right." Lyra added, throwing up her hands.
"The guild's compensation barely covers the essentials. And don't forget—we have a whole logistics team to feed."
Ryuu spoke next, her expression calm but serious, "Plus, some of our patrols are self-initiated. If this keeps up, we might even struggle to put food on the table."
"It's not that bad yet, Ryuu. Don't scare Akira." Noin said brightly, holding Ryuu's arm with a teasing grin.
Akira raised an eyebrow and said, "I am not scared. I know how much it takes to keep a familia running. Besides, didn't I give Lyra a pile of materials from my last dungeon run? I figured they'd help with the finances."The latest_epɪ_sodes are on_the N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
Lyra nodded and said, "True, but I didn't sell them. You've been leveling up so fast that your gear soon be obsolete. You should start investing in new gear."
"I already placed an order with the Hephaestus Familia. Custom weapons tailored to me. So, you can use the remaining Valis." Akira explained.
"Oho? Tell me how much did it cost. I'll help you collect it." Neze said, scratching her head.
"Well... I paid two million Valis upfront as a deposit. The final cost will be around ten million."
"Ten million Valis?!" Everyone gasped.
Even Alise sat up in shock.
Ryuu immediately got in Akira's face, pushing Alise aside as she grabbed his shoulders.
She said, "Are you sure you weren't scammed? Even if it's the Hephaestus Familia, there could've been a con artist involved."
"That's way too expensive for a level two weapon!" Alise added.

chapters.title: Chapter 72 - 72: Proactive Alise, Exposed
chapters.content:
Astraea gently reached out and touched Ryuu's ear, a soft gesture that made the elf suddenly freeze and blush.
With a calm yet coaxing voice, she said, "Relax for a moment, Ryuu. I don't believe Akira is the kind of person to fall for a simple trick. Let him explain himself first."
"That's right, you useless elf. Not everyone gets scammed as easily as you do." Kaguya chimed in, flicking Ryuu's forehead with the edge of her hand in a light chop.
Alise also said, "And to think, you even pushed my beautiful face away so roughly… It truly wounds my heart, Ryuu."
Alise, ever the dramatist, took Akira's hand and sat on his lap again, covering her cheeks with exaggerated sorrow.
"I'm sorry, Alise. I was too anxious." Ryuu said apologetically, her head slightly bowed.
"But the situation on my end is more dangerous! Alise, what exactly are you doing?!" Akira screamed internally, struggling with mixed emotions.
When he glanced to the side, his eyes were drawn to the breastplate Alise had discarded upon returning home.
Though not as voluptuous as Astraea's, Alise's figure still had its own impact—soft yet energetic, with every subtle movement on his lap sending ripples of agony through his adolescent, high-energy body.
Her hips, which Lyra once claimed looked "tight and firm like an elite swordswoman's," constantly rubbed against his legs.
Akira clenched his fists. He couldn't take it anymore.
Even Ryuu, usually so composed, had once been described by Lyra as having "muscles soft as mochi but a curve that invites sin—like cotton candy for the soul." That image alone was dangerous.
This was hell.
He forcefully held down Alise, who had been shifting around on his lap like a restless kitten.
His face remained composed, but his voice trembled ever so slightly. "I believe the other party is trustworthy. She's the Cyclops Tsubaki, the top blacksmith of the Hephaestus Familia. I don't think someone like her would deceive others."
"Ohhh, that famous adventurer-craftsman? If it's her, I guess we don't need to worry." Ryana twirled a lock of her hair and nodded.
"Tsubaki? The one whose height makes even dwarves cry out in envy?" Asta murmured, her expression mixed with awe and envy.
Akira turned toward her and gave her a struggling thumbs-up.
He said, "Asta's just as lovely as she is. I'm sure there's someone out there who would choose you in a heartbeat."
Like me.
Asta gave him a sweet smile and said, "Thanks for the compliment, Akira."
Meanwhile, Alise, perhaps sensing something, suddenly froze. Her face burned red, and she looked downward, adjusting her position subtly.
"Hissssssss—" Akira sucked in a sharp breath through his teeth.
Astraea, who had been quietly watching, gave a knowing smile. She clapped her hands, and stood up with cheerful authority.
"Well, since everyone's here, let's get started on dinner preparations. Those who haven't showered yet, go clean up first."
"Whatever you want to talk about, save it for the dinner table." She added, grabbing Kaguya and Maryuu by the arms and dragging them toward the kitchen.
"Understood!" came the chorus of responses.
"I-I understand…" Alise echoed, her voice trembling as she stood up unsteadily.
As the others filtered out of the hall toward the bath, Akira quickly slipped out from under Alise and pulled her aside.
"You... you… Akira actually did that to me…" Alise mumbled, hiding her red face in her hands as her voice broke off in embarrassment.
Akira rolled his eyes and said, "Don't act like I attacked you. You were the one rubbing against me so much that... of course this happened!"
"I'm sorry… but you were the one who got up without asking me first…" Alise mumbled again, her voice growing smaller.
Akira's sharp ears didn't miss a thing. "Haah?! I'm a healthy man, okay?! Having a reaction is totally normal!"
"I know, you don't have to spell it out..." Alise muttered, suddenly lowering her hands and lunging forward.
She pushed Akira onto the sofa, grasping both of his wrists and straddling him in one bold move.
"Alise! You absolute idiot—what the hell are you doing now?" Akira didn't resist, but the helplessness on his face was plain.
His deep black eyes met her bright forest-green ones. Their gazes locked.
The space seemed to freeze, thick with tension.
Then Alise averted her eyes, shame flooding her expression as she whispered with trembling lips, "It's your fault. You made me this way… I'm supposed to be the perfect captain, and now look at me. You have to take responsibility!"
"…Also."
She added with a bitter smile, "I heard what you and Maryuu talked about in the hallway this morning. I didn't realize just how close you and Astraea-sama have gotten."
Her voice grew softer, tinged with vulnerability, "I'm jealous, you know. I was the first one to find you. The one who brought you into our familia."
Akira spoke gently, "But Alise already has a great relationship with Astraea-sama too."
Alise retorted, "It's different. You and Astraea-sama… the feeling is different. That's why I don't want to lose to her. I want to be someone you like as well!"
Without warning, she leaned down and kissed him—just a light brush of her lips.
Then, just as quickly, she jolted upright, cheeks blazing. She let go of Akira's hands and scrambled to stand up, clearly planning to flee.
But Akira caught her by the arm and tugged her back, wrapping his left hand around her waist and leaning in close.
Alise's eyes went wide. Her hands landed on his back in a daze, unsure whether to push him away or just surrender.
After a long moment, he released her gently.
"Is that enough proof that I've fallen for you too?" Akira asked with a grin as bright as the morning sun.
Alise's face was crimson, her eyes shimmering with unshed tears.
She nodded quietly, then muttered under her breath, "…Pervert."
Akira said without shying away, "Haha. That's me. Now go shower before someone comes looking."
"I-I get it, hehe…"
Alise stood up with Akira's help, a silly smile plastered on her face—only to freeze when she spotted two distinct heads poking out from the crack in the door.
One was the sly grin of a mischievous mouse. The other… a certain useless elf whose face was beet red.
The moment their eyes met, Lyra broke into a laugh while Ryuu let out a squeaky "Chi! Chi! Chi!" sound and darted off like a frightened rabbit.
"Wait for me, Ryuu!" Lyra shouted, slamming the door shut before giving chase.
Akira leaned toward Alise and whispered, "Well, we've been caught. What's the plan now, Captain?"
Slapping her cheeks to refocus herself, Alise puffed out her chest and declared, "Don't worry. Just leave this to the perfect captain. I'll go handle them!"
She threw open the door and, blushing fiercely, called back, "Next time, it's your turn to sleep with me! Got it?!"
'Do you really see me as some kind of body pillow...?'
"I know, I know... but I can't promise I'll behave." Akira replied with the same sly smirk Lyra always wore.ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ
That did it. Alise's face burned brighter than a tomato as she slammed the door again and fled to her room, leaving Akira standing alone in the hall.
(End of Chapter)
