chapters.title: Chapter 99 - 99: Let The Banquet Begin
chapters.content:
After saying that, Riveria gently raised her slender hand again, tapped Ais's delicate golden head with the tip of her finger, and admonished her in a calm but earnest tone.
"And you, Ais… no matter how excited or happy you are, you absolutely cannot push the door open so roughly. What if someone had been standing behind it? You could have hurt them badly. You must be more careful next time, understand?"
The tone wasn't harsh, but it carried the weight of a concerned elder, and it immediately pulled Ais back to reality.
Before she could even open her mouth to share all the fascinating things she had seen and experienced today, Ais was met with gentle scolding.
Her small face, which had been filled with radiant anticipation and vibrant excitement, froze for a moment.
Then, her expression gradually changed—those golden eyes dimmed slightly, her lips pressed together, and she looked down in grievance.
Helpless and wronged, Ais could only nod quietly to show she acknowledged her mistake.
"Well, well… I think Ais is just really happy, that's all. Riveria, there's no need to be so strict with her, especially not today."
Finn said warmly, stepping forward with his usual gentle smile as he tried to smooth things over like the kind-hearted captain he was.
"Besides, we've got a banquet to look forward to later, don't we?"
Hearing that, Akira, who had been silently watching the scene from the side, couldn't resist adding fuel to the fire.
With a light chuckle and a righteous posture, he declared boldly, "That's right! Riveria-san, you really are quite long-winded sometimes."
He even turned to Ais with a mischievous glint in his eye. "Right, Ais?"
Perhaps it was because she had experienced too many exciting and unpredictable adventures with Akira that day or perhaps it was simply the effect of being emboldened by his support but the usually quiet and obedient Ais actually puffed out her cheeks and nodded seriously.
"Yes… Riveria is really talkative today." She muttered in a pouty voice, her tone soft but surprisingly defiant.
Riveria, of course, wasn't truly angry. She simply sighed, her elegant brows twitching slightly. She reached out with both hands and, without warning, grabbed their cheeks and pulled.
"You two really have no self-control!" She scolded, pinching both their faces at once with a stern expression.
However, her actions were more playful than punitive. "Don't get too full of yourselves just because you ran around one day."
After releasing them, Riveria took a breath, straightened her posture, and finally asked, "Now then, Ais, what is it that you were so excited to share?"
The moment she received permission, Ais's expression brightened again. She eagerly began recounting her day's adventure to the three adults in the room.
She told them all about the places she had gone with Akira and the breathtaking sights she had witnessed. Her voice grew lively and animated as she described how they soared through the sky like birds, training amidst clouds and storms.
However, when it came to the topic of altitude, Ais glossed over it with vague words. She didn't mention the exact height she had flown to—likely because she knew Riveria would give her an even longer lecture if she found out.
To others, it might have sounded like the two were just goofing off in midair with magic. But to Ais and Akira, it had been something truly meaningful—something unforgettable.
Just as the room was still filled with their friendly chatter and laughter, a light knock came from the doorway.
Moments later, a young man with spiky hedgehog-like hair stepped inside. He walked quickly and respectfully up to the gathered group.
He said in a polite tone, "Captain, the dinner is ready. Everyone can head to the hall now."
Hearing this, Finn gave the boy a nod and a kind smile. "Thanks for the heads-up, Raul. Good work. In that case, let's not keep the others waiting—shall we?"
He clapped his hands together, calling the room to attention before taking the lead. The rest of the group followed after him, walking down the corridor with anticipation.
— — —
Inside the spacious and brightly lit banquet hall, an atmosphere of celebration was already in full swing.
The entire place was buzzing with energy. Cheers erupted in waves like crashing tides, and the long tables—several of them placed end-to-end—were already filled with all kinds of exquisite dishes, mouthwatering and fragrant.
Delicious food, golden drinks, and shining cutlery glittered under the crystal chandeliers.
Members of the Loki Familia, both veterans and newcomers alike, gathered joyfully around the tables. Toasts were being exchanged, mugs clinking together in rapid succession, and laughter spilled freely throughout the room.
Akira, although technically a guest, was soon swept up in the enthusiasm of the scene.
Even though many of the members weren't sure exactly why this banquet had been organized—after all, it wasn't a celebration for a Loki Familia member—they didn't question it.
Akira was clearly trusted by their captain, and if someone like Finn had personally invited him, then that was more than enough.
Besides, it wasn't like Akira's name was unknown.
Ever since that morning, the rumor of an adventurer named Akira, who had defeated the Level 3 Ais despite being only Level 2, had already begun to spread across the entire city of Orario.
It was only natural that everyone here wanted to meet the boy in person.
As the lively sounds of conversation and music continued, Finn slowly rose from his seat near the head of the banquet table. In his hand, he held a finely crafted wine glass, filled with golden liquor.
With a broad smile, he raised the glass and called out loudly, "Everyone!"
His voice boomed through the hall, and instantly, all noise faded. Heads turned, and countless eyes focused on him.
"I believe most of you have already heard of this particular adventurer—some of you probably know more about him than I do."
He said with a chuckle, "Rumors have been flying fast, so I won't bore you with them again."
He gestured to the youth standing beside him.
"This is Akira, from the Astraea Familia!"
The moment those words left his mouth, the entire banquet hall erupted into thunderous applause and cheers.
"Whooooaaaa!!"
Akira, standing there with a bashful smile, scratched the back of his head.
He waved to everyone a little awkwardly and said with a laugh, "Uh… thank you all. I'm just here to eat. Really."
The crowd laughed, and Finn grinned before raising his glass again.
"No need for more introductions! With that, let the banquet officially begin!"Thɪs updatᴇd by ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
As his words rang out, the room exploded into renewed celebration.
"OOOOHHHH——!"
Everyone shouted together, raising their cups and plates. The atmosphere soared even higher.
However, Akira barely had time to sit down and grab a bite before a barrage of enthusiastic questions was launched his way.
"How did you defeat Ais!?"
"It's just… a bit of special magic." Akira replied with a shrug.
"How did you level up so fast, Akira-senpai?" Raul leaned in, eyes sparkling.
Scratching his cheek, Akira said, "Uh… well, I did level up a little fast, yeah. But come on, Raul, you joined the familia before me. No need to call me senpai. Just Akira is fine."
"Really? Is that okay?"
"Totally. As for how I leveled up quickly… it varies for everyone, right?"
He muttered inwardly, 'It's not like I can tell them I'm cheating the system...'
"I get it now. Thank you, Akira!" Raul responded, a bit disappointed but still respectful.
"Okay, okay, move aside!" A group of energetic young women shoved Raul away and took his place.
One of them leaned in and asked in a syrupy voice, "What kind of girls do you like? Are we okay?"
"Hey—!" Akira reeled back in panic, trying to avoid the barrage of playful touches and teasing gazes.
Don't blame the girls. After all, while there were male members in the Loki Familia, most were veterans who had been around since the early days. The majority of newer members were striking young women—something that was clearly the result of Loki's preferences.
It was no secret throughout Orario that Loki was an unapologetic lover of beauty, especially when it came to her recruitment policies. Her familia's gender balance was skewed on purpose.
And now, standing in front of this mostly-female crowd, was a handsome, mysterious, and strong young man who had appeared out of nowhere.
"Uhh… gentle? I like gentle girls?" Akira stammered, shrinking backward.
If I'd known things would turn out like this, I would have—
Seeing the situation spiral, Akira quickly looked around the room for salvation.
His eyes sought out Finn, Riveria, and Ais like a desperate puppy begging for rescue.
As for Gareth?
The veteran dwarf was already deep into a drinking contest with Loki herself, surrounded by empty bottles.

chapters.title: Chapter 100 - 100: 200 Million Valis
chapters.content:
However, Akira remained blissfully unaware that the banquet he was currently enjoying had been meticulously orchestrated by none other than the goddess Loki herself—head of the notorious Loki Familia and a deity renowned throughout Orario, and among the gods, for her unrestrained mischief and bottomless appetite for scheming.
At the head of the hall, Loki sat reclined in her chair, a sly smirk curling her lips as she gently swirled the wine in her hand.
The crystal goblet shimmered under the lights, glowing with hues of ruby and gold. Her crimson eyes narrowed slightly, flashing with an unmistakable glint of ill intent as she observed the bustling crowd.
More specifically, her eyes were locked onto Akira, who was still surrounded by a mob of overly enthusiastic adventurers bombarding him with all manner of invasive questions.
She wasn't just watching.
She was plotting.
Loki's expression turned even more playful, lips quirking as she mouthed two exaggerated words across the room, deliberately slow and teasing—"Enjoy it~!"—before spinning around with dramatic flair, as if she had just pulled off the greatest prank of her life.
She strutted off like a mischievous child who had successfully stolen a cookie and gotten away with it.
Poor Akira had no idea what kind of trouble he was really in. Still flanked by smiling faces, curious voices, and overly affectionate women, he continued to fend off awkward questions and friendly ambushes one after another.
But as everyone knew—or rather, as everyone would eventually find out—this entire scene was nothing less than a meticulously crafted farce, a spontaneous play written and directed by none other than Loki herself.
And while Akira navigated the tide of people, Loki was seated a short distance away, gleefully reveling in her victory. Her mind was practically dancing as she celebrated her own genius in silence, shoulders shaking with suppressed laughter.
A moment later, pretending as though nothing had happened, she gracefully approached Gareth and took a seat beside the burly dwarf. Without a word, she plopped down, picked up a mug, and challenged him to a drinking duel.
The air between them crackled with the unspoken energy of countless past battles—liquid battles, that is.
Meanwhile, Finn, who sat nearby, turned his head slightly and allowed his gaze to drift toward Akira once again.
The boy was still surrounded.
Akira wore a helpless but genuinely warm smile, doing his best to maintain his composure.
Despite the whirlwind of conversation, hands tugging at his sleeves, and an onslaught of questions flying at him faster than arrows in a dungeon ambush, he remained patient—graceful even.
He gave each person a fair share of attention, nodding here, replying there, trying not to let anyone feel ignored. It was awkward. It was chaotic. But it was real.
Finn smiled softly.
How rare... It's not often the Familia gets to laugh and talk like this. And now they have something new to bond over—something to bring up with Ais. Three birds with one stone, indeed.
Finn chuckled to himself, his thoughts drifting inward.
Later, I'll have to explain everything to Akira—why everyone's acting like overzealous fans. But for now… let him suffer a bit. It's good for him to get used to this kind of attention.
Eventually, just when it looked like Akira was about to be swept away by a second wave of admirers, a savior descended.
Riveria stepped forward with elegant grace, reached out calmly, and pulled Akira to her side with an air of quiet authority. The crowd instinctively backed off.
Thus, the crisis was finally resolved.
As the feast gradually neared its end, and people relaxed with food and drink, an unexpected figure approached Akira once more.
Gareth, cheeks already tinged red from alcohol, sauntered up beside him with surprising stealth. With a quiet smile, he handed Akira a glass of richly colored wine that sparkled faintly under the chandeliers.
It had a mellow, fruity fragrance—clearly a potent variety of fruit wine.
Although Akira's physical resilience far exceeded that of most adventurers—possibly even surpassing Gareth himself—the alcohol still triggered a slight flush on his cheeks.
His metabolism neutralized the intoxication quickly, but it couldn't completely prevent the warmth from spreading across his face.
Even so, compared to the two drunken veterans wobbling beside him, Akira's condition was nearly pristine.
Loki was now clinging tightly to Gareth's shoulders, laughing uproariously as she half-yelled, half-slurred, "Pfft—! Hahahaha! I'm still standing! Gareth, you're wobbling already!"
"Hmph!" Gareth snorted, swaying but refusing to concede.
"Don't be ridiculous, woman. You're the one who can't even sit straight anymore!"
"Me? Unconscious? In your dreams!" Loki laughed so hard she nearly fell off her chair. "I could drink circles around you!"
"Keep dreaming, Loki," Gareth grunted. "You've got the tolerance of a squirrel!"Tʜe source of this ᴄontent ɪs ɴovᴇl(F)ɪre.ɴet
And with that, the two launched into another heated argument/drinking contest, much to the amusement and quiet resignation of those around them.
By the time the festivities concluded, the group of rowdy drunks had staggered off somewhere toward the office quarters, arms linked, feet uncoordinated.
Finn, who had only sampled two glasses, and both Riveria and Ais, who hadn't touched a single drop, watched the comedic scene unfold in resigned silence.
Riveria sighed heavily and rubbed her temples.
She glanced at Akira and murmured with a hint of exasperation, "Sorry you had to witness that. Those two lose all sense of decorum every time there's a banquet. They're… troublesome people."
Akira gave a sheepish grin and raised his hands in a pacifying gesture.
He said, "It's alright. Really. I mean, it is a party held in my honor. As long as everyone's happy…"
He paused, then mumbled under his breath, "Even though I still don't understand why they're throwing an actual banquet just for me."
His words made Riveria and Finn exchange a knowing glance before the two of them simultaneously burst into quiet laughter.
After a few moments, Finn stepped forward, gently patting Akira's shoulder. "Not long ago, Akira… you gave us something very valuable. A magic tool."
Riveria continued, her voice steady and sincere, "That kind of thing isn't something we can accept casually. We needed to express our gratitude. A simple thank-you wouldn't suffice."
"So, we decided a banquet was the least we could do." Finn concluded with a smile.
He looked Akira directly in the eye and added, "And if there's ever anything troubling you, no matter what it is—don't hesitate to tell us. We'll do everything we can to help."
Akira nodded seriously, visibly moved by their sincerity.
"I understand. And… even though magic tools are precious, I gave them to you because I don't want to lose friends like you when danger comes."
But then, with a shift in tone, Akira added casually, "Besides, making them isn't really difficult for me."
His words stunned both Riveria and Finn.
"And honestly… only I can make them."
With that, Akira pulled out a bag from [Backpack] and handed it to Finn. Inside were over a dozen newly crafted magic tools—freshly forged and neatly packed.
As his level increased, the rate at which Akira could produce these tools had soared. He could easily make over a dozen per day now.
If not for his concerns about destabilizing the market—or worse, letting these fall into the hands of Evilus—he might have already sold hundreds.
At present, he had nearly a hundred teleportation props tucked away in his room. If sold at market price, they would easily net the Astraea Familia billions of Valis.
Seeing the contents of the bag, Finn and Riveria's jaws nearly dropped.
Akira smirked and said, "Well, I'm trying to make a little money too, so this time I'm charging you—discounted price, of course. Two hundred million Valis. Take them all."
He added with a grin, "Since everyone keeps saying the familia's running out of money, I figured I'd collect a little."
Finn's eyes sparkled like he'd just struck gold. He eagerly accepted the bag, but in his excitement, he accidentally gripped Akira's hand too hard.
Despite being a pallum, Finn's strength—backed by his Level 5 status—still made Akira wince slightly in pain.
"Only two hundred million Valis? That's it? Should we pay more?" Finn asked breathlessly.
"We can pay more!"
"Oi! You're hurting him!" Riveria immediately grabbed Finn's hand and pried it away from Akira's with a frown.
Turning to Akira, she asked gently, "Are you sure this is enough? Just because we're friends, you shouldn't lower the price by this much."

chapters.title: Chapter 101 - 101: Akira Protects His Innocence
chapters.content:
Akira shook his head and replied with a smile that bore a striking resemblance to Astraea's gentle expression, "No need. If my familia wasn't short on funds lately, I would've given them to you for free. As for the rest of the magic tools, just let me know when you run out."
He glanced at the small bag filled with precious items, then added casually, "Besides, I doubt you'll be heading out on another expedition anytime soon."
Finn nodded earnestly, his voice solemn with genuine appreciation. "Understood. Once again, thank you, Akira. With these magic tools, the chances of our familia members encountering danger in the deeper floors can be significantly reduced."
But just as Finn's words trailed off, a sudden movement broke the calm.
Loki, who had previously been sprawled out lifelessly in a drunken daze, abruptly sprang to life as if struck by divine inspiration. She lunged toward Akira.
"Ahaha~ So that's how it is. I finally understand why they all like you so much…" She muttered dreamily, her eyes sparkling with intoxicated affection.
Akira's expression turned stiff.
"H-Hey! W-Wait a minute—"
Before he could react further, he found himself nearly tackled by the drunken goddess, her arms flung wide open as she closed in for a hug.
Panic erupted in Akira's heart like a firework. He raised both hands in alarm, his palms pressing desperately against Loki's face as he tried to hold her at bay.
"Hey! I said stop hugging me!! Didn't you say you were drunk just now!?"
But Loki merely giggled like a mischievous child, her voice thick with amusement and mischief.
"Hehehe~ Who knows? Maybe my deep love for children has sobered me up! Don't fight it, Akira~ Let's get a little closer~"
As she spoke, the silly grin on her face twisted into something more terrifying—a lovestruck smile so crazed and predatory it sent chills down Akira's spine.
He watched in horror as Loki's flushed face slowly advanced toward him, the stench of alcohol trailing ominously in the air. Her lips edged dangerously close to his.
At first, Akira restrained himself from reacting too strongly. He was afraid of hurting her in her drunken state.
But when Loki's pursuit showed no sign of stopping and in fact, only intensified—he finally snapped.
"LET ME GO, YOU CRAZY BITCH!!!"
BANG—!!!
A thunderous impact echoed across the room.
"AAAHH!!"
With a shriek, Loki was sent flying like a human cannonball, her petite frame crashing headlong into the unsuspecting dwarf nearby.
Akira stood there, gasping. His chest heaved with every breath, and his right fist trembled slightly in the air—still extended from the devastating punch.
Finn, Riveria, and Ais stared blankly for a few heartbeats, stunned into silence. None of them had processed what had just occurred.
It wasn't until Loki lay groaning on the ground, a swollen cheek rapidly forming, that the others snapped back to their senses.
Riveria immediately rushed to tend to the injured goddess with a resigned sigh, while Finn and Ais hurried to Akira's side, offering words of comfort.
Trying to pretend the incident never happened, Akira averted his gaze from the drunken mess on the floor and cleared his throat.
"Speaking of which, our familia's heading out on an expedition tomorrow. How about letting Ais join us?"
His gaze shifted to the blonde girl standing beside Riveria. "After all, you probably wouldn't want her going too deep into the dungeon on her own."
Riveria and Finn exchanged thoughtful glances.
Finn crossed his arms. "It's possible… but would that burden you?"
Riveria reached out and pinched Ais's cheek affectionately. "You know, this girl tends to be impulsive. She might end up causing you trouble."
"Uuu… I won't anymore, Riveria." Ais grumbled softly, puffing her cheeks in mild protest.
Akira chuckled and patted her golden head gently. His voice lowered as he said with a tender smile, "It's alright. I'll take care of Ais. And Ais, you'll listen to me, right?"
Ais nodded fervently. Her wide eyes shimmered with a mix of anticipation and anxiety, clearly terrified they might still say no.
"Mm! Yes! I'll be really, really obedient!"
Her earnest reaction made Finn laugh. He turned to Riveria with a persuasive smile.
"See? Ais really wants to go, and she'll be in good hands. With Akira around, what could go wrong?"
Riveria let out an exasperated sigh and looked away. "Hmph. When did I say I didn't agree? Honestly…"
Yet despite her grumbling, her expression was impossibly soft, her eyes filled with a warmth that showed her affection for the girl.
Ais instantly threw her fists into the air and shouted with joy, "Yay! That's great!"
Akira laughed. "Alright, then let's meet tomorrow at Stardust Garden."
Later that night, as he stepped out of the grand doors of the Twilight Manor, Akira raised a hand to his flushed cheek. He could still feel the lingering warmth from the fruit wine.
"Damn it... I don't want Astraea-sama to find out I drank." He muttered.
As if reacting to his concern, the magic power inside his body surged like a river unbound. The energy coursed rapidly through his limbs, purging every trace of alcohol from his system.
In just a blink, the flush on his cheeks faded completely, as though a painter had brushed a fresh layer of white over his skin.
With a relieved sigh, Akira pulled out a delicate silver pocket watch from inside his coat. The glowing blue hands of the watch pointed to a time already well into the night.
"Wow… It's really late. And I'm so tired after all that... Let's head home."
Yawning broadly, he stretched his arms and ambled down the streets with lazy steps.Thᴇ link to the origɪn of this information rᴇsts ɪn NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
Though darkness cloaked Orario, North Street remained lively. Most of the passersby were adventurers or shopkeepers locking up for the day.
In the distance, Akira imagined the lively bustle at the Hostess of Fertility, packed with adventurers laughing, drinking, and bragging about their latest exploits.
Roughly ten minutes later, after navigating several winding alleys and turns, Akira finally arrived at his home—a splendid villa not as grand as Loki's castle, but still luxurious and spacious beyond normal standards.
He slipped the key into the lock, the door swinging open with a satisfying click. He stepped inside, ready to bathe and crash into bed.
But just as he reached for the lock, a soft, familiar voice called from behind.
"You're back. Did you have fun at Loki's place, Akira?"
Startled, Akira froze.
Turning around, he saw a breathtaking sight illuminated by the soft glow of a magic stone lamp.
Astraea stood a few steps away, her figure bathed in gentle light. Her face was serene, radiant as starlight, and more beautiful than the night sky itself.
Akira gulped and replied softly, "Yes. I had a lot of fun. I got to know more of Loki Familia's members… made a few friends, I think."
After securing the door, he tiptoed toward her and lowered his voice, asking in a sheepish tone, "Has Astraea-sama not gone to sleep yet?"
She smiled at him, that divine expression like a blossom blooming quietly in the spring.
"Hmm~ You're leaving on an expedition tomorrow, aren't you? If I don't take a good look at my Akira tonight, I'll feel so lonely while you're gone~"
She blinked at him, her eyes gleaming with affection and playful longing.

chapters.title: Chapter 102 - 102: Goodnight Kiss
chapters.content:
Akira took a deep breath, steadying the emotions that stirred quietly in his heart.
He walked forward with light steps and gently took the magic stone lamp from Astraea's hand. Without hesitation, he naturally intertwined his fingers with hers.
Their palms pressed together with a quiet intimacy, as if their hearts had long since come to a silent agreement.
A faint, contented smile rose on Akira's lips as he spoke softly, "Is that so? Then... will Astraea-sama be staying in my room tonight?"
A playful glint flashed in Astraea's eyes as she teased with a charming giggle, "Oh my, it seems my little Justice has missed sleeping in my arms."
She said, "Alright, I'll spoil you tonight. Let's sleep in your room together."
She said it so nonchalantly, as if sharing a bed was the most natural thing in the world for a goddess and her beloved child.
Then, as if remembering something, Astraea tilted her head curiously and asked, "By the way, did you make any new friends at the party?"
"Yeah… everyone was friendly. I made a lot of new acquaintances."
Akira pouted a little, clearly displeased. "But really, why does Astraea-sama still care so much? Aren't we already in a relationship?"
Hearing this, Astraea let out a laugh, light and melodious, echoing softly in the still corridor.
She leaned in playfully, winked, and said with mock mischief, "Fufu~ I was worried our cute little Akira would be too clingy and avoid making any new friends."
The corridor was quiet except for their voices and footsteps, which overlapped and echoed gently. The warmth between them spread in the silence like light from a flickering flame, soft and comforting.
Akira glanced sideways at Astraea walking beside him and muttered in a low voice, "I can make friends, you know… I just think too many friends are a hassle. I don't have the energy to deal with all of them."
They spoke casually as they reached Akira's room. In his right hand, he held the glowing magic stone lamp. In his left, he still held the soft hand of the goddess who had long taken residence in his heart.
Just as he was about to let go of her hand to open the door, Astraea took the initiative and reached out gracefully, pushing the door open with delicate fingers.
Once inside, Akira watched as Astraea elegantly sat down on the edge of the bed. Only then did he release her hand, walking over to the wardrobe and beginning to search for his pajamas.
After a moment, he found a soft, comfortable set and turned around. "I'll go take a shower first. I won't be long, Astraea-sama."
"Don't take too long. And be sure to wash thoroughly. Otherwise I won't let you into bed!" Astraea pouted playfully, though her teasing smile never left her face.
She waved him off like a mischievous wife seeing her husband off to his nightly bath.
Once Akira disappeared into the washroom, Astraea began to walk around the room with a hint of leisure in her steps. She went over to the bags in the corner, delicately lifted her skirt, and crouched gracefully to inspect the magic items within.
She picked up a few, one by one, inspecting them with mild curiosity, but quickly lost interest. Standing up, she wandered to the bookshelf, choosing a thick tome and flipping through its pages idly. However, the text didn't hold her attention for long, and her gaze gradually grew unfocused.
With a soft sigh, Astraea slid off her slippers and pulled back the cozy quilt of Akira's bed. She climbed in, curling up with a quiet vulnerability, her fingers clutching the fabric gently.
She stared at the door, quietly awaiting Akira's return.
A few minutes later, the door creaked open, and Akira stepped back into the room. He was drying his damp hair with a towel, his footsteps quiet. The moment he looked up, his gaze fell on Astraea lying beneath the covers, gazing blankly at the ceiling.
Her beautiful face was painted with a look of gentle loneliness, as if she were a goddess forgotten by the stars themselves.
Akira let out a low laugh. "So our goddess really can't bear to part with us, huh? It's only a few days of expedition, yet she looks like she's about to cry."
He sat on the edge of the bed, crossing one leg over the other and leaning slightly toward her. With a soft gaze, he looked down at Astraea, meeting her eyes directly.
A playful smirk appeared on his lips as he said, "Hehe… I never realized Astraea-sama was also a god who's afraid of being alone."
Astraea blinked in surprise, then slowly came back to herself. She reached out with a hand as fair as snow and gently caressed his cheek.
With a low murmur, she confessed, "It's true. Even I didn't expect that just a few days away from you could make me feel so… empty."
Her gaze softened, voice warm as she continued, "Ever since you joined our Familia, Akira… you've become like sunlight in the middle of a cold winter. Your warmth brings me happiness I didn't even know I needed."
"In all my long years, no one has ever given me such… beautiful moments."
Akira's heart trembled.
Astraea-sama… if you continue saying such things, I might never want to leave. I might abandon all other pursuits, and choose to stay in this tiny world beside you forever.
But I can't. I must become stronger—for your sake and mine—so that I can protect this happiness.
Thoughts raced through Akira's mind, but in the end, he reached out and gently placed his hand on hers, offering silent comfort.
"It's okay." He said softly.
"Astraea-sama is a good person. I promise… no matter how long it takes, whether it's a thousand years or ten thousand years… I'll always stay by your side."
"So… please don't feel lonely just because of a short separation."
His words were firm, yet tender.
Astraea giggled, pulling him into a tight embrace and burying him in her arms.
Her voice was warm and full of passion as she whispered, "I know… I believe in you, Akira. Because you are my star—my justice!"
"Mmmph… I get it, I get it! But if you squeeze me any tighter, I won't be able to breathe." Akira mumbled, patting her shoulder helplessly.
Reluctantly, Astraea loosened her grip and smiled playfully. "Really now… such a killjoy."
Seeing her regain her usual self, Akira breathed a sigh of relief. He climbed under the covers and quickly nestled against her side, drawn to her warmth like a child seeking shelter.
With a sleepy yawn, he murmured, "Now that Astraea-sama is back to normal… can I sleep? My eyelids are already about to fall."
Astraea rolled her eyes but didn't protest. Instead, she gently patted his back and said, "Okay, okay, sleep well."
But just as Akira was about to drift off, he suddenly reached out, wrapped an arm around her waist, and pulled her tightly into his embrace.
Before she could react, he lowered his head and gently kissed her lips—a light, fleeting touch.
"Hehe… that's my goodnight kiss." He whispered with a boyish grin.
Astraea blinked in surprise, then smiled softly as she looked at Akira's peaceful sleeping face. Her fingers gently traced the curve of his cheek.
"…Let me see you again, my child."
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 103 - 103: Akira is a Lolicon?
chapters.content:
The soft golden light of dawn filtered through the curtains, spilling warmth across the wooden floorboards.
The morning sun had just risen above the eastern horizon, painting the sky with hues of rose and amber. Its rays gently bathed the quiet city of Orario, and in a certain room of the Astraea Familia's home, another day was beginning.
The clock tower's long hand ticked slowly toward six. The bell had not yet rung, but within the room, a boy stirred.
"..."
Akira blinked open his eyes slowly, his vision still a little hazy. He groggily propped himself up with both arms, his body sluggish with leftover warmth from the bed.
The moment he sat up, he instinctively reached to his side—only to find it empty. His hand touched only the cool sheet beside him.
He squinted, temporarily blinded by the flood of light pouring through the window. His mind was foggy for a moment, but then clarity slowly returned.
"She must have gotten up early again..." He murmured to himself, his lips curving into a faint smile.
"Looks like Astraea-sama went to make breakfast."
His tone was gentle, filled with a warmth that he didn't even try to hide.ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ NovᴇlFɪre.ɴet
With a stretch and a yawn, he climbed out of bed. After hastily folding the quilt in a manner that could only be described as "functionally tidy," he walked over to the corner of the room to retrieve his equipment.
Within a few minutes, he was fully dressed and had fastened his sword to his waist. By the time he stepped into the kitchen, the scene was already lively.
The smell of fresh bread, eggs, and stew wafted through the air, and the members of the Astraea Familia were already seated around the table, chatting energetically.
Today was the start of their expedition, so everyone had risen earlier than usual.
"Good morning!" Akira greeted, sliding into his usual seat with a smile.
"Morning, sleepyhead." Lyra said teasingly, handing him a bowl of stew.
Akira tucked in immediately, chewing with delight as he glanced around.
After a few spoonfuls, he casually asked, "Alise, I was wondering—can we bring one more person on this expedition?"
The moment he spoke, the table stilled.
Alise paused with a piece of bread halfway to her mouth. She slowly chewed, swallowed, then gave Akira a suspicious look.
"Huh? What brought this on all of a sudden? Who are you trying to bring along? Someone from Loki Familia, perhaps?"
Akira grinned. He grabbed two pieces of bread—one long and one short—and raised them like puppets in the air, forming an exaggerated "V" shape with his arms.
"Bingo! You hit the mark in one go, Captain. She's from Loki Familia."
Alise gave a mock sigh and rolled her eyes, her lips twitching upward. "Tch, as expected of me. Such trivial matters are nothing to a genius captain like me."
At that moment, a palm smacked down on Akira's head with crisp precision.
Bonk!
Kaguya, with her usual stern expression, said coldly, "Stop playing with your food. Eat properly, and speak clearly."
Lyra guessed, "So, who is it from Loki Familia? Don't tell me it's that blonde girl? In terms of strength, she's the only one who's comparable to us."
Lyra leaned back in her chair, sipping her milk leisurely.
When Ryuu who was sitting next to Akira heard this , a hint of sourness appeared on her face but she quickly concealed it.
Then she agreed seriously, "Hmm... I wouldn't be surprised if it's her. Akira and she are pretty close. Weren't they exploring the dungeon together a lot recently?"
She glanced sideways at Akira casually but pointedly with her blue eyes and blinked
Everyone's eyes landed on Akira.
Unfazed, he finished the last of his stew and let out a small burp of satisfaction.
He dabbed his mouth with a napkin and replied simply, "It's Ais. She's not doing much lately since the Loki Familia doesn't have an active expedition plan, so I thought it'd be good to bring her along. She's strong and reliable. Plus... having more support never hurts."
Akira paused before adding with a grin, "Besides, we'll inevitably have to work with Loki Familia more in the future. Might as well build rapport early."
Noin leaned forward curiously, her eyes gleaming. "Ara~ When did you and Ais become so close, Akira? You sound like you're defending her."
Lyra chuckled darkly and folded her arms. "Heh... I see what's going on. Our Morning Star's upgraded a few levels and now his heart's not satisfied staying in one familia anymore. He's trying to expand his harem."
The table burst into laughter.
Even Astraea, who had been listening quietly with a serene expression, covered her mouth and chuckled like a mischievous girl.
Akira could only sit there, a stiff smile on his face, as dark lines slowly crept across his forehead.
"W-Wait, you're misunderstanding—!"
But no one paid him any mind.
Ryana propped her cheek up with one hand, eyes sparkling with mischief. "Now that I think about it... isn't that little war girl only about nine years old mentally? Akira, are you really going to pursue someone like that?"
Akira nearly spat out his tea. "It's not like that!"
As if that wasn't enough, Iska dramatically pointed her finger in the air. "Ah! Isn't she the one... you know, the one that the gods said... the, uh—what was it again?"
She froze, her face scrunching as she tried to recall.
Before she could finish, both Kaguya and Lyra echoed loudly in perfect unison.
"Lolita!"
The entire dining room erupted again. The girls roared with laughter, some banging the table, others wiping tears from their eyes.
Akira covered his face with both hands, now completely resigned.
"I-It's not what you think." He murmured pitifully, but his voice was completely drowned out by the chaos.
Indeed, he was the only male in the familia, surrounded by beautiful and powerful women. A blessing on the surface... but inside? It was a battlefield.
The ratio had always been skewed, and when surrounded by such overwhelming female presence, the man's words held no power.
Akira slumped over the table, his cheek pressed against the cool surface. His raised hand trembled before slowly falling limp to his side, defeated.
As if on cue, Maryuu leaned over from behind and mischievously tickled his ear, causing him to flinch.
Ignoring her antics, Akira sighed internally.
I thought I had finally risen above them... that I wouldn't be the butt of the joke anymore. But now... I'm the one being teased by everyone... again.
After what felt like an eternity of laughter, the room finally quieted down.
Akira sat up, ruffled his hair, and asked with exaggerated seriousness, "So, Captain... do you agree to let Ais join us?"
Alise smirked, her arms crossed. She then stood up, clapped her hands, and declared dramatically, "Since we've laughed so much this morning, I shall graciously forgive your decision to consult us after making the arrangement!"
Then she raised a finger.
"However! As punishment, and as compensation—everyone here gets to make Akira promise one thing!"

chapters.title: Chapter 104 - 104: Could This Be Jealousy?
chapters.content:
Hearing the ominous cheer from the group, Akira's eyes widened slightly, locking onto the smug, sinister grins plastered across the girls' faces. There was no mistaking it—the wolves had smelled blood.
He cursed inwardly, "Good fellows, you were waiting for me right here, huh? Truly impressive. I walked right into your trap without even realizing. I was careless... should've dodged."
But now that things had escalated to this point, he had no choice but to face it head-on. There was no escape. Only forward.
Accepting his fate with the kind of helpless bravery seen in martyrs and fools, Akira nodded slowly.
Then, putting on a mask of fake magnanimity and indifferent confidence, he said with forced calm, "Alright, alright... I get it. It's just a dozen requests. I accept. You have my word."
The girls exploded with joy.
"Ohhhhhh!" Cheers erupted like thunder.
The atmosphere grew even more spirited as the implications of Akira's agreement sank in. Mischievous smiles lit up the room like lanterns.
Lyra's lips curled into a devious arc. She gave a soft snort—twice, for emphasis—and said in a singsong voice, "Hmm~ Well, now that the decision has been made, you're not allowed to go back on your word, okay?"
She even winked at him, her gaze full of sly provocation. The glint in her eye said, "You asked for this."
Akira stared blankly at her, expressionless. But deep in his heart, he gritted his teeth and snarled silently, "One day… I'll make you cry under the sunrise to the sound of cicadas chirping. Then you'll know who's right and who's wrong."
As he was immersed in his quiet inner fury, Kaguya, standing elegantly to the side, gracefully raised her slender hand and gently covered her mouth with a long, flowing sleeve. Her narrow, mesmerizing eyes arched into a smile—but that smile didn't reach her pupils.
A cold, almost imperceptible gleam flickered in her gaze, like the flash of a blade drawn under moonlight.
And then she said, in an unhurried but bone-chilling tone, "If he dares to go back on his promise... then allow me to slice off his little finger with my blade... huhuhuhu…"
Her dainty giggle followed, refined and elegant. But it sent a shiver down everyone's spine.
Akira's lips twitched, a black line sliding across his forehead. His expression turned utterly speechless as he turned to stare at the usually composed Kaguya—who now looked like she had just stepped out of a murder mystery play.
Why is she suddenly acting like some psychotic yandere...?!
He sighed internally. Truly... helpless.
But before he could even process more of the psychological trauma, a subtle tremor rippled through the magical field enveloping the entire Stardust Garden. His expression shifted ever so slightly.
Two unfamiliar but refined magic power signatures had just entered the vicinity. They were approaching the gate steadily, their presence calm but commanding.
Riveria and Ais?
Akira raised both hands slightly, and with a smooth motion, began to retrieve the vast tide of magical energy that had been buried deep beneath the estate like a sea beneath a frozen surface.
Under his precise control, the enormous current gradually reversed direction, flowing back toward him like a mountain stream, before gently returning into the depths of his body.
He had deployed that magic purely for detection—he had no intention of overwhelming his guests. It was simply a subtle trick to confirm their arrival.
Now that he was certain, he casually pulled out a chair, stood up, and announced to the room with a hint of ease, "Looks like Riveria-san and Ais have arrived. I'll go open the door and bring them in."
The moment his words landed, the effect was instant and electric.
Ryuu and Celty, seated nearby, jolted up as if struck by lightning. Their reaction was so abrupt, it seemed almost comedic. Their faces filled with panic and nervousness as they cried out in unison.
"W-Wait, WHAT?! Princess Riveria's coming here?! We need to go greet her immediately!"
There was no time to finish their food. They practically flung their bowls aside and dashed toward the entrance like bolts of lightning.
Even among elves, Riveria's presence carried a weight that was difficult to describe. She was of the royal lineage—an elven princess whose bloodline resonated with ancient reverence. Most elves, even those who prided themselves on their independence, couldn't help but lower their heads before her.
Even half-elves like Ryuu and Celty felt an instinctual awe in her presence.Follow current novᴇls on
Riveria herself found such treatment exasperating. She detested being seen only as royalty, disliked the distance it placed between her and others. That was why she appreciated Akira's attitude—blunt, honest, and unaffected by her status.
So when Ryuu and Celty broke into a full sprint, leaving behind streaks of wind, Akira blinked a few times in confusion.
"Hey! Ryuu, I get it, you're fast, but Celty... aren't you a mage?! Since when do you run like that?!"
The two were already vanishing around the corner. Flustered, Akira quickly chased after them, shouting at the top of his lungs, "Hey—wait up! What's with you two?! Why are you running like the world's ending?!"
Asta looked at their receding vacks and said with a chuckle, "Even though Astraea-sama and Maryuu told me that Akira is a half-elf from another world… it's still hard to get used to how little respect he shows to the elven royal family."
Neze, standing nearby, nodded with a thoughtful expression. "Indeed. When you contrast Akira's casual demeanor with Ryuu and Celty's reverent panic… it does feel a bit surreal."
Over the past few days, with Akira's permission, Astraea had finally revealed his secret to the entire familia.
She explained that Akira wasn't just from another country or distant land—but from another world entirely.
He had come across the stars, across the boundary of time and space, farther even than the divine realm where the gods once dwelled.
At first, the girls didn't grasp the weight of that revelation. They thought it merely meant Akira had left his homeland behind.
But as the goddess detailed the nature of his journey, their eyes widened. Their hearts trembled.
He hadn't just left his home—he had been ripped from it. Thrown into a strange world, with no allies, no direction, and likely no way of ever going back.
The gravity of his reality hit them like a stone. Though they kept their expressions composed, not one of them left that conversation unaffected.
They each carried scars, yes—but Akira's loneliness… his displacement from everything familiar, from the very world he belonged to… that left a mark on them.
A quiet sorrow. A shared pain. And a growing desire to protect the boy who stood so strong, despite the loneliness he must have felt.
Just as those thoughts stirred among them, the front door opened and Akira returned, Riveria and Ais following closely behind.
The moment the two guests entered the hall, the idle chatter came to an abrupt halt.
Riveria took a step forward and bowed her head slightly. Her tone was calm, dignified.
"It's been a while, Goddess Astraea. And everyone... I'm pleased to see you all well."
Then, she turned to Ais, gently patting the girl's golden hair.
She lowered her head and said softly, "Ais, come now. Say hello to everyone. You know this much, don't you?"
Ais looked up at her, tugging nervously at the hem of Riveria's sleeve. Her golden eyes scanned the unfamiliar crowd. There were eleven people in front of her—every one of them watching her with curious, assessing, and subtly probing gazes.
Ais wasn't used to this. She wasn't good with crowds, let alone scrutiny.
But under Riveria's gentle prodding, she bowed slightly and said, her voice soft and a little flat, "Good morning, Goddess Astraea... everyone."
"Good morning!"
The Astraea Familia members echoed cheerfully, though several pairs of eyes remained locked on her.
Even though Ais had met Alise and a few of the others before, it was nothing like this. This time, it felt... overwhelming.
Their eyes weren't hostile, but they were intense. Ais felt small under their attention, and for the first time in a long while, she felt a flutter of anxiety. She edged closer to Riveria, as if her mentor's presence could shield her.
And beside her, Akira stood quietly, observing the room.
He noticed how several of his companions were looking at Ais. It wasn't malicious, but... the emotions behind those gazes were complicated.
And for reasons he couldn't fully explain, an odd feeling bloomed in his chest.
A strange, heavy emotion that made him narrow his eyes slightly.
Could this be... jealousy?

chapters.title: Chapter 105 - 105: The Mighty Astraea Familia
chapters.content:
Akira let out a soft sigh, as if surrendering to fate itself. He stretched out his left hand slowly, helplessly, and placed it in front of Ais.
His face carried a hint of resignation, and his voice was gentle as he said, "Since we're heading on this expedition together, I suppose I should formally introduce them to you, Ais. I'm guessing you only remember a few… like Alise."
"Mm." Ais responded with a soft hum, her mood visibly lifting.
Without hesitation, she naturally reached out and held the hand offered to her.
Akira's helplessness deepened as he led her gently toward the crowd. His pace was steady, and at the same time, his eyes subtly scanned the gathered members of the familia.
His gaze was suggestive—firm yet wordless—signaling everyone to reel in their overly intense curiosity. After all, their unconcealed stares had already put the new girl visibly on edge.
Noticing Akira's silent cue, the ever-gentle and composed Maryuu took the lead. She stepped forward with a soft movement, crouching slightly so her gaze met Ais's at eye level.
With a kind smile blooming like spring flowers, she spoke warmly. "Hello, I'm Maryuu. If you get hurt during the expedition, just come find me, little Ais."
Seeing Maryuu take the first step to break the ice with the famed War Princess, the rest of the familia members quickly withdrew their probing gazes.
One by one, they stepped forward, introducing themselves with friendly smiles and welcoming gestures, their attitudes easing into genuine camaraderie.
Meanwhile, Riveria stood off to the side, engaged in a quiet conversation with Astraea and the veteran four-member group, carefully gathering every bit of information about the expedition's details.
From time to time, her eyes drifted toward Ais. Watching her once-reclusive pupil slowly beginning to blend into this unfamiliar crowd, Riveria finally relaxed her stiff shoulders. A breath of relief escaped her lips.
The Astraea Familia had long been known for their relentless dungeon expeditions. Much like other elite exploration-type familias, they frequently ventured into the deep floors of the labyrinth.
Though their numbers were few, each member was a seasoned warrior—an elite in their own right. Their battle records were astonishing.
They had successfully defeated floor bosses no less than twenty-one times. Truly, they were a group of terrifyingly capable girls—powerful and brilliant, their swords as radiant as their smiles.
Of course, the vast majority of those victories came against the infamous Goliaths.
And the reason was obvious: Goliaths regenerated quickly and dwelled on the shallower floors. All it took was a short wait of around two weeks before they could be challenged again.
Other floor bosses weren't so easy to deal with. Some took as long as a month to revive, while others required up to three long months.
The deeper the floor, the longer the wait and the more terrifying the enemies.
The areas themselves were daunting, and unless a large-scale expedition was mounted, simply encountering such powerful monsters was nearly impossible.
What made the situation even more intense was the sheer strength of the deep-floor bosses. Even the Loki Familia, one of the most powerful groups in all of Orario, chose to steer clear of certain foes rather than suffer unnecessary casualties.
That was exactly why Riveria was so meticulous in her information-gathering. She needed to clearly understand the Astraea Familia's goals for this expedition so she could provide sound strategic guidance and ensure Ais's safety.
There were only two particularly troublesome challenges ahead of them.
The first issue was the Guild's high expectations. So far, the deepest that the Astraea Familia had ventured in their previous expeditions was somewhere between the 25th and 33rd floors.Google seaʀᴄh ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
This time, the Guild hoped they could go even further—aiming to break through at least two or three more floors beyond their prior limit.
The second challenge was tied to finances and reputation. With the Loki Familia's generous 200 million Valis contribution now in the hands of Alise, their monetary problems had been solved.
However, Akira and the others had also taken on a number of commissions from familias whose goals weren't limited to dungeon exploration. These missions came with their own risks, and if they failed to deliver, it could tarnish the Astraea Familia's credibility as champions of justice.
After absorbing this information, Riveria frowned slightly and asked, "So this means… you'll need to pass through the 27th floor?"
"That's right." Alise replied coolly, arms crossed over her chest and wearing a confident smile.
"Unless something unexpected happens, our goal this time is to at least reach the 36th floor. If we're lucky, we might even peek into the upper edge of the 37th."
The idea of pushing into the 37th floor made Riveria narrow her eyes.
And there was good reason for that.
To even be allowed into the 37th floor by Guild regulations, a team had to meet stringent conditions.
A minimum of five members, all adventurers needed to be at least Level 4 and everyone's base stats had to be no lower than the D rank.
Unfortunately, the Astraea Familia wasn't quite there yet.
Among their ranks, nine were still at Level 3, while another three remained at Level 2. That alone made the idea of pushing into the 37th floor an extremely dangerous proposition—one that could easily end in tragedy.
Though Alise had ways of temporarily boosting her own level to 4 using her magic and unique skills, she understood all too well that such gains weren't sustainable.
Even with Akira—undoubtedly their strongest member—as their ace, and despite the existence of magic items that could teleport the party back to the surface in a pinch, Alise and the others were clear on one point.
Relying too much on Akira or those tools would inevitably erode their fighting spirit.
True strength wasn't measured by external aids. It came from one's own blood, sweat, and resolve—the ability to face adversity with nothing but a weapon and sheer will.
After pondering all of this, Riveria finally spoke, her tone even and measured. "Then… during this expedition, you'll likely encounter the floor boss on the 27th floor. It's due to reappear in the next few days."
The moment those words left her mouth, the atmosphere in the room shifted. Everyone turned serious.
The two-headed dragon of the 27th floor—if born in water—could unleash power equivalent to Level 6. That alone was enough to send chills down any seasoned adventurer's spine.
But Alise? She just laughed.
"Hahahahaha! That's true." She said, running a hand through the back of her fiery hair, her confidence radiating like sunlight.
"But the floor boss of the 27th floor is no big deal for us. With our current strength, we'll take it down easily. No need for you to worry, Riveria!"
Her bold declaration, laced with hearty laughter, seemed to pierce the heavy atmosphere like a ray of dawn. The tension that had crept into the room moments ago vanished almost immediately.
Riveria, struck by Alise's usual courage, couldn't help but let a small smile tug at her lips.
She gave a graceful nod and replied softly, "Then… it seems I truly have nothing to worry about."
(End of Chapter)
