chapters.title: Chapter 117 - 117: Beetle Swarm
chapters.content:
"Listen up, my friends! Our brave and fearless Astraea familia is about to set out on our journey once more."
Standing tall atop a large crystal, Alise raised her arm dramatically and declared with a voice full of vigor and pride.
"Our destination is one we've never reached before—the thirty-sixth floor, the end of the lower floors!"
"Ooooooh! Charge!"
"I'll do my best!"
"Captain Alise is so handsome!"
"Hahaha! You're absolutely right! Someone like me—naturally beautiful, clever, and brave—is, of course, extremely handsome!"ʀᴇᴀᴅ ʟᴀᴛᴇsᴛ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀᴛ NovᴇlFirᴇ.ɴet
Though her words were filled with playful bravado, her confident stance radiated an undeniable charisma that inspired trust and admiration in those around her.
Akira and the girls laughed, caught up in the cheerful atmosphere. Their banter and lighthearted jokes filled the air with warmth and camaraderie.
Even in this short reprieve, they adjusted their condition quickly. Once everyone had gathered the necessary supplies, they continued their journey forward.
Their next stop brought them to Rivira.
As planned, they retrieved large quantities of food and medicine from their pre-prepared supply stash, sorting them with practiced coordination.
When all was ready, Akira and the team charged forward again, without hesitation or delay.
Although the earlier part of the trip had only taken a few hours—thanks to the upper floors posing little threat—their real challenge was just beginning.
From here on, they needed to push through from the 18th to the 36th floor.
Each descent would cost time, energy, and resources, with no shortage of danger. Battles became frequent, and even with their strength, exhaustion gradually mounted.
The dungeon's walls had changed. Gone was the familiar rocky terrain—replaced by a strange border between worlds.
Towering trees stretched endlessly in every direction, with tangled branches creating confusing passageways above and below. The air was thick with the pungent stench of decaying wood, and a dense white fog cloaked the entire region, obscuring vision and swallowing sound.
There were no clear landmarks to guide them, and the vast forest seemed more like a twisting maze than a dungeon floor.
The ground was a poisonous swamp, forcing the group to stick to narrow, precarious tree paths.
In this alien world, danger lurked everywhere.
They could be facing enormous insects that looked like something out of a horror story, or swift jungle creatures that camouflaged perfectly in the mist.
Sometimes swarms of tiny monsters descended in overwhelming numbers, enough to make anyone's scalp crawl. Other times, elusive enemies took advantage of the fog to launch surprise attacks.
On the 21st floor, the group encountered such enemies again.
Akira was forced to use magic frequently to fend off cunning tapir bears that darted from the mist and targeted the rear-guard mages.
After dispatching another sneak attack, the group found themselves facing a new threat—an overwhelming swarm of wild, frenzied green beetles charging toward them at an alarming speed.
Amid the chaos, Ryana turned to the girl beside her and calmly instructed, "Celty, let's use magic together. Time it with me."
"Roaring, rising, coming from the source. Open the door, survival of the fittest, deep flame holding the jaws—devour it all!"
A glowing magic circle formed beneath Ryana's feet, responding to her invocation.
Holding her wand high, she began chanting. From the tip of her staff, a furious flame erupted—blazing and wild, like a fire dragon waiting to consume all in its path.
The magic circle's appearance underfoot signified the manifestation of her developed magic ability.
"I understand." Celty responded, a calm light in her eyes.
A matching circle glowed under her feet. Raising her staff, she aimed at the oncoming swarm.
Brilliant white light burst from the gem atop her staff, accompanied by a sharp crack of thunder. Forks of lightning—twisting and writhing like living serpents—danced through the mist.
"Hah!!" The two shouted in unison.
Ryana's flame shot forward in a wide column, and Celty's lightning wrapped around it like a glowing net, accelerating the combined spell into a devastating, spiraling blaze of fire and thunder.
BOOM! BOOM!!
The explosion rocked the forest.
The beetle swarm was obliterated instantly, disintegrated into tiny chunks that scattered like confetti in a storm.
The raw magic continued surging forward, tearing through the trees ahead. Flames roared. Bark blackened and cracked as several trees toppled under the impact, their branches crackling with residual sparks.
"Well done, you two!" Alise called out excitedly, her eyes gleaming.
Her beloved sword, Crimson Order, pulsed with radiant light. As she slashed the blade through the air, red arcs of energy flew forth, cleanly slicing apart any stray beetles that had escaped the blast.
With the path cleared, the group regrouped under Lyra's guidance and ran toward a massive tree trunk with a hollow in its base—that was the entrance to the next floor.
At the entrance of the 24th floor, everyone finally took a short breather.
Some stood, others slouched casually on the thick roots of the surrounding giant trees. All eyes turned toward Maryuu, waiting as she prepared to cast recovery magic.
"...Rea Vindemia!!"
As her chant concluded, a soft emerald glow erupted from Celty's staff, which Maryuu had borrowed. The healing magic spilled forth like a gentle spring breeze, wrapping around each member of the group.
Fatigue, aches, and pain dissolved with the warmth, as if sunlight had melted away the weight of battle.
"Mmm... as expected of Maryuu. That recovery magic really hits the spot." Lyra sighed contentedly, stretching her arms overhead.
"Haha, no, no. It's the only thing I can do," Maryuu said with a small smile. "I'm not as good in combat, so let me handle the healing."
She handed the staff back to Celty, then gripped her mace with both hands, her expression resolute.
Watching her quietly, Akira reached into his [Backpack] and retrieved a silver pocket watch. He glanced at the time, then turned to address the team.
"It's around 5 o'clock now. If we keep pushing, we can break through to the 25th floor and set up camp for rest."
"Got it. Everyone, you heard Akira!" Alise raised her sword high, rallying the group. "Hold on just a little longer—justice will prevail!"
"OOOHH!!"
The cry echoed through the forest.
Weapons in hand, spirits reignited, the Astraea Familia set off once more toward the ever-deepening unknown.

chapters.title: Chapter 118 - 118: Akira: Very Beautiful
chapters.content:
Bang!
Noin raised her small round shield, firmly blocking the Hobgoblin's heavy punch.
Not only did she block the force, but she also skillfully redirected it with her trained technique. In the same motion, she twisted her wrist and slashed out with her razor-sharp one-handed sword—swift and precise. The blade cut cleanly into the Hobgoblin's limbs, leaving no room for retaliation.
Then, with a light step, she retreated just in time to evade another heavy strike from a second monster closing in.
"Switch!"
"Leave it to me!" Neze's voice rang out confidently as she responded to the signal.
In the blink of an eye, wind magic surged into her palms, forming into twin whirling blades shaped like ferocious claws.
With explosive force, Neze kicked off the ground and launched forward like a flying arrow, closing the distance between her and the dazed Hobgoblin before it could react.
She crossed her arms and slashed diagonally, and—
Tear—!
A vicious ripping sound echoed through the dungeon as a massive spray of blood erupted from the Hobgoblin's torso, painting the surroundings red.
The Hobgoblin's body was instantly torn apart by the dual claws, so violently that even the magic stone within its chest was crushed to dust.
"Ohhh! As expected of Bloody Justice Fang. Nice work, Neze!"
That nickname, bold and fierce, was what people once called the werewolf girl in her early days.
Although Alise and the others thought it was super cool, Astraea—her patron goddess—had once been utterly mortified.
So much so that at the next Denatus, she personally pressured the other gods to change the alias to something more refined: Delta Virginis.
Supposedly, it referred to a red giant star in Virgo…
Before Noin could finish her enthusiastic praise, more trouble came charging straight at them.
"ROAR! ROOOOAR!!"
Two mammoth-like beasts stormed in from the distance, crushing roots and foliage underfoot, moving side by side in a full-body charge that cared nothing for obstacles or enemies.
Seeing the massive creatures approach, and sensing that many in the group were already growing fatigued, the rest of the team quickly parted to clear a path.
Asta, however, held her ground. She braced herself, raising her massive shield with both hands and intercepting one of the rampaging beasts head-on.
The impact pushed her back several steps, her boots dragging furrows in the soil. But she didn't falter. In that split-second window, she raised the axe in her right hand and brought it down hard on the mammoth's leg.
Thud!
The axe sank deep into the creature's leg, cutting through flesh and tendon and exposing gleaming white bone.
The beast screamed in pain. Its balance gave out, and it crashed to the ground in a thunderous heap.
At that moment, Akira appeared above it in a flash, leaping into the air and gathering wind magic into a swirling spiral sphere in his palm. With a twist of his body, he slammed it down—
Boom!
The attack landed on the top of the monster's head, silencing it instantly.
As for the second beast, it charged forward recklessly—only for Iska to leap like a dancer in midair, seizing one of its tusks with her nimble hands.
Using the creature's own momentum, she twisted and flipped her body, planting both feet against the side of its head in a devastating dropkick.
Wham!
The mammoth's head snapped sideways, its eyes spinning in disorientation. It stumbled, its legs tangling awkwardly beneath it, and finally collapsed in a heap.
That was when Kaguya made her move. Silent as a shadow, she emerged from the mist. In her hands, the crimson blade Higanbana gleamed wickedly.
With elegant precision, she slipped forward and sliced through the beast's skull, plucking out the core magic stone without a wasted motion.
As the battlefield fell quiet, Lyra unfurled a weathered map and pointed toward a branching path to the right.
"Go that way."
She said calmly. "Just a little further and we'll reach the entrance to the twenty-fifth floor."
Everyone nodded. Without a word, they picked up speed and followed the path Lyra indicated.
Minutes passed. The dense fog began to lift, and the blurred surroundings gradually came into focus.
But—
Something wasn't right.
Everyone stopped abruptly.
As if by instinct, they scattered and jumped back just in time.
Splurt!
A sticky, yellow liquid rained down from the treetops—viscous and reeking—splashing onto the spot they had stood moments ago.
It oozed like thick honey, slow and suffocating. From above, several massive deadly hornets buzzed out of their nest, filling the air with a piercing hum.
A pulsing, purple-black mass resembling a grotesque pinecone now blocked their path.
As Akira and the others glanced up, they saw the bark above peel away like dead skin, revealing the monstrous hive's true form.
This was no ordinary beehive. It was a nest intimately fused with the dungeon itself, allowing it to rapidly spawn deadly hornets.
And that sticky liquid?
Though it wasn't lethal, its terrifying viscosity could slow adventurers and worse, it acted as a tracking scent. Even a drop could mark someone, luring more deadly hornets from nearby hives like a curse.
In short, getting hit meant becoming prey.
"This is a pain!" Alise yelled, eyes lighting with resolve. "Fine then. Burn! Burn! Full flame power!!"
Without hesitation, she began chanting her strongest magic.

Before the hive could spawn another swarm, Alise's magic reached its peak.
BOOOOM!!!
A violent explosion tore through the air.
Flames erupted upward like a volcanic geyser, lighting the dim maze in brilliant crimson. The fire's roar shook the trees, and wind surged as sparks flew like fireworks.
To Akira, it looked like flowers blooming in the darkness—dangerous, beautiful, and unstoppable.
The stored-up magic burst forth in a dazzling blaze, igniting the air itself.
Crimson flames, the same hue as Alise's hair, surged around her limbs and wrapped tightly around her rapier.
In one fluid movement, she shot forward.
The ground cracked beneath her as she launched herself like a fireball, heatwaves trailing in her wake.
In the next instant, Alise was before the hive. With a shout, she swung the flaming blade down.
Crack!
The hive split in two.
Flames poured from the exposed core, roaring and devouring all. A thick stench of burnt insect flesh wafted out, sharp and pungent, overwhelming everyone's senses.
And yet, Alise wasn't finished.
As the hive began to collapse, she leapt atop it and used the rebounding force to flip backward, landing gracefully near Akira's side.
A split-second later—
KABOOM!
The hive exploded, engulfed in a sea of flame. Fire surged outward, consuming trees, roots, and everything else in its path. The dungeon floor shook from the force.
The group watched as the hive was reduced to ash.

Whether he meant the magic or something else entirely... no one could say.

chapters.title: Chapter 119 - 119: Dungeon Expedition? More Like a Vacation
chapters.content:
At the entrance to the 25th floor, the Astraea Familia prepared to establish their camp. The site they selected was tucked along a small offshoot path that deviated slightly from the main route—secluded, yet marked as safe.
After walking a bit farther down that narrow trail, they discovered a cave nestled at the base of the slope. Akira and the others decided to settle there for the night. According to the guild's maps, this location had long been designated as a potential resting spot on the 25th floor.
When an expedition team decides to rest in the Dungeon, the very first thing they must do is alter the terrain.
Using weapons, they smashed parts of the dungeon walls and floor—this trick forced the Dungeon to enter a repair state, halting monster spawns in the immediate area for a short period.
Next came the setup. A few members were posted at the cave's entrance and exit to guard against stray monsters wandering in. Meanwhile, Akira and a few others quickly eliminated the monsters already inside, clearing the cave of threats.
At the same time, others wielded axes and hammers to strike large cracks into the cave walls, reinforcing the "safety zone" effect.
Once all the monster bodies were dragged outside, Akira stepped forward and used water magic to cleanse the bloodstains from the cave floor. Afterward, a burst of fire magic quickly dried the moisture, leaving the space clean and dry.
With the base now secured, everyone jumped into action.
Akira, Alise, and Ryuu took turns guarding the cave entrance. Kaguya and the two elder sisters were responsible for tonight's dinner. The rest of the party moved efficiently to set up tents and organize their temporary base.
Thankfully, the Astraea Familia wasn't a massive group. A team of their size only required a few travel packs and with Akira's [Backpack], carrying essential supplies was far more convenient.
If this had been a massive expedition like the ones led by Loki Familia—with dozens of members—the very first step would've been building a fully functional base camp.
A group that large carried an enormous variety of supplies. If not meticulously organized and maintained, confusion and losses would become inevitable.
And with the amount of gear they brought, it all had to be securely loaded into solid, reinforced cargo crates to ensure stability, protection, and easy access during emergencies.
Fortunately, for this smaller party, everything moved smoothly.
After a flurry of activity, the tents were finally erected.
Standing proudly in front of their neatly arranged shelter, Lyra admired their work with a satisfied nod.
Then she turned toward the cave entrance and called out loudly, "Akira, take those things out."
Hearing the call, Akira stepped back into the cave, a slightly puzzled look on his face.
"Uh, what things? You know this backpack's stuffed full—how am I supposed to know what you're talking about?"
Lyra crossed her arms with a sigh and said matter-of-factly, "The weapon maintenance tools. Let's get everyone's weapons serviced before dinner."
"Oh, that's what you meant." Akira's eyes lit up with realization. He crouched down and began rummaging through his [Backpack].
Moments later, he pulled out a full set of weapon maintenance gear—whetstones, polishing powder, clean cloths, and a few other handy supplies.
Although Lyra wasn't a professional blacksmith, she had a thirst for knowledge and enjoyed learning new skills. Weapon maintenance, bomb-crafting, and a dozen other survival tricks were all part of her growing arsenal.
Once everyone's weapons—Ais's included—had been checked and serviced, a delicious aroma wafted through the air.
Kaguya's dinner was ready.
Maryuu arrived with a tray of steaming food and laid it on a makeshift table conjured by Akira's ice magic. Although it appeared to be made of ice, Akira had neutralized the chill, leaving it with a smooth, stone-like texture.
It was solid, comfortable, and surprisingly luxurious.
At that moment, Noin lounged back in her ice chair, a wide grin of satisfaction on her face as she stretched her limbs and let out a contented sigh.
"Mmm~ this is so nice. Ever since Akira joined, our expeditions have felt like luxury retreats. Best decision ever!"
After all, before Akira joined, they had been eating while squatting on the cave floor.
Seated beside her, Neze nodded in agreement. She stared curiously at the translucent tabletop, reached out, and gently ran her hand across the surface.
"Right? Honestly, I never thought I'd be this comfortable while deep inside the Dungeon."Follow current novels on NovᴇlFɪre.nᴇt
Their words brought chuckles and smiles from the others. Spirits were high as everyone sat around the table and dug in.
Kaguya had prepared a dish from the Far East: a salted rice porridge topped with golden egg drops, shredded meat, diced vegetables, and bits of dried fruit. The scent alone whetted everyone's appetite.
Soft bread, golden-crusted steak, and glasses of chilled juice completed the spread.
For a brief moment, the girls forgot they were in the middle of an expedition.
Alise inhaled her bowl of porridge at lightning speed. Her cheeks flushed, and she mumbled through a mouthful of food, face filled with childlike bliss.
"Mmm~ it's delicious! So good! Hot food after a workout... I need another bowl!"
At her words, the others reflexively began eating faster—no one wanted to miss out on seconds.
Meanwhile, Akira sat at the edge of the table, idly chewing as he looked up and asked casually, "By the way, does anyone feel like taking a bath tonight?"
Asta, caught off guard by the question, blinked a few times and tilted her head. "Huh? There's a pool nearby? If I have to run all the way to the waterfall, forget it. That's way too far."
Akira waved his hand and pointed toward the vacant patch of land beside the cave.
"No need to go through all that trouble. We'll just dig a hole over there."
Everyone turned to stare at him, baffled.
"Dig... a hole?"
Confusion was written across every face.
Even if they dug a hole, how were they supposed to fill it? Water wasn't exactly infinite on expeditions.
Kaguya narrowed her eyes and said bluntly, "If you've got a plan, spit it out already."
Akira set down his bowl, crossed his arms confidently over his chest, and gave a smug little grin.
"Hehehe... would you girls like to soak in a nice, relaxing hot spring tonight?"
"Hot spring!?" The entire group's jaws dropped in shock.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 120 - 120: Making a Hot Spring
chapters.content:
Noin, who had never shown a shred of shyness in front of Akira, immediately cheered and waved her arms excitedly.
"Hey, Akira! What are you going to do? As long as there's a hot spring to bathe in, I don't mind bathing together with you."
Several of the girls laughed and nodded in agreement, though despite her bold claim, Noin's expression showed her true feelings. Her cheeks flushed a brilliant red, like ripe apples, and her eyes flitted around nervously, unable to meet Akira's gaze.
"Well, let Akira finish his meal first." Maryuu said gently with a smile, trying to calm the atmosphere before it got too chaotic.
"I'll say this in advance."
Akira added, raising a hand as he finished chewing his food, "The water's going to be made from my own magic power, so, uh… don't be grossed out."
...
Once dinner was over, Akira checked his pocket watch. The hands pointed to eight o'clock.
He stood and walked over to the open area beside the camp, wind magic swirling faintly around his hands. He raised his right arm like a blade and drove it straight into the ground.
With the windstorm twisting violently, the earth tore apart under its force. A square pit, three meters wide, quickly took shape under Akira's precise control.
Then, placing both hands on the edge of the pit, Akira released a surge of magic. The energy flowed outward and crystallized, forming a hard, glossy surface that spread evenly to line the bottom and sides.
But he didn't stop there.
A stream of crystal-clear water gushed from his palm, rapidly filling the newly formed pool. Once it reached the appropriate depth, Akira shifted his elemental control to fire, subtly heating the water's temperature.
He even tapped into the natural ground fire beneath the dungeon, igniting a low but steady flame under the hot spring to maintain an ideal warmth.
Steam slowly rose from the surface of the pool, the area now glowing softly in the dim torchlight.
When the final magical adjustments were complete, Akira turned around with a satisfied smile. The girls' eyes sparkled with anticipation.
"It's done. Go enjoy it." Akira said calmly, brushing his hands. "I'll be on guard outside."
He turned to walk toward the cave entrance, but before he could take more than a few steps, he felt two soft tugs at his arms.
He blinked and looked down—only to find Alise clinging to one side and Kaguya to the other. The girls behind them exchanged sly smiles, their intentions clearly written in their eyes.
Alise grinned mischievously, while Kaguya—though looking mildly annoyed—was clearly playing along.
"Eh?" Akira tilted his head slightly, confused. "Is there something wrong with the hot spring?"
Alise's lips curved into a dazzling smile. Her bright, expressive eyes shimmered with mischief.
"Nope, the hot spring's perfect!" She chirped. "But... this time, we've decided—you're joining us!"
Akira's eyes widened slightly. He looked toward Kaguya, half-expecting a sharp rebuke or a joking punch.
But instead, Kaguya raised an eyebrow and smirked. "Hmph. I just think it'd be unfair for you to miss out after setting everything up. Consider it a reward."
"Uhh… but…"
"Don't worry. We'll wear our towels properly. Right, everyone?" Alise winked and lightly patted Akira's chest to reassure him.
The rest of the girls chimed in with smiles and nods, their expressions innocent but filled with teasing delight.
Trapped between two determined beauties, Akira could only sigh in defeat and nod reluctantly.
Before entering the spring, he conjured a thick black mist barrier at the edge of the area. From the outside, it appeared like a dense wall—perfect for shielding their activity.
More importantly, it served a second purpose.Nᴇw ɴovel chaptᴇrs are published on NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
Monster deterrence.
While not universal, many dungeon creatures reacted with greater hostility toward unnatural light sources or changes in scenery—especially ones that glowed or flickered like flames or magical barriers. This curtain of mist would help mask the unusual activity and keep most threats at bay.
Inside the tent, the girls had already begun undressing, chatting and giggling as they wrapped themselves in towels.
Maryuu's gaze drifted quietly to Ais, who was slowly peeling off her outer layers with a blank expression, showing no signs of embarrassment.
"…Ais-chan." Maryuu asked softly, a hint of concern in her voice. "Are you really okay with Akira seeing you while we're bathing?"
Wrapped in a white towel, Ais lifted her head and looked at Maryuu with a tilt of her head. Her golden eyes were filled with childlike confusion.
"Akira… it's fine." She replied plainly.
It was as if the question itself didn't make sense to her.
Maryuu blinked, clearly taken aback by the blunt honesty.
Standing nearby, Ryana chuckled and reached out, gently ruffling Ais's hair. "Hehe, I don't understand how you two got so close."
Ais smiled faintly and replied, "Because Akira can use wind… and he teaches me to grow stronger."
"Eh? That's all?" Ryana laughed again.
She didn't understand the connection between those statements, but even so… she could tell that Ais genuinely liked Akira.
Meanwhile, outside the tent, Akira stood silently as steam from the hot spring curled into the air.
The magical lights within the tent illuminated the silhouettes of the girls behind the curtain. Their soft outlines flickered gently through the mist—smooth curves, graceful movements, and slender limbs danced before his eyes like a mirage.
The playful sway of their towels, the faint giggles, the delicate contours…
Akira gulped. His thoughts blurred for a moment before he mentally slapped himself back to clarity.
Are they really that unguarded? No… calm down. This is just an ordinary bath. Ordinary…
Still, as he stood guard, his heart couldn't help but whisper.
It's great to be part of the Astraea Familia. Thank you for the hospitality.
The hot spring wasn't massive, but it was spacious enough to comfortably fit thirteen people if they sat shoulder to shoulder.
After making sure the mist shield was secure, Akira wrapped a towel around his waist and entered the warm water.
Steam rose all around, and the soft red glow of Kaensekis reflected off the water's surface.
The girls had already taken their seats. Their faces relaxed, glowing with joy, laughter echoing gently through the cave.

chapters.title: Chapter 121 - 121: Enjoying Sake in The Hot Spring
chapters.content:
The water temperature of the hot spring was just right—neither too hot nor too cool. The moment the body gently slid into the soothing water, a wave of warm energy surged through the limbs, spreading rapidly through every muscle, every fiber, every cell.
A sense of melting relaxation blanketed them all.
Steam coiled upward in lazy spirals, curling around their faces like a fine, translucent veil. It softened their surroundings, turning the world into a hazy dreamscape. The dim lighting, the gentle sound of bubbling water, the faint fragrance of minerals—it was like a brief escape from the dungeon's constant tension.
Through this mystical layer of mist, Akira beheld a scene so surreal it might as well have been a painting.
Right before his eyes, Alise was draped languidly over the edge of the spring, her back arched slightly out of the water. Her bare skin gleamed pale under the glow of magic light—soft, smooth. Not the slightest effort was made to hide it from Akira's sight.
Her cheeks, flushed from the heat, added an intoxicating charm to her dazed expression.
"Hahh… This is heavenly." Alise murmured in bliss, her voice dreamy and muffled as her body slowly sank deeper into the spring. "It's like… all the exhaustion of the day just disappeared into the steam…"
Not just Alise—one after another, the rest of the girls eased into the embrace of the spring, letting themselves melt into relaxation.
Every so often, someone would let out a satisfied moan or sigh, completely absorbed in the moment.
Only Kaguya and the two older girls kept their graceful posture, sitting upright and composed.
Meanwhile, Ais, who was notoriously afraid of water, sat obediently on the step Akira had specially raised for her, her towel neatly wrapped around her tiny frame.
Beside Alise, Noin mumbled with a lazy smile, "Yeah… I feel like I could just fall asleep right here."
She yawned, long and loud, eyelids drooping as though she might actually doze off at any moment.
At that moment, Kaguya scooped up a handful of steaming water and watched it slip through her fingers. The ripple of the surface reflected the soft light, casting playful shadows on her expression. Then, as if reminded of something, she turned to Akira—who sat with his eyes closed, basking quietly in the warmth.
Her voice was soft but clear. "Come to think of it, it's not complete without something else. Akira, help me get the sake I brought this morning."
It was a small request, yet it added a luxurious touch to their indulgence.
Truthfully, if not for the recent system update that greatly expanded the storage slots in Akira's [Backpack], it would've been impossible to bring so many miscellaneous items on this expedition.
They'd already packed quite a bit.
Hearing Kaguya's request, Akira gave a small nod. "Got it."
He raised a hand and made a grasping motion in the air. Instantly, a beautifully carved glass bottle materialized in his palm.
He stood and walked toward Kaguya with light steps, but before he could reach her, Maryuu shifted slightly to the side and patted the empty space beside her with a warm smile, motioning for him to sit down.
Akira hesitated, a bit overwhelmed by the invitation but it was hard to refuse.
So, after a small pause, he squeezed into the space between Maryuu and Kaguya, carefully settling in.
As soon as he sat down, the warmth of two soft bodies pressed against him from both sides. The sensation was… distracting. His heartbeat quickened, and he had to consciously calm his breathing.
Trying not to focus on it, he handed the sake bottle to Kaguya.Follow current ɴᴏᴠᴇʟs on N(o)vᴇl(F)ire.nᴇt
She took it casually and raised her voice slightly, "Hey, anyone else want a drink?"
Akira reached into his [Backpack] again and pulled out a set of small, elegant wine glasses, placing them gently on a floating tray he had conjured beside the spring.
"I'll drink! No way I'm missing out on sake in a hot spring!"
"Me too! Pour me a cup!"
The voices of agreement rang out enthusiastically.
Ryuu, on the other hand, stared wide-eyed, utterly baffled. "Wait… Kaguya, you actually asked Akira to bring sake? Seriously? We're on an expedition."
Her disbelief echoed through the mist.
Kaguya chuckled, her tone playful. "Come on, don't be so uptight. It's just a little sip to relax. Won't affect our performance."
Watching the scene unfold, Lyra sighed with a tired smile. "Unbelievable. You're all too carefree. Enjoying the start of the expedition like this…"
Alise, previously melting from relaxation, instantly snapped back to her usual lively self.
She clapped Lyra on the back and laughed boisterously, "Hahaha! It's fine! Just a little drink before bed—what's wrong with that? Don't tell me you don't want a glass."
"…I never said that." Lyra reached out and accepted a cup, her expression reluctant but her hand steady. "Just a small amount. I don't want my sharp mind turning as soft as Alise's."
"Hah?! That's rude! I'm plenty smart, thank you very much!" Alise shouted, raising her cup with pride. "Definitely smarter than Ryuu!"
"Hey—Alise! Why are you always dragging me into this!?" Ryuu snapped, her composure cracking at last.
She had tried her best to ignore the bathhouse chaos and just enjoy the peaceful water, but Alise's jab hit her pride like a hammer. Her ears turned red.
"For the record—I am not an idiot!"
"Yeah, sure." Akira chimed in from the middle, smirking. "If I hang around Ryuu long enough, I'll turn into a moron myself."
"Hah!? Are you serious, Akira?!"
"You won't really become dumb, right?!"
"…"
Laughter echoed off the cave walls, bright and carefree.
Even though they were deep in the dangerous and unpredictable dungeon, for this one fleeting night, joy filled the atmosphere.
After soaking to their hearts' content, it was finally time to settle down.
They moved to decide on sleeping arrangements.
There were four tents, each capable of holding four people—but with thirteen members, the math was simple.
Akira would have no tent to himself. And so, inevitably, he had to share with three girls.

chapters.title: Chapter 122 - 122: Tent Allocation
chapters.content:
Seeing the complicated expressions on the girls' faces, Akira raised a hand to his forehead and sighed deeply, his voice laced with helplessness.
"What are you all imagining now? We have enough tents, okay? And don't forget—we're still on an expedition."
As he spoke, he gestured toward the nearby dungeon walls, where the mossy surface was slowly being restored by the dungeon's automatic regeneration.
"And if none of you want Astraea Familia to go down in history as the first to be crushed to death by a collapsing wall mid-expedition, then someone better keep destroying these walls regularly."
"Ah! I completely forgot about that. Ahaha…" Alise laughed awkwardly, scratching the back of her head, her eyes darting sideways in embarrassment.
Aside from the two well-known captains—Alise and Kaguya—if there were a third in charge, it would undoubtedly be her…
The werewolf, Neze, nodded seriously with a rueful smile. "Yeah… I honestly forgot too. But that's because Akira's been doing way too much today. He's covering for all of us."
Kaguya stood silently beside them. Though her expression remained composed, a small voice in her heart wondered if she, too, had ended up becoming a fool like Alise.
"…Indeed." Kaguya finally turned, her voice quiet, as if reluctant to admit it.
Then Noin dropped to her knees dramatically, lifting both hands in a prayerful gesture. "Ahh! Almighty Akira, you must have another miraculous idea, right? Save us again, please?"
Everyone's eyes turned toward him, glittering with anticipation and shameless expectation.
Do you all think I'm Doraemon or something…?
Akira sighed inwardly but shrugged. "It's possible. But that means I'll have to sleep right in the middle of the storm tonight."
He lifted both hands, showing them empty palms.
"And I can't guarantee that nothing in the dungeon will change overnight. So I'll stay on watch. I'm not planning to take it easy tonight."
"That won't do," Maryuu said gently, her tone warm but firm. "If someone has to stand guard, then we'll set a rotation. You don't need to do it alone."
"Right! Akira's already done enough today. Just leave the final shift to us." Alise added, puffing up her chest with conviction.
Everyone nodded in agreement.
But then, as if a mischievous spark had been lit, Alise's eyes gleamed, and her tone took on a playful lilt.
"Say, Akira… who are you planning to sleep with tonight?"
The atmosphere shifted instantly.
The previously calm and orderly group fell into silence, eyes turning toward Akira like wolves smelling blood. Their gazes sparkled with mischief and curiosity, their lips twitching with suppressed laughter.
A bead of sweat slid down Akira's temple.
"In the end, we're back to this again." He sighed internally. "These girls really enjoy teasing me."
After a moment of consideration, he pointed calmly toward Lyra, Ais, and Asta.
"I'll be in a group with them."
"Eh?! Why?" Alise yelped, dramatically pointing at herself. "Shouldn't you choose me, your lovely, beautiful captain?!"
"You're too troublesome." Akira replied flatly.
"Wha—!?"
Alise's eyes widened in disbelief, her mouth falling open. It was as if she'd been struck by lightning.Thɪs novᴇl(ꜰ)ire.ɴet
Then, her body began to stagger backward like she'd taken a fatal wound.
"Ah… My heart… It's breaking…"
She stumbled dramatically, swaying on her feet, muttering incoherent words like a tragic heroine in a play.
With a final sigh, she collapsed into a nearby chair, clutching her chest with both hands.
"This… is this what it feels like to be abandoned by the man you love? The pain… It's unbearable…"
Akira stared at her performance in deadpan silence, his lips twitching slightly. Then he turned away and pretended not to see it.
Kaguya, unamused, stepped forward and said calmly, "Leave the night watch to me, Alise, and Ryuu. The next rotation will go to the other three. That way, no one's overworked."
Ryuu nodded with a serene expression. "Yes. The rest of you can get some proper rest."
With that, the rest of the group relaxed visibly.
"Ohh! Got it. We'll sleep first then. You three, be sure to keep watch properly."
Everyone began to break off into their respective groups, heading toward their tents.
Akira waved at the night watch trio with a smile. "Good night."
Just then, a sly whisper brushed past his ear.
"So… Akira's got a lolita complex, huh? Right, Asta?" Lyra's teasing voice drifted beside him, her elbow nudging the girl beside her as they walked.
Asta paused, eyes rising to glance at the taller girls, a faint trace of bitterness in her gaze. She mumbled softly, "…Maybe Akira thinks we're smaller, so it's easier to fit us into the same tent?"
Lyra waved a hand dismissively, wearing a carefree grin. "Ah, don't take it so seriously! We're both fully formed now. And let's be honest—there's no hope of us getting any taller at this point."
Her words, though seemingly intended to console, sounded more like a teasing jab.
Akira, hearing this, blinked in confusion.
Wait… was that really meant to comfort her?
Still, he said nothing. Instead, he quietly took Ais's small hand—her face a little flushed from excitement—and gently moved beside Asta.
"It's fine, Asta. Being petite has its own charm." Akira said warmly. "Besides… you've got a great figure. Lots of people would love someone like you."
Then his eyes shifted subtly to Lyra.
"As for Lyra…"
Their eyes locked. In Akira's gaze, an unspoken message lingered: Besides me, no one would put up with you.
Asta giggled, brushing away her moment of insecurity. "Hehe, so that's what Akira thinks of me… Thanks for the compliment. But Lyra's really popular too."
Lyra lifted her chin proudly. "See? I'm popular too."
But then, as their gazes crossed again, Lyra narrowed her eyes and licked her lips slowly, as if conceding something silently.
Fine. I'll let you have this one.
"Yeah, yeah… If not for a certain someone, maybe no one would like a short, skinny pallum like me. Isn't that right, Akira?"
Her teasing words carried a faint edge of challenge.
Akira grinned and answered in a dramatic tone, "Ahahaha, come now. The infamous 'Cunning Rat' is plenty famous. There's bound to be someone who likes her."
Hearing that, Asta chuckled and gently took Lyra's hand while still holding onto Akira's.
"You two really get along, don't you?" She said with a laugh.
As they stepped into the tent together, Asta released their hands and flopped onto the mattress. Her expression turned thoughtful.
"No, wait. Actually… I think Akira gets along best with you, Alise, Kaguya and Ryuu. Is it because you saved him before?"
She looked up with wide, curious eyes, her head tilted slightly.
(End of Chapter)

chapters.title: Chapter 123 - 123: Naughty Activities
chapters.content:
The question made Akira and Lyra look at each other, then they slightly turned their heads away and said in a brisk tone, "That should be it."Follow current novᴇls on ɴoᴠel Fɪre.nᴇt
Watching the two people's performance, Asta seemed to have a flash of enlightenment, and said with a smile, "Oh, I understand, so that's how it is."
Then she didn't say what she understood, and got into bed. She patted the place next to her and said to Ais, "Ais-chan, can you sleep next to me?"
"Well... I can, but I want to sleep next to Akira." Ais looked at Akira expectantly.
Now, the three of them looked at Akira.
Akira thought, 'Why do I feel like everyone has been staring at me since I joined the expedition?'
Akira reached out and touched Ais's head, and said gently, "Next time, you can sleep next to me when it's time to go to bed."
"I understand." Ais nodded slightly frustrated.
She clenched her hand, let go and crawled into the quilt next to Asta.
When Akira and Lyra were about to lie down to rest, Asta suddenly gave them a meaningful smile, which instantly made them feel uneasy and sweaty.
After a while, the surroundings gradually became quiet, and the only sound left was the even and subtle breathing of others.
Akira carefully raised his hand and reached for the magic stone lamp in the corner of the tent. He pressed it lightly and the light suddenly went out.
In an instant, the entire tent was shrouded in darkness, with only a tiny ray of light coming through from the campfire outside, bringing a faint glow to the darkness.
Listening to the intermittent, slight and fine cutting sounds outside, as if it were a lullaby, gradually, a strong sense of sleepiness surged into Akira's heart like a tide, and his eyelids became heavier and heavier. Finally, he could not resist the invasion of sleepiness and fell asleep.
Time passed little by little, and except for Alise and the other two, everyone else seemed to have fallen asleep. All that could be heard was the breathing and the occasional sound of turning over.
At this moment, there was a rustling sound next to Akira, and then a soft and warm body crawled into his arms, causing him to open his eyes suddenly and slightly lift the quilt.
Looking at the petite body in his arms, Akira said in a soft voice, "It's so late, what else do you want to do, Lyra?
Hearing this, Lyra not only did not retreat at all, but instead held Akira's arm even tighter, then slowly climbed up his body, and did not stop until she was shoulder to shoulder with Akira.
She lowered her voice and replied, "Of course I came to make out with you. Now that everyone is asleep, isn't this the best time?"
Obviously, once Lyra finds an opportunity that is beneficial to her, she will never let it go easily, but will take the initiative without hesitation.
"Can't we do this when we get home?" Akira put his arms around Lyra's slender waist, fearing that she would make some noise due to excessive movements.
However, at this moment, what made Akira feel a little embarrassed was that Lyra's soft chest was constantly rubbing against his chest, giving him a strange touch.
Although Lyra had previously commented that her figure was a little thin, in fact, for a pallum like her, this size was already quite good.
After all, Lyra had a very miserable childhood, and going hungry was a common thing for her. If she hadn't been malnourished for a long time, maybe she could have grown to the same size as Alise.
Lyra, whose whole body was pressed tightly against Akira, suddenly felt a hard sensation in her abdomen and lower body.
After a brief thought, she naturally understood what this meant in an instant.
Thus, in this pitch-black environment, a smile as brilliant as a flower quietly emerged on Lyra's pretty face unconsciously.
Then she whispered, "But now you can only look at me."
As soon as she finished speaking, Lyra's small hand gently slid across Akira's abdomen.
This sudden act of intimacy instantly gave Akira goosebumps all over his body. Even in the dark, he could clearly see Lyra's brilliant smile. There was nothing he could do.
After thinking for a moment, he lowered his head and kissed Lyra's red lips. After a long while, the two reluctantly parted their lips.
He looked at Lyra, who looked satisfied, and said, "That's all. Go back to your bed quickly. It will be hard to explain if someone sees you."
"What are you afraid of? You have such a good relationship with everyone. You don't have to worry that they will hate you." Lyra whispered in dissatisfaction, and then bit his face lightly.
'Oh, you are such a troublesome guy. I don't understand if you really want to have a harem? Can you be a little thicker-skinned? No one will laugh at you.' Lyra complained wildly in her heart.
Then, Lyra quietly reached for the handle with her right hand, and she clearly felt Akira's body suddenly stiffen.
Akira said in a shocked voice, "Lyra! What are you doing?"
As he spoke, he loosened his left hand that was hugging the slender waist and quickly grabbed the little hand that was doing something wrong.
"Of course it's a reward for you, for your initiative tonight and for making me feel that I am also attractive." Lyra replied in the face of Akira's surprise and obstruction.
Hmm...why can't other people hear their voices?
Of course, it's because the sounds made by Alise and the others damaging the dungeon are covering them up.
...
Under Akira's hopeless gaze, Lyra crawled slowly along the bed as if she had completed a difficult task, and finally returned to her own bed.
The corners of her lips slightly raised, and she smiled faintly at Akira, then she gently closed her eyes and fell asleep.
At this moment, Akira was the only one left, standing alone in a daze in the silent night.
Although the experience just now brought him an indescribable sense of comfort, he knew in his heart that his body did not seem to be fully satisfied.
This feeling of unfulfilled desire made him unable to calm down for a long time.

chapters.title: Chapter 124 - 124: Asta Knows
chapters.content:
Amid the rustling and bustling of morning activity, Akira slowly opened his eyes. A trace of fatigue lingered within them. With effort, he supported his body and sat up from his sleeping position.
Just the night before, he had lain there alone, thoughts surging within him like turbulent tides. After a prolonged period of silent self-adjustment, he had finally managed to calm his heart and drift into a restless sleep.
By the time he awoke, the other three who had shared the tent with him had already disappeared. Akira lifted the curtain of the tent gently and stepped out into the open.
Outside, the scene was already lively. The members of the Familia were busily packing their luggage, preparing for the descent to the next floor of the dungeon.
Akira moved toward the place where his toiletries were placed, bent down to pick them up, and squatted nearby to begin his morning wash.
Not long after, Akira returned and placed the utensils neatly back on the table.
Alise appeared, holding breakfast in her hands. She looked at him and teased, "Finally awake? It's rare for Akira to sleep in like this. Let me guess—not used to sleeping in the dungeon yet, right?"
She placed the food down with a soft chuckle. "It's okay. I was just like you when I first came down here."
"...That's right." Akira murmured after a pause, taking the breakfast.
He was silent for a moment before answering.
Can I say it was because of unfulfilled desires last night?
Alise walked over lightly, hands resting behind her slender waist, and leaned in close to Akira's face.
She observed him carefully, quickly picking up on the subtle signs of fatigue still etched into his expression.
Her tone turned gentle. "Are you alright? If you're still tired, you can rest here for half a day. We brought plenty of supplies this time, so there's no need to push yourself."
Akira felt a warmth bloom in his chest at her concern, but he still waved a hand dismissively, smiling. "No, really, I'm fine. I just didn't sleep well last night. Give me a moment, and I'll be good as new."
He sat down and began to eat his breakfast.
Seeing his persistence, Alise refrained from pushing further.
Instead, she plopped down next to him, propping her chin up with both hands, swaying her body side to side as she watched him eat with unblinking curiosity.
After a few bites, Akira noticed her staring and asked with a smile, "What is it? Why are you staring at me like that?"
"Hehe~ Nothing! I just got charmed again by how handsome you are." Alise beamed and reached out to ruffle his hair.
Looking at her lovely face, Akira chuckled. "Is that so? As expected of me. Even the perfect captain can't help but fall for my charm."
They exchanged grins until Alise huffed, "Even if you flatter me, I won't give you any benefits, you know. Well... maybe we can talk about it when we go back."
Just then, a voice filled with resentment broke their romantic exchange.
"Stupid Captain! Quit fangirling and come help me pack! And you too, Akira!" Kaguya's exasperated shout rang out.
As they turned to her, a ghostly image of a wrathful demon seemed to loom behind her, sending a chill down their spines. The two immediately snapped into action.
"Yes, ma'am!" They chorused.
...
After viewing the majestic Waterfall, the group continued their descent.
On the way to the next floor, Akira and Lyra served as temporary supporters, waiting for the front line to exhaust themselves before rotating in.
Ahead of them, the girls were locked in fierce combat with the monsters that surged forward endlessly. The clang of steel and cries of battle echoed through the cavern.
Taking advantage of a momentary lull in the fighting, Lyra approached Akira silently, as light and graceful as a cat.
She leaned in close and whispered, "What we did last night... I think Asta found out."
"Huh!?"
Akira's eyes widened in panic as he glanced at Asta, who was calmly cleaving a monster in half with her axe up front.
Akira immediately ducked his head close to Lyra's ear and whispered anxiously, "That's why I told you not to do that kind of thing. This is bad enough already if people find out."
"Hehe~ Okay, okay. I didn't think we'd get caught." Lyra said teasingly, patting his waist. "Besides, even if someone did find out, what's the worst that could happen?"
She shrugged as if it didn't concern her in the slightest.
Akira sighed in surrender. "Haah... whatever, I give up. Do what you want."
Just then, Noin's sharp voice rang out from ahead. "Hey, you two! Stop slacking off with your supporter work."
A stuffed bag flew through the air.
Akira quickly reached out and caught the bag in one smooth motion, scratching his head with a sheepish grin. "Sorry, I got distracted."ɴᴇᴡ ɴᴏᴠᴇʟ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs ᴀʀᴇ ᴘᴜʙʟɪsʜᴇᴅ ᴏɴ ɴovel(ꜰ)ɪre.nᴇt
Nearby, Celty began to slow her pace. Holding her staff, she turned to look at the pair curiously.
"Is there something wrong with this stretch of the dungeon? Why are you two whispering so much?"
Her innocent question struck like a pebble in a still pond.
One by one, heads began turning from the front line, glancing back with curiosity.
Akira stiffened. Especially when he noticed Asta's face—though concealed beneath heavy armor, her exposed eyes weren't hidden by her usual mask. She avoided his gaze, and her cheeks seemed faintly flushed.
So it was true.
Sighing silently, Akira replied, "Nothing. I was just discussing something with Lyra about the potential floor boss up ahead. You know... Amphisbaena."
"Ah, is that so?" Celty nodded. "Don't worry. We've faced it a few times already. We'll be fine."
With that, the curiosity in the group faded. The others returned their focus to the trek ahead, uninterested now that the mystery had turned mundane.
"Really? That's a relief. The sooner we beat it, the faster we can reach the safe zone." Akira replied with a smile.
Just then, a group of metallic crabs skittered into view.
"Alright, break time's over." Ryuu reminded gently. "The monsters are here."
With fluid precision, the Astraea Familia moved into action.
Akira and Ais were about to step forward to help but it was clear that the others didn't need their help.
With Ais's specialized monster-slaying abilities complementing their tactics, they simply stepped back and returned to supporting roles, watching in awe as the battle unfolded before them.

chapters.title: Chapter 125 - 125: Borrowing Names
chapters.content:
At the 27th floor, the team rotated once again, with Akira taking the lead.
On this level, the monsters dwelling within the Water City had grown significantly stronger. Among them were several blue-bodied, blue-maned, horse-shaped monsters—Kelpie and Lamia—half-human, half-serpent female monsters with wicked claws and long, serpentine tails.
One charged across the water toward Akira and the others, while the other slithered aggressively on the damp stone ground, its muscular tail swaying ominously.
Facing the oncoming threats, Akira wasted no time. With a swift motion, he unsheathed the one-handed sword at his waist.
In the blink of an eye, his figure blurred—like lightning weaving through the narrow, dim corridor. It was as if he'd teleported seven times in rapid succession.
With each burst of movement, the sword sliced through the air with a piercing whistle, sharp gusts of wind trailing behind the arcs.
Then, like a meteor streaking across the night sky, Akira's blade danced.
"Seven Lights." He said.
The next moment, he reappeared in front of the group of monsters. His sword glinted faintly as he gently shook it, scattering the droplets of monster blood that clung to the blade.
A muffled "puff" echoed through the corridor, and an invisible force slammed into the creatures. In unison, blood gushed from deep gashes, and their bodies suddenly split cleanly in two. Their lifeless remains crashed onto the cold dungeon floor.
Witnessing the seamless execution, Alise chuckled and tapped Kaguya on the shoulder. "Hey, isn't that your move, Kaguya? What's with 'Seven Lights'? I thought it was supposed to be 'Five Lights'? Hahaha."
[T/N: This refers to Kaguya's move Iai no Tachi "Gokou" where Gokou means Five Lights.]
Veins popped along Kaguya's forehead. She crossed her arms inside her sleeves and narrowed her eyes.
"I didn't teach him any technique. And his move isn't the same as mine. He just swung his sword seven times really fast. It has nothing to do with me."
Her own technique, "Five Lights," was the result of combining magic and sword skill—a different art entirely.
"Are you sure he's not borrowing your technique name?" Alise teased.
Kaguya frowned, reached out, and pinched Alise's cheek. "It's just a name. What's so funny about it?"
Before the debate could continue, Akira's shout echoed from ahead.
"Chrysanthemum!"
His sword ignited with blazing flames as he charged into another pack of monsters.
Kaguya burst into laughter and smacked Alise on the back. "Now it's your turn, Stupid Captain."
"Hmph. I should charge Akira a naming fee!"
While their banter echoed in the corridors, the expedition team finally arrived at the expansive lake where Amphisbaena dwelled.
Due to the unique terrain of the 27th floor, this floor boss held a distinct trait—the uncertainty of its spawning location.
Among the four known monster rexes of the Dungeon, both Goliath of the 17th floor and Udaeus of the 37th had fixed chambers within stone structures. Their locations never changed.
However, the remaining two—Amphisbaena on the 27th floor and Barol on the 49th—were influenced heavily by their environments.
The 49th floor, known as the "Great Wilderness," lacked any stone chambers, allowing Barol to roam freely across its expansive terrain.
Amphisbaena, on the other hand, was deeply affected by the interconnected waterways of the 25th, 26th, and 27th floors, all joined by a massive waterfall.
As a result, the two-headed dragon could appear on any of the three floors.
Throughout the expedition, the Astraea Familia remained vigilant, watching for signs of Amphisbaena. Yet, having found no trace of the beast on the upper two floors, it was all but confirmed that it waited here, on the 27th.
The 27th floor, the lowest point of the Water City, was dominated by a vast lake that absorbed water from the waterfall above and circulated it across the region.
Fighting Amphisbaena here meant facing the beast on its home turf—in the water.
According to intelligence from Riveria, Amphisbaena's aquatic combat potential ranked near Level 6. It was an existence comparable to the floor boss of the 37th floor, Udaeus.
Moreover, prior experience taught them that each of Amphisbaena's two heads bore unique abilities.
One head could unleash devastating flames, not magical in nature but raw, combustible jet-fire born from volatile fuel within its body. It was a physical attack with immense force.
The second head exhaled a thick mist that blanketed the area, severely weakening the effects of magic within its range.
Its entire body was coated in resilient, ivory-colored dragon scales, rendering magic largely ineffective against it. Combined with its tenacious vitality, the beast was a nightmare for any lone mage.
Looking over the silent surface of the lake, the girls recalled past tactics, where they had to lure the creature out. Otherwise, a battle wouldn't even commence.
But this time, they had Akira.
Having shared his plan beforehand, the team stood ready.
Alise slung an arm around Akira's shoulders and pointed at the tranquil waters. "Once the fight starts, that part's on you, Akira."
"Leave it to me." Akira nodded. "I'll provide the footing you all need."
Before engaging in battle, each member pulled out their protective garments—special gear akin to the Undine cloth used in earlier floors.
Woven from narcissus essence, the garments allowed adventurers to breathe underwater and move more swiftly while submerged.
In this flooded labyrinth, venturing in without them would be suicide. Even with the suits, danger was ever-present.ɪꜰ ʏᴏᴜ ᴡᴀɴᴛ ᴛᴏ ʀᴇᴀᴅ ᴍᴏʀᴇ ᴄʜᴀᴘᴛᴇʀs, ᴘʟᴇᴀsᴇ ᴠɪsɪᴛ NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
Raising her palm high, Alise shouted with a blazing spark in her voice, "Is everyone ready? Then the battle against Amphisbaena begins! Let's go!"
A thunderous cheer erupted in response. "Ohhhh!!!"
...
At the edge of the lake, Akira stood tall and still. His gaze fixed on the massive silhouette slumbering beneath the water's surface.
With a breath of resolve, Akira initiated his transformation, switching his class to Glacial Master.
As the shift completed, his body underwent a dramatic change. His jet-black hair faded into a snowy white cascade. His eyes, once a deep darkness, now blazed a cold, blood-red hue like frozen fire.
Even though the others had seen this form before, they still felt a tingle of awe. Akira, in this state, exuded a chilling majesty that captivated all eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 126 - 126: Facing Amphisbaena
chapters.content:
However, Ais, who was witnessing Akira in this posture for the very first time, reacted completely differently from the others.
Her golden eyes widened in astonishment, lips slightly parted as a breath escaped her lungs, and her adorable little face was etched with pure disbelief. She was utterly stunned by the overwhelming spectacle before her.
Akira, his expression grave, extended his right hand and slowly raised it.
In that moment, the atmosphere around him seemed to freeze. The air solidified under the crushing weight of the magic radiating from his body—a torrent of magical power that surged outward with an unstoppable force.
Under the sheer pressure of that power, a massive rectangular block of ice began to rapidly form in the air. The block resembled an iceberg, exuding a chilling aura that sent shivers through the surroundings.
Then, as though sculpted by an invisible craftsman, the front of the ice block began to shift and sharpen, slowly morphing into the pointed tip of a colossal spear.
Suddenly, Akira stepped forward.
The ground beneath him groaned under the pressure and cracked apart, splitting into deep fissures as if the earth itself could not withstand his force.Nᴇw novel chapters are publɪshed on No(ᴠ)ᴇlFire.nᴇt
In the next instant, the enormous ice spear launched forward like a thunderbolt, slicing through the air and crashing down into the still surface of the lake.
With a deafening splash, the spear pierced the water like a divine lance descending from the heavens, shattering the tranquility of the lake and causing towering sprays to erupt from the impact.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
The water erupted with a cascade of crashing sounds—ten violent, echoing detonations.
The once-calm lake was now churning wildly. Waves surged and collided, the entire surface roiling like a boiling cauldron.
And then it came—a roar.
"ROOOAAAR!!!"
The furious roar rose from the depths of the lake, echoing across the expanse with pure, primal rage and majestic power. It was enough to make one's heart tremble.
Alise's voice cut through the tension like a whip. "Akira has successfully awakened Amphisbaena! Everyone, follow the plan and prepare for battle!"
Ryuu, Ryana, and Celty began chanting their respective magic incantations, their voices weaving spells to be unleashed upon the Floor Master the moment it appeared.
At the rear, Maryuu focused on healing, while Noin, Iska, and Asta took up formation in front of the magic users, shielding them like an unyielding wall.
The rest of the party stood ready, their roles clear: launch a concentrated assault once Amphisbaena was forced ashore.
Beneath the turbulent surface, Amphisbaena seethed.
Akira's earlier strike had torn through the monster's durable scales, plunging into its massive body like a jagged blade. Though the blow had narrowly missed its vital organs, the searing pain had ignited a firestorm of fury within.
Its two grotesque heads snapped up, and four baleful, glowing dragon eyes locked onto Akira. Those cold, murderous eyes radiated hatred and bloodlust.
With a thunderous slap, Amphisbaena churned the water and surged toward the lake's edge, determined to crush the human who dared provoke it.
At that same moment, the lake exploded upward in a towering pillar of water.
"Amphisbaena is coming! Mages, ready yourselves!"
Alise shouted, her gaze locked on the monstrous silhouette rising from the lake.
Without hesitation, Akira focused. He channeled the icy magic within his body, conjuring frigid frost that lashed outward in jagged waves.
The frost spread rapidly across the surface, crawling up Amphisbaena's submerged torso and encasing it in thick, unyielding ice. The monster's movements slowed, its strength hampered.
Akira knew his job here was done. He quickly leapt backward, putting distance between himself and the target to avoid interfering with his allies' attacks.
Seeing that Amphisbaena was successfully restrained, Alise raised her arm and shouted, "Fire!"
Luminous Wind!
A volley of massive light orbs, each trailing emerald gales, surged into the sky like meteors.
Behind Ryuu, a radiant magic circle gleamed with pure elven magic. As she finished her chant, she, Ryana, and Celty launched their spells in unison.
The first to strike was Ryuu's Luminous Wind.
With blinding speed, it struck Amphisbaena's dual heads before it could react.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
Explosions erupted. Dragon scales shattered, blood geysered from the wounds, and Amphisbaena's once-armored heads now bore exposed flesh, raw and vulnerable.
Flames and lightning followed, scorching the beast with merciless precision.
The battlefield erupted in firestorms, crackling bolts, and thunderous detonations. It was a sight to behold—beautiful and devastating all at once.
Under the onslaught, Amphisbaena let out a bone-chilling scream, its massive jaws raised high as it howled in agony.
"ROOOOOAAAR!!!"
The sound threatened to rupture eardrums.
Alise didn't hesitate. "Akira, now!"
But even before her words reached him, Akira had already moved.
In the blink of an eye, he vanished like a ghost.
In the next instant, he stood atop the lake—no, the battlefield.
Akira lowered both hands to the water's surface. Tremendous magical pressure erupted from his body, flooding the surroundings.
And then, as if the world answered his call, his power surged forth and turned the very water beneath him to solid ice.
The transformation was swift and stunning.
The massive lake solidified in seconds. Wisps of frost curled in the air, and the freezing wave reached down into the lake's depths.
Even the parts of Amphisbaena still submerged beneath the water could not escape. The floor master's lower body was trapped in the growing glacier.
With its movements hindered, the creature was slowly but surely lifted out of the lake, its entire form forced into the open.
By the time Akira stepped back, a vast field of ice had formed, providing his comrades with firm ground on which to battle.
The stage was set. Now it was up to them to finish what he had begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 127 - 127: Astraea Familia and Ais
chapters.content:
When the Amphisbaena was stranded on the shore, its fate was already sealed.
The once-formidable floor master, now grounded and fully exposed, could no longer maintain its former majesty.
The light of its life flickered like a dying star hanging in the far reaches of the night sky—dim, unstable, and on the verge of vanishing forever.
Though Amphisbaena remained incredibly powerful, its overall strength assessed at the level of a terrifying level 5, it now stood before a group of elite adventurers whose abilities far exceeded the standards of any ordinary level 3. Against such a lineup, the countdown to its demise had already begun.
Alise, flushed with exhilaration, couldn't contain her rising emotions. She had never imagined that their campaign against a floor boss like Amphisbaena could proceed so swiftly and effectively.
"Lyra, I'm too fired up! You take over the command!" She exclaimed, her voice practically shaking with excitement.
Hearing this, Lyra frowned slightly and responded with exasperation, "Fine. But for the love of the gods, calm down. Don't lose your head in the middle of battle."
"I get it!"
Alise replied hastily, before darting forward like an arrow released from a drawn bow, her figure blurring as she charged straight for Amphisbaena.
Just then, the two grotesque, bloodied heads of the beast began to stir. Perhaps spurred into action by the barrage of magic that had bombarded its body, the right head reared upward and opened its gaping maw, unleashing ten thick streams of crimson mist into the air.
The dense, blood-red fog rapidly surged outward, wrapping itself around Amphisbaena like a protective shroud.
This fog wasn't just for show—it acted as a defensive barrier, significantly dampening the power of magic that dared to pierce it. The spells launched by Ryuu and the others began to lose potency upon contact, their force nullified by the thick mist.
At the same time, the left head locked eyes on the rear-guard magic casters—the source of its torment.
Akira, always attuned to the battlefield's subtle energy shifts, could feel an intense, searing heat rapidly coalescing at the base of Amphisbaena's throat.
"It's charging its dragon breath." He muttered, narrowing his eyes.
The mouth of the left head opened wide, revealing jagged fangs and a terrifying glow.
A fireball, blazing with tremendous intensity, began to form—a burning sphere of destruction. The air around it twisted with heat, distorting reality like a mirage.
"Oh no, you don't." Akira said coldly.
He swiftly planted both palms on the icy lake surface beneath him. At once, an overwhelming surge of ice-elemental magic erupted from his body, sweeping outward like a flood.
With a thunderous crack, a massive wall of glacial ice rose from the ground, thick and resolute. It shot upward with incredible speed, intercepting the right head just before it could unleash its blazing fury.
Boom!
The fire exploded inside the beast's own mouth, the detonation echoing through the battlefield like a cannon shot.
Amphisbaena howled in agony. The internal blast had caused grievous harm—it thrashed wildly, steam pouring from its nostrils as its head reeled backward.
Seeing the opening, Alise turned sharply to Ais and shouted, "Ais-chan! Handle the red mist—now!"
Ais gave a small nod. Her lips moved quietly. "Tempest."
Wind began to churn around her, green and wild.
This time, however, Ais didn't form her usual wind barrier. Instead, she concentrated the wind into her sword. The slender rapier in her hands gleamed with an emerald brilliance.
Gripping the hilt tightly, Ais let out a battle cry in her heart.
The next moment, a monstrous gust roared out from her sword, a storm of raw power surging like a beast unchained.
Even Ais herself struggled to resist its force—her feet skidded along the ground as she fought to maintain her stance.Thɪs updatᴇd by NovᴇlFir(e).nᴇt
Swooooosh—!
The green tempest slammed into Amphisbaena with a deafening roar.
Deep gouges were torn into the dragon's flesh, and torrents of blood gushed from the wounds. The red mist protecting it instantly dispersed, unveiling the creature's disfigured and rage-filled faces.
"Nice one, Ais-chan!" Alise cheered, her voice vibrant with admiration.
Without hesitation, she turned toward Kaguya and Neze. "Let's go! It's our turn!"
"Yeah." Kaguya responded casually, while Neze nodded with sharp resolve.
As the right head lunged again, Alise dodged swiftly to the left, her sword igniting in blazing flame. With a fierce swing, she delivered a series of slashes that scorched the beast's thick hide, branding it with blackened wounds.
Suddenly, the injured head twisted its neck furiously, dragging its battered body backward in retreat. But even as it recoiled, it retaliated with vengeance.
Its maw opened wide, and a blast of dragon breath erupted with devastating fury—directed straight at the advancing Kaguya and Neze.
Facing the terrifying and blazing attack head-on, Kaguya remained unfazed. Her sharp eyes never wavered as she shouted toward the werewolf girl beside her, her voice firm and commanding, "Neze!"
As if responding to an unspoken signal that only true partners could understand, Neze immediately caught on.
As someone who had fought side by side with Kaguya countless times before, she didn't need further instruction.
She simply nodded without hesitation, acknowledging the command with silent determination.
The moment was critical.
The two of them moved at the exact same time—splitting apart in a blur of motion to evade the searing dragon breath that raged toward them like a tidal wave of destruction.
(End of Chapter)
